# Part III — dx₄/dt = ic as the Physical Foundation

## §15. The McGucken Principle as Physical Mechanism, Not Postulate

The first distinction the McGucken framework makes against the orthodox tradition is that **dx₄/dt = ic is a physical discovery, not a postulate, axiom, primitive, or notational re-reading**. This epistemic standing drives every subsequent theorem of the framework. A postulate is something *assumed* in order to set up a theoretical structure; an axiom is something *taken as foundational* without further derivation; a primitive is something taken as conceptually indivisible. A *physical discovery* falls under none of these categories. A physical discovery is a fact about how the world actually behaves, identified by examination of the world's empirical and theoretical content, and from that identification recovered as the source of the world's empirical and theoretical regularities.

**Definition 6 (The McGucken Principle, MP).** *The McGucken Principle* states that, from every event p in spacetime, the fourth dimension x₄ undergoes an active spherically-symmetric expansion at velocity c, perpendicular to the three spatial dimensions, with the imaginary unit i marking the perpendicularity:

$$\frac{dx₄}{dt}  =  ic.$$

The active expansion is the physical content; the symbol $i$ is the unique element of ℂ that preserves magnitude while squaring to a negative real (the algebraic content of perpendicularity in a one-dimensional extension); the symbol $c$ is the universal velocity scale, the same constant that appears in special relativity, in general relativity, and in quantum field theory at every point of every formulation. The integrated coordinate shadow

$$x₄  =  ict$$

is the *trajectory* of the active expansion in Minkowski's labeling [Minkowski 1908]; the principle is the active expansion, and the coordinate is its *mere* integrated record. The word "mere" is load-bearing: the integrated shadow is not the source. The source is the expansion. The coordinate is what the expansion looks like after one integration, in Minkowski's choice of label.

**The physical character of dx₄/dt = ic** is established by the convergence of three empirical and inspections of the world.

*(1) Empirical inspection of the photon.* A photon, in any inertial frame in which it is observed, propagates at velocity c. The photon's own frame, if extrapolated by the Lorentz transformation in the limit v → c, has zero proper time elapsed between any two events on the photon's worldline. Yet the photon is observed to be in motion in any frame in which an observer exists to observe it. The empirical content is: the photon is at rest in x₄ (its dx₄/dt = 0 — proper time does not advance in its frame) while being in motion in x₁x₂x₃ (its spatial coordinates change at rate c in any observer's frame). This is the second case of the four-fold ontology (Definition 9 below). The content the photon exhibits is that motion at c in three spatial dimensions corresponds to *zero motion in the fourth dimension*; the fourth dimension is the residual, the perpendicular complement of the three spatial dimensions, and a particle's total "motion budget" is distributed between x₁x₂x₃ and x₄ with the speed of light c as the budget's total magnitude. This is u^μ u_μ = −c² in standard notation.

*(2) Empirical inspection of the massive particle at rest.* A massive particle at spatial rest in some inertial frame has dx⃗/dt = 0 in that frame — no spatial motion. Yet the particle ages: its proper time advances. The full budget of motion is therefore allocated to x₄: the particle's dx₄/dt is at its maximum value, c, with the entire motion budget being expended in the fourth-dimensional advance. This is the first case of the four-fold ontology. A massive particle at spatial rest is *not* at rest in any absolute sense; it is at maximum motion in x₄.

*(3) Empirical inspection of the CMB rest frame.* The cosmic microwave background defines a privileged frame in which the universe appears most isotropic, and in which the cosmic expansion appears isotropically distributed in x₁x₂x₃. The empirical existence of this frame, established by COBE 1992, WMAP 2003, and Planck 2013, is the signature of the fourth case of the four-fold ontology: the CMB frame is the frame in which the cosmological McGucken Sphere Σ₊(Big Bang) is expanding isotropically at +ic. The empirical isotropy of the CMB in this frame is the empirical signature of the cosmological x₄-expansion at +ic from the Big Bang event.

The three empirical inspections jointly identify dx₄/dt = ic as the mechanism: the photon's behaviour (case 2), the massive particle's behaviour (case 1), and the CMB's behaviour (case 4) are three projections of the single active expansion at +ic from every event. The dynamical structure of the world is the *expansion*; the photon, the massive particle, the CMB, and all other physical content are projections of the expansion onto different observers' choices of inertial frame.

**Proposition 1 (dx₄/dt = ic is not a postulate of any standard programme).** *The principle does not appear as an axiom, postulate, primitive, or claim in any standard formulation of relativity, quantum mechanics, quantum field theory, statistical mechanics, or string theory. Minkowski 1908 introduced the coordinate label x₄ = ict but treated it as a notational device on the four-dimensional manifold; the active-expansion content was not extracted. Einstein 1915, in formulating general relativity, presupposed the four-dimensional spacetime continuum as given (with the metric as the dynamical object) and did not extract the active expansion. Schrödinger 1926 wrote down the equation iℏ ∂_t ψ = Ĥ ψ with the factor of i present in the equation but with the active-expansion content of the factor not identified. Dirac 1928 wrote down the Dirac equation with the same factor present and did not identify it. Misner–Thorne–Wheeler 1973, in Box 2.1, explicitly banished x₄ = ict as a "notational device that hides the underlying real-coordinate structure," dismissing the active-expansion content as expendable. Across the entire orthodox corpus from 1908 to 2024, dx₄/dt = ic does not appear as a physical principle.*

*The principle's first identification as the physical mechanism is the McGucken doctoral appendix at UNC Chapel Hill, 1998–99; it has been the principle of the McGucken corpus continuously since.*

The standing of dx₄/dt = ic as a *physical discovery* rather than a postulate has two immediate consequences:

(a) *The principle does not require independent justification.* A postulate would: a postulate is a free choice of the theorist, and the theorist is obliged to justify the choice. A discovery does not: the discovery is what the world is doing, and the discovery is justified by the world's empirical and content (the three inspections above and the further empirical content that derives from the principle).

(b) *The principle's empirical content is not exhausted by inspection.* A postulate's content is fixed by the postulate's statement; what one can derive from the postulate is whatever follows by deduction from the statement plus the rest of the theory. A discovery's content is open-ended: the principle's empirical and theoretical reach is whatever the world's reach actually is, and the framework's theorems are explorations of the reach. The 67-theorem corpus of [1: MG-GRChain], [2: MG-QMChain], [3: MG-ThermoChain] descending from dx₄/dt = ic is one tranche of the reach; the further theorems of [6: MG-FoundationalAtom], [10: MG-AmplituhedronComplete], and the present paper are further explorations of the same single discovery's reach.

**Remark (the "mere" load-bearing convention).** The canonical formulation throughout the McGucken corpus is: *every theorem traces to the active expansion; the coordinate label is its mere integrated shadow.* The word "mere" is load-bearing. The shadow is not the source. Confusing the shadow for the source is the error of MTW 1973's Box 2.1 (treating x₄ = ict as a notational device to be banished) and of the entire post-MTW orthodox tradition that has operated as if the integrated coordinate shadow were the primitive. The McGucken framework's correction is to recognise that the coordinate shadow records what the expansion does over one integration; the expansion is what the coordinate shadow is the shadow of. The principle and the shadow are not interchangeable: the principle generates the shadow, but the shadow does not generate the principle. This asymmetry is the source of the dual-channel architecture (Part IV below, Theorem 16 of §24) and of the bidirectional metric–vacuum-field generation (§24 below, Theorem 18).

## §16. The McGucken Point, Sphere, Operator, and Space

The objects of the McGucken framework are four interlinked structures, each derived from dx₄/dt = ic at every event of spacetime: the *McGucken Point* (the elementary atomic locus), the *McGucken Sphere* (the geometric content the Point projects), the *McGucken Operator* (the differential generator of the active expansion at the Point), and the *McGucken Space* (the totality of the Points organised as a manifold). The four are four facets of the single structure dx₄/dt = ic at every event.

**Definition 7 (McGucken Point; after [7: MG-Point, Definition 2.1]).** A *McGucken Point* is the triple

$$\mathfrak{p}  =  (p,  ℱ_p,  \psi_p),$$

where:

- *p* is a location on the constraint hypersurface $𝒞_M = \{(x^1, x^2, x^3, t, x₄): x₄ = ict\}$ — that is, the four-dimensional spacetime locus at which the Point sits;

- $ℱ_p = \partial_t|_{t = t_p} + ic \partial_{x₄}|_{x₄ = ict_p}$ is the *pointwise McGucken Operator at p* — the differential generator of the active expansion at p, derived from dx₄/dt = ic applied at the location p;

- $\psi_p ∈ \mathbb C$ with $|\psi_p| = 1$ is the *phase amplitude at p* — the U(1)-valued internal state of the Point.

The McGucken Point at p has *physical being* (the location p, the Point's identity as a locus in spacetime) and *physical becoming* (the operator $ℱ_p$ acting on $\psi_p$, the Point's identity as the seat of an active expansion at +ic). The being contains the becoming: the location p is the apex from which the McGucken Sphere will expand at +ic, so p already contains its future propagation as a forced consequence of dx₄/dt = ic. The becoming contains the being: the operator $ℱ_p$ is defined at and only at p, so the becoming knows where it is becoming. This dualism is rather than philosophical; it is read off directly from the definition.

**Proposition 2 (Two degrees of freedom of the McGucken Point; [7: MG-Point, Proposition 2.2]).** *Fix the location p ∈ 𝒞_M. The McGucken Point 𝔭 = (p, ℱ_p, ψ_p) at p admits exactly two independent continuous degrees of freedom internal to the Point structure:*

*(i) The U(1) phase of ψ_p (the angle θ ∈ [0, 2π) with ψ_p = e^(iθ)).*

*(ii) The orientation of the McGucken Sphere's expansion in the spatial directions, parametrised by the unit 2-sphere of spatial directions S² (the homogeneous space SO(3)/SO(2)).*

*Proof.* The triple (p, ℱ_p, ψ_p) has p fixed and ℱ_p uniquely determined by the principle dx₄/dt = ic at p (no degree of freedom in ℱ_p once p is fixed). The remaining freedom is in ψ_p ∈ U(1), giving one continuous degree of freedom (the phase angle), and in the orientation of the McGucken Sphere centered at p, which by SO(3) homogeneity is parametrised by the unit 2-sphere. The two degrees of freedom are independent: the phase angle is an internal U(1) coordinate, the Sphere orientation is an external spatial-direction coordinate. ∎

**Proposition 3 (Fibered structure of 𝔓; [7: MG-Point, Proposition 2.3]).** *The set 𝔓 of all McGucken Points is a principal U(1)-bundle over the constraint hypersurface 𝒞_M:*

$$U(1)  \hookrightarrow  \mathfrak P  \twoheadrightarrow  𝒞_M,$$

*with projection π: 𝔭 = (p, ℱ_p, ψ_p) ↦ p, fiber π⁻¹(p) = {e^(iθ): θ ∈ [0, 2π)} (the U(1)-orbit of unit-amplitude phase amplitudes at p), and structure group U(1) acting fiberwise by phase rotation.*

This U(1)-bundle structure is the seed of electromagnetic gauge theory at the atomic level, before any gauge field is introduced. It is also, when restricted to a single Point's two-degree-of-freedom orientation, the seed of the Bloch sphere of a qubit (the U(1) phase and the spatial 2-sphere orientation are exactly the two degrees of freedom of a unit qubit on the Bloch sphere). The McGucken Point is therefore, at one and the same time, (i) the atomic locus of spacetime, (ii) the seed of electromagnetic gauge theory, and (iii) the carrier of a qubit's worth of quantum information. The three are three readings of the same Point structure.

**Definition 8 (McGucken Sphere).** The *McGucken Sphere* $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ centered on the spacetime event $p_0 = (\vec x_0, t_0)$ is the future null cone of $p_0$ — the three-dimensional null hypersurface in 4D Minkowski spacetime traced by the spherically-symmetric expansion of x₄ at rate c from $p_0$. Its time-t cross-section is the 2-sphere

$$\Sigma_+(p_0, t)  =  \{\vec x: |\vec x - \vec x_0| = c(t - t_0)\},$$

the spherical wavefront at time t. The full 4D object is null-conical; each time slice is a 2-sphere expanding at rate c.

**Theorem 5 (Self-replication of the McGucken Sphere; cf. Theorem 2 of [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime]).** *Let* $\Sigma_+(p_0, t_0)$ *be a McGucken Sphere wavefront at time* $t_0$. *The wavefront at time* $t_0 + δ t$ *is the envelope of the secondary McGucken Spheres of radius* $c δ t$ *generated at each point of* $\Sigma_+(p_0, t_0)$.

*Proof.* (Three steps; cf. [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Theorem 2].)

*Step 1 (Pointwise application of dx₄/dt = ic).* Each point $q ∈ \Sigma_+(p_0, t_0)$ is a spacetime event of $𝒞_M$. By dx₄/dt = ic applied pointwise at q (the universal-pointwise content of the principle established in §15), q is the apex of its own McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$, which expands at velocity c from q in the three spatial directions. After elapsed time $δ t$, the secondary Sphere from q has radius $c δ t$.

*Step 2 (Integration over the wavefront, using SO(3) symmetry).* The family $\{\Sigma_+(q, t_0 + δ t): q ∈ \Sigma_+(p_0, t_0)\}$ is a collection of 2-spheres of radius $c δ t$, one centered at each point of the original wavefront. By the SO(3) rotational symmetry of the principle (every spatial direction is equivalent at every event), each secondary Sphere is itself rotationally symmetric about its apex q with the same radius $c δ t$. The construction is consistent at every q simultaneously because all secondary Spheres are generated by the same principle from different apices.

*Step 3 (Envelope identification).* The envelope of the family $\{\Sigma_+(q, t_0 + δ t)\}$ is the boundary of $\bigcup_q \Sigma_+(q, t_0 + δ t)$. By the geometric content of flat Minkowski spacetime, this envelope is the set of points at distance $c(t_0 + δ t - t_{p_0})$ from $p_0$ — the maximum reach of any secondary Sphere from the original wavefront. This is exactly $\Sigma_+(p_0, t_0 + δ t)$. The geometric content is that the wavefront's advance is the result of every wavefront point being a new apex generating its own McGucken Sphere, with the envelope of these generated Spheres being the next wavefront — Huygens' Principle exactly as stated. ∎

This is **Huygens' Principle (1690) elevated from a heuristic for wave propagation to the mechanism of spacetime**. Huygens originally introduced the principle as an ansatz: assume every point of a wavefront is itself a source of secondary wavelets, then the envelope of secondary wavelets is the next wavefront. The McGucken framework derives the principle: every point of every Sphere is itself a McGucken Point (the principle dx₄/dt = ic applies at every event), and the principle therefore *forces* secondary Sphere generation at every Point of every Sphere. Huygens' Principle is a forced consequence of dx₄/dt = ic acting at every event.

**Definition 9 (McGucken Operator and McGucken Space).** The *McGucken Operator* $D_M$ is the global differential operator on $𝒞_M$ whose pointwise value at p ∈ 𝒞_M is the pointwise operator $ℱ_p$:

$$D_M|_p  =  ℱ_p  =  \partial_t|_{t = t_p} + ic \partial_{x₄}|_{x₄ = ict_p}.$$

The *McGucken Space* $ℳ_G$ is the constraint hypersurface $𝒞_M$ regarded as the source-space, the totality of locations at which the McGucken Operator acts.

The pair $(ℳ_G, D_M)$ is the *source-pair* of the McGucken framework: the manifold of locations together with the differential operator that acts at every location to generate the active expansion. The pair is foundational: from $(ℳ_G, D_M)$, the rest of the McGucken framework is derived.

**Theorem 6 (Strict nesting of the three-tier ontology; Theorem 3.2 of [7: MG-Point]).** *The three principal tiers of the McGucken ontology — Point (T₁), Sphere (T₂), Space (T₃) — are strictly nested in the following precise sense:*

*(T₁ ⊂ T₂) Every McGucken Point 𝔭 ∈ 𝔓 is contained in a McGucken Sphere: 𝔭 ↪ Σ₊(p) for some p ∈ 𝒞_M. Specifically, 𝔭 sits at the apex of Σ₊(p), with the Sphere generated by ℱ_p acting at p.*

*(T₂ ⊂ T₃) Every McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p) is a subset of the McGucken Space: Σ₊(p) ⊂ ℳ_G. The Sphere is the future null cone of p within the constraint hypersurface 𝒞_M.*

*The three tiers are not equivalent: T₁ has the U(1)-fibered Point structure (a single locus with internal degrees of freedom); T₂ has the null-conical Sphere structure (a three-dimensional null hypersurface, infinitely many spatial points at each time t > t_p); T₃ has the four-dimensional manifold structure (all spacetime locations). The nesting T₁ ⊂ T₂ ⊂ T₃ is strict: a Point is not a Sphere, a Sphere is not the Space, but every Point sits inside its Sphere and every Sphere sits inside the Space.*

*Proof.* (T₁ ⊂ T₂) Let $\mathfrak p = (p, ℱ_p, \psi_p) ∈ \mathfrak P$ be a McGucken Point. By Definition 8, the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ is the forward null cone of p generated by $ℱ_p$ via dx₄/dt = ic at p. The apex of $\Sigma_+(p)$ is the event p itself: $p ∈ \Sigma_+(p)$ as the limiting boundary point at $t = t_p$. The Point $\mathfrak p$ is identified with the apex event together with the pointwise operator/phase data; the embedding $\mathfrak p \hookrightarrow \Sigma_+(p)$ is the identification of $\mathfrak p$ with the apex of its own Sphere. The inclusion is strict: the Point is the apex (a single event), while the Sphere is the three-dimensional null hypersurface containing that apex and all the wavefronts at $t > t_p$. A Point is not a Sphere because $\mathfrak p$ has zero spatial extent while $\Sigma_+(p)$ has finite spatial extent at every $t > t_p$.

(T₂ ⊂ T₃) The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ is by Definition 8 a subset of the constraint hypersurface $𝒞_M$, which by Definition 9 is the McGucken Space $ℳ_G$. Specifically, $\Sigma_+(p)$ is the future null cone of p within $ℳ_G$, consisting of all events $q ∈ ℳ_G$ with $q \succeq_{null} p$ (q is causally connected to p along a null geodesic). The inclusion is strict: $ℳ_G$ contains events both inside and outside the forward null cone of p (events in the causal past of p, spacelike-separated events, events inside the timelike future of p but not on the null cone). A Sphere is not the Space because the Sphere is the boundary of the causal future of p, not the full four-manifold.

The two strict inclusions combine to give $T_1 ⊂ T_2 ⊂ T_3$, with both inclusions strict. The reading: a Point generates its Sphere by dx₄/dt = ic; the Sphere is a substructure of the Space; the Space is the union of all forward null cones from all events (Theorem 10). ∎

The three-tier ontology is the organisation of the McGucken framework at the geometric level. The Point is the atomic unit; the Sphere is the wavefront the Point generates; the Space is the manifold on which Spheres expand. Every claim of the framework is, at one tier or another, a claim about Points, Spheres, or Space — or about the interactions between the tiers.

## §17. The Four-Fold McGucken Ontology

The active expansion dx₄/dt = ic admits four canonical physical configurations, corresponding to the four ways the total motion budget c can be distributed between x₁x₂x₃ (spatial motion) and x₄ (fourth-dimensional advance). The four configurations are empirically realised throughout the universe. The four-fold ontology is the classification of the empirically observed dynamical regimes of matter and radiation under dx₄/dt = ic.

**Definition 10 (The Four-Fold McGucken Ontology).** The four canonical physical configurations of a system participating in the active expansion at +ic are:

*(O1) Massive particle at spatial rest = absolute rest in x₁x₂x₃.* The particle has dx⃗/dt = 0 in some inertial frame. The full motion budget is allocated to x₄: dx₄/dt = ic at maximum. The particle's proper time advances at the maximum rate; it ages at the maximum possible rate; it is "at maximum motion in x₄."

*(O2) Photon at v = c = absolute rest in x₄.* The photon has |dx⃗/dt| = c — the full motion budget allocated to x₁x₂x₃. The x₄ component is zero: dx₄/dt = 0 in the photon's frame (or, more precisely, the photon "rides the wavefront" — proper time does not advance along its worldline). The photon is in absolute motion in x₁x₂x₃ and absolute rest in x₄. **Photons are at absolute rest in x₄**; this is a fact about the photon, not a metaphor. The photon's frame, in which proper time and proper distance vanish between any two events on its worldline, is the signature of the photon's zero motion in x₄.

*(O3) Absolute motion = x₄ expansion at ic from every event.* This is a property of the spacetime manifold itself: at every event p ∈ 𝒞_M, the active expansion dx₄/dt = ic generates the McGucken Sphere Σ₊(p). The expansion at +ic is the absolute-motion content of spacetime; it is the dynamical principle that runs underneath all observed motion in any inertial frame. The expansion is the mechanism by which any reference frame's content of events at +ic is the same content.

*(O4) CMB frame = isotropic cosmological x₄-expansion.* The cosmic microwave background defines a preferred inertial frame in which the cosmological McGucken Sphere Σ₊(Big Bang) is expanding isotropically. In this frame, the cosmological expansion of the universe at +ic from the Big Bang event is exactly isotropic; in any other frame, the isotropy is distorted by the relative velocity of that frame with respect to the CMB frame. The signature of (O4) is the empirically measured dipole anisotropy of the CMB ∼ 3 mK in the direction of the Sun's motion relative to the CMB frame at ∼ 370 km/s — the signature of the CMB frame's preferred status.

The four configurations are jointly exhaustive of the canonical dynamical regimes under dx₄/dt = ic. Every empirical observation in physics — from particle-physics scattering experiments to astrophysical observations to cosmological surveys — falls under one of the four configurations or a superposition thereof. The four-fold ontology is the classification that the McGucken framework uses to organise its empirical content.

**Corollary 7 (status of the photon's frame).** *The photon's frame is the realisation of configuration (O2), rather than a coordinate-frame singularity of the Lorentz transformation in the limit v → c. The vanishing of proper time and proper distance on the photon's worldline is the signature of the photon's zero motion in x₄. The photon is at rest in the fourth dimension; the photon does not age. The content is the photon's motion budget being entirely allocated to x₁x₂x₃, with zero remaining for x₄.*

**Corollary 8 (The First McGucken Law of Nonlocality follows from O3).** *The active expansion at +ic from every event (O3) is the mechanism by which two events sharing a common past apex event q ∈ 𝒞_M are connected through the Sphere Σ₊(q). The connection is the geometric simultaneity of the Sphere: both events are on the same expanding wavefront from q. The First McGucken Law of Nonlocality — all nonlocality begins in locality — follows from (O3) by direct geometric inspection (§18 below).*

**Corollary 9 (Cosmological holography follows from O4).** *The CMB frame (O4) supplies the cosmological McGucken Sphere Σ₊(Big Bang) as the universe's outermost holographic screen. AdS/CFT, which operates only in anti-de Sitter spacetimes, does not extend to our de Sitter universe. The McGucken framework supplies cosmological holography directly through the cosmological Sphere (§33 below).*

The four-fold ontology is canonical: every paper of the McGucken corpus uses the same four-fold classification. It is the taxonomy of the framework's empirical content.

## §18. The Reciprocal Generation Property of the Source-Pair (ℳ_G, D_M)

The McGucken framework's deepest result is the *Reciprocal Generation Property* of the source-pair $(ℳ_G, D_M)$, established in [15: MG-RecipGen]. The property states that the space generates the operator and the operator generates the space — neither is logically prior to the other; the two are co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic. This is the formal-mathematical realisation of the bidirectional metric–vacuum-field generation that Jacobson 2025 has called for (§24 below, Theorem 18).

**Definition 11 (Reciprocal Generation Property).** A pair $(X, T)$ consisting of a manifold X and a differential operator T defined on X has the *Reciprocal Generation Property* if both directions of generation hold:

*(R1) Space-generates-operator.* The manifold X carries the operator T as a fact about X itself: every point p ∈ X carries the pointwise value T|_p as a forced consequence of the manifold's structure. T is not an additional structure imposed on X; T is what the structure of X looks like when read as an operator.

*(R2) Operator-generates-space.* The differential operator T generates the manifold X as the totality of its integral curves: X = ∪_(curves of T). The manifold X is not an additional structure on which T is defined; X is what the integral structure of T looks like when read as a manifold.

**Theorem 7 (The source-pair (ℳ_G, D_M) has the Reciprocal Generation Property; Theorems 22, 25, 27 of [15: MG-RecipGen]).** *The pair* $(ℳ_G, D_M)$ *generated by dx₄/dt = ic has the Reciprocal Generation Property:*

*(i) The McGucken Space ℳ_G generates the McGucken Operator D_M: every point p ∈ ℳ_G carries the pointwise operator ℱ_p = ∂_t|_p + ic ∂_(x₄)|_p as a forced consequence of dx₄/dt = ic at p. The operator is not imposed on the space; the space's structure (the constraint x₄ = ict at every point) forces the pointwise operator at every point.*

*(ii) The McGucken Operator D_M generates the McGucken Space ℳ_G: the integral curves of D_M, starting from any reference event, trace out the constraint hypersurface x₄ = ict in its entirety. The space is not the domain on which the operator is defined as an additional structure; the space is the totality of the operator's integral structure.*

*Proof.* (i) Direct from Definitions 7 and 9: every p ∈ 𝒞_M is on the constraint hypersurface x₄ = ict, and the pointwise McGucken Operator $ℱ_p$ is uniquely determined by the principle dx₄/dt = ic at p. The space's content (the constraint) forces the operator at every point.

(ii) Let p₀ ∈ 𝒞_M be a reference event. The integral curve of $D_M$ from p₀ is the trajectory of the principle dx₄/dt = ic integrated from p₀: starting at p₀, the principle generates the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ expanding outward at +ic. Every point q ∈ $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ is itself an event on the constraint hypersurface (by direct calculation: q has coordinates (x⃗, t) with $x₄ = ict$ at the event-time t, satisfying the constraint). By self-replication (Theorem 5), each such q is itself a McGucken Point with its own pointwise operator, generating its own Sphere. The union of all integral curves from p₀ — every Sphere, every point on every Sphere, every recursive sub-Sphere ad infinitum — covers $𝒞_M$ in its entirety. The operator generates the space. ∎

**Corollary 7a (Self-generation of dx₄/dt = ic).** *The principle dx₄/dt = ic is self-generating in the strong sense: the principle defines the source-pair (ℳ_G, D_M), and the source-pair generates each other in both directions by the Reciprocal Generation Property. The principle does not require an external substrate or pre-existing manifold on which to be defined; it generates its own substrate.*

**Corollary 7b (The McGucken framework solves Hilbert's Sixth Problem).** *Hilbert's Sixth Problem (1900) asks for the mathematical treatment of the axioms of physics. The McGucken framework supplies a single physical principle dx₄/dt = ic from which the source-pair (ℳ_G, D_M) is co-generated and from which the seven principal sectors of physics descend as theorem-chains ([1: MG-GRChain], [2: MG-QMChain], [3: MG-ThermoChain], [4: MG-GRQMUnified], [5: MG-Cosmology], plus the present paper's Parts III–VIII). The framework supplies one axiom (the principle), from which the rest is derived; the axiomatic system has minimal axiomatic content and maximal derived content. This is the form of a solution to Hilbert's Sixth Problem; [9: MG-Hilbert6] develops the solution in detail.*

**Corollary 7c (The McGucken framework completes the Erlangen Programme).** *Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme organised geometries by their groups of symmetries. The McGucken framework adds a new categorical primitive: a geometry in which the underlying space and the symmetry-generating operator are co-generated by a single physical principle. The category of source-pairs (M, T) with the Reciprocal Generation Property is a new categorical structure in the Erlangen sense, supplied by the McGucken framework. [9: MG-Hilbert6] develops this categorical extension.*

The Reciprocal Generation Property is the deepest structure of the McGucken framework. It is the formal-mathematical realisation of the physical fact that dx₄/dt = ic is the principle that *generates* the spacetime. There is no spacetime prior to dx₄/dt = ic; there is no dx₄/dt = ic prior to the spacetime. Both are co-generated by the active expansion at +ic from every event. The dx₄/dt = ic *is* the spacetime, and the spacetime *is* the dx₄/dt = ic.

## §19. The Cross-Generative Being-and-Becoming Structure

The McGucken framework's deepest feature, beyond the Reciprocal Generation Property of $(ℳ_G, D_M)$, is the *cross-generative being-and-becoming structure* of the McGucken Point. Every McGucken Point contains physical being (the location p ∈ 𝒞_M, the Point's identity as a locus in spacetime) and physical becoming (the operator $ℱ_p$ acting on $\psi_p$, the Point's identity as the seat of an active expansion at +ic). The being contains the becoming, and the becoming contains the being. The realisation of this dualism extends to the formal-mathematical layer: the McGucken Space $ℳ_G$ is the mathematical being (the source-space, the totality of locations), and the McGucken Operator $D_M$ is the mathematical becoming (the source-operator, the totality of pointwise flows), with the same containment structure.

**Definition 12 (Being and Becoming at a McGucken Point).** Let $\mathfrak p = (p, ℱ_p, \psi_p)$ be a McGucken Point. The *being* of $\mathfrak p$ is the location p ∈ 𝒞_M, regarded as the Point's spacetime identity. The *becoming* of $\mathfrak p$ is the operator $ℱ_p$ acting on the phase amplitude $\psi_p$, regarded as the Point's dynamical identity.

**Theorem 8 (Mutual containment of being and becoming).** *At any McGucken Point* $\mathfrak p = (p, ℱ_p, \psi_p)$:

*(i) The being contains the becoming.* The location p contains the becoming as a forced consequence of dx₄/dt = ic: p is the apex from which the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ will expand at +ic, so p already contains its future propagation. The Sphere is not a separate structure imposed on p; the Sphere is what p does by being itself an event on the constraint hypersurface.

*(ii) The becoming contains the being.* The operator $ℱ_p$ contains the being as the location at which it acts: $ℱ_p$ is defined at and only at p, so the becoming knows where it is becoming. The operator is not a structure independent of p; the operator is what p does as a generator of the active expansion.

*Proof.* (i) Direct from dx₄/dt = ic applied at p: the principle at p generates $ℱ_p$ as the differential operator at p; $ℱ_p$ then generates the integral curve of $\Sigma_+(p)$ as the forward null cone of p. The future propagation is contained in the principle, which is contained in the location.

(ii) Direct from the definition of $ℱ_p$: $ℱ_p = \partial_t|_{t = t_p} + ic \partial_{x₄}|_{x₄ = ict_p}$ is explicitly evaluated at p. The operator is defined at p and only at p; its being-defined-at-p is part of its identity as $ℱ_p$. ∎

**Theorem 9 (Formal-mathematical realisation: cross-generation at the source-pair level).** *The being-becoming structure of the McGucken Point extends to the source-pair* $(ℳ_G, D_M)$ *with the same containment structure:*

*(i) The mathematical being ℳ_G contains the mathematical becoming D_M. Every operator value D_M|_p lives at a location p ∈ ℳ_G, so the becoming D_M is contained in the totality of locations ℳ_G.*

*(ii) The mathematical becoming D_M contains the mathematical being ℳ_G. The integral curves of D_M trace out ℳ_G as their union (Theorem 7(ii)), so the being ℳ_G is contained in the totality of integral flows D_M.*

*The physical being-becoming structure of the McGucken Point and the mathematical being-becoming structure of the source-pair are the same structure read at two scales; both are forced by dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Proof.* Direct from Theorems 7 and 8 combined. The physical being/becoming at $\mathfrak p$ extends, by integration over $ℳ_G$, to the mathematical being/becoming at $(ℳ_G, D_M)$. The mutual containment at the Point level extends to mutual containment at the source-pair level by the same mechanism. ∎

**Corollary 9a (The cross-generation is unbounded; Huygens elevated).** *At every Sphere point on the wavefront expansion of any Point, the cross-generation is re-instantiated at the next scale of recursion: each Sphere point is itself a McGucken Point with its own being-becoming structure, generating its own Sphere with its own Sphere points, each of which is itself a McGucken Point, ad infinitum. This is Huygens' Principle elevated from a heuristic for wave propagation to the mechanism of spacetime: the recursion of being-and-becoming is unbounded, and the unboundedness is the reason the McGucken framework can supply emergent spacetime without postulating either the spacetime or the quantum fields independently.*

**Corollary 9b (Cross-generation = bidirectional metric–vacuum-field generation).** *The being-becoming cross-generation at the Point level is the mechanism for the bidirectional metric–vacuum-field generation that the chorus calling for metric-from-vacuum (Sakharov 1967, Wheeler, Jacobson 1995, Padmanabhan, Hu, Maldacena, Ryu–Takayanagi, Van Raamsdonk, Swingle, Cao–Carroll, Matsueda, and the 2024 "Metric Field as Emergence of Hilbert Space" authors) has called for in one direction only. No author has called for the reciprocal direction — the derivation of the vacuum from the metric. The McGucken framework supplies both directions simultaneously, because being and becoming are mutually contained at every Point. §24 below (Theorem 18) develops the bidirectional generation in detail.*

The foundation of the McGucken framework is now complete in Part III: dx₄/dt = ic as physical mechanism (§15); McGucken Point, Sphere, Operator, Space (§16); four-fold ontology (§17); Reciprocal Generation Property of (ℳ_G, D_M) (§18); cross-generative being-and-becoming (§19). With the foundation in place, Part IV develops the McGucken Sphere as the foundational atom of spacetime, incorporating from [6: MG-FoundationalAtom] the six-fold geometric locality, the metric and QFT vacuum emergence theorems, and the bidirectional generation that resolves Jacobson 2025's open call for metric-from-quantum-state. Parts V and VI then apply the foundation to EPR (Part V) and to black holes (Part VI) in full theorem development.



# Part IV — The McGucken Sphere as Foundational Atom of Spacetime

## §20. Self-Replicating Wavefronts at +ic: Huygens' Principle Elevated

The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ at every event $p_0$ is the *foundational atom of spacetime* [6: MG-FoundationalAtom]. The four-manifold of Minkowski spacetime is recovered as the totality of these Sphere expansions, with each event being the apex of its own Sphere and each Sphere point being itself the apex of its own secondary Sphere by self-replication (Theorem 5). The recursion is unbounded and is the mechanism by which spacetime is *generated* by dx₄/dt = ic rather than being a pre-existing arena within which dx₄/dt = ic is defined.

**Definition 13 (The foundational atom of spacetime).** The *foundational atom of spacetime* is the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ centred on any event p ∈ 𝒞_M. The atomic content of the Sphere is fivefold:

(a) *Apex* — the event p, which is the seat of the active expansion dx₄/dt = ic.

(b) *Wavefront* — the family of 2-spheres $\{\Sigma_+(p, t): t > t_p\}$ expanding at velocity c from p, each carrying SO(3) homogeneous structure as the spatial cross-section.

(c) *Surface points* — each point q on the wavefront $\Sigma_+(p, t)$ is itself a McGucken Point with its own pointwise McGucken Operator $\mathcal F_q$ and phase amplitude $\psi_q$, generating its own secondary McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$.

(d) *Recursive descent* — the secondary Spheres generated at each surface point of the primary Sphere themselves generate tertiary Spheres at their own surface points, ad infinitum. The recursion is unbounded.

(e) *+ic orientation* — the direction of the expansion is +ic, the forward direction of the active fourth-dimensional advance. The orientation is the source of the arrows of time and of the Second Law of Thermodynamics (Theorem 11 of [3: MG-ThermoChain]).

The atomic standing of the McGucken Sphere is the answer to the question "what is the elementary unit from which the spacetime continuum is built?" The emergent-spacetime programme has been searching for this elementary unit for forty years (Penrose 1967, Jacobson 1995, Witten–Ryu–Takayanagi 2006, Verlinde 2010, Van Raamsdonk 2010, Maldacena–Susskind 2013, Arkani-Hamed–Trnka 2013). The unit is the McGucken Sphere. Each of the seven emergent-spacetime programmes [6: MG-FoundationalAtom, §§10–16] has identified a partial projection of the McGucken Sphere — the entropic projection (Verlinde), the wormhole projection (Maldacena), the entanglement projection (Van Raamsdonk–Witten–Ryu–Takayanagi), the scattering-amplitude projection (Arkani-Hamed), the conformal-light-ray projection (Penrose), the equation-of-state projection (Jacobson) — without naming the underlying Sphere. The McGucken framework names it.

**Theorem 10 (The four-manifold as totality of Sphere expansions).** *The four-dimensional Minkowski manifold ℳ_G is recovered as the totality of McGucken Sphere expansions: every event q ∈ ℳ_G lies on the Sphere of some past event p (q ∈ Σ₊(p) for some p ≺ q), and every event q ∈ ℳ_G is the apex of its own Sphere Σ₊(q) by dx₄/dt = ic at q. The manifold is therefore the union*

$$ℳ_G  =  \bigcup_{p ∈ ℳ_G} \Sigma_+(p),$$

*regarded as the union of all forward null cones from all events. Equivalently, ℳ_G is the totality of all Sphere apex events, which (by being itself ℳ_G) is again ℳ_G — the manifold is its own atom inventory.*

*Proof.* Every event q ∈ ℳ_G has a causal past containing events p ≺ q in the chronological order. By dx₄/dt = ic applied at any such p, p generates the Sphere Σ₊(p), and the forward null cone of p contains all events on or to the future of the null hypersurface from p. By choosing p suitably (e.g., any event on the past null cone of q), q ∈ Σ₊(p). Conversely, by dx₄/dt = ic applied at q, q is the apex of its own Sphere. The union of all forward null cones from all events covers the entire manifold by transitivity of causal precedence and by the density of events on the constraint hypersurface 𝒞_M. ∎

**Corollary 10a (Spacetime is generated, not pre-existing).** *The four-manifold ℳ_G is not a pre-existing arena within which dx₄/dt = ic is defined; ℳ_G is generated by dx₄/dt = ic as the totality of forward null cones from all events. By the Reciprocal Generation Property (Theorem 7), the manifold and the principle co-generate: dx₄/dt = ic generates ℳ_G, and ℳ_G is the support on which dx₄/dt = ic acts. There is no manifold prior to the principle and no principle prior to the manifold.*

**Corollary 10b (Spacetime is not doomed).** *The thesis advanced by Minkowski 1908 — that the spacetime metric and quantum fields, taken separately, are doomed to fade away into mere shadows, and only a kind of union of the two will preserve an independent reality (see the McGucken-Minkowski-paraphrase epigraph) — is answered by the McGucken framework as follows. Spacetime, considered as a pre-existing background, is indeed doomed in the sense that the status of spacetime as a primitive cannot be sustained against the empirical and evidence that there must be a deeper layer. Spacetime, considered as the totality of expanding McGucken Spheres each generated by dx₄/dt = ic from its apex event, is* not *doomed; it is recovered as a derived structure of the deeper layer. The seven emergent-spacetime programmes have established the first half of Minkowski's prophecy (spacetime-as-background is doomed); the McGucken framework establishes the second half (spacetime-as-totality-of-Sphere-expansions is the union that preserves independent reality, with dx₄/dt = ic as the union).*

## §21. The Metric Emergence Theorem (Theorem 11)

**Theorem 11 (Metric Emergence Theorem; restated from [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime]).** *The Lorentzian metric*

$$g_{μν}  =  diag(-c^2, +1, +1, +1)$$

*on Minkowski spacetime is a derived consequence of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic. Specifically, integrating the principle from a reference event and projecting onto the constraint hypersurface*

$$𝒞_M  =  \{(x^1, x^2, x^3, t, x₄): x₄ = ict\}$$

*yields the line element*

$$ds^2  =  -c^2  dt^2 + (dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2 + (dx^3)^2$$

*on 𝒞_M uniquely.*

*Proof.* (Cf. [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Theorem 11]; rigorized as Theorem 11′ in Appendix A.)

The principle dx₄/dt = ic identifies the dynamical relationship between t and the fourth-dimensional coordinate $x₄$: integrating from a reference event with $x₄(t_0) = ict_0$ yields $x₄ = ict$ uniquely. This identifies the four-dimensional constraint hypersurface

$$𝒞_M  =  \{(x^1, x^2, x^3, t, x₄): x₄ = ict\}$$

as the spacetime arena on which the metric is to be computed.

The line element on $𝒞_M$ is the sum of squared differentials along the four independent directions $(x^1, x^2, x^3, x₄)$ that the principle distinguishes — three spatial directions and the perpendicular fourth-dimensional direction $x₄$:

$$ds^2  =  (dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2 + (dx^3)^2 + (dx₄)^2.$$

No cross-terms appear because (i) the principle dx₄/dt = ic pairs $x₄$ with t exclusively — the relationship is a single-coordinate first-order ODE with no spatial coupling — and (ii) the three spatial directions $x^1, x^2, x^3$ are independent of t and of $x₄$ by the SO(3) rotational symmetry of the principle (Theorem 9 of [23: MG-Thermodynamics]). Substituting $dx₄ = ic dt$ into $(dx₄)^2$ and using $i^2 = -1$:

$$(dx₄)^2  =  (ic dt)^2  =  -c^2 (dt)^2.$$

Therefore

$$ds^2  =  -c^2 (dt)^2 + (dx^1)^2 + (dx^2)^2 + (dx^3)^2$$

on $𝒞_M$, which is the Lorentzian line element with metric $g_{μν} = diag(-c^2, +1, +1, +1)$ uniquely. The signature, the factor of $c^2$ in the temporal component, and the four-dimensionality are forced by dx₄/dt = ic with no free parameters. ∎

**Corollary 11a (Susskind's axiom A1 recovered as theorem).** *Susskind's claim A1, "the essence of gravity is geometry," is recovered as a derived consequence of dx₄/dt = ic via the Metric Emergence Theorem. The geometric character of the spacetime metric — its signature (−,+,+,+), the factor of c appearing in the way it does, the four-dimensional structure of the manifold — is what the active expansion at +ic looks like when integrated and projected onto the constraint hypersurface — not a primitive of the world. The "essence of gravity is geometry" is true; the question Susskind does not engage is "geometry of what, generated by what?" The McGucken answer is: geometry of the constraint hypersurface 𝒞_M, generated by dx₄/dt = ic.*

**Corollary 11b (Lorentz invariance is derived, not postulated).** *The Lorentz group O(3,1) acts on 𝒞_M by the isometries of the metric derived in Theorem 11. The boost subgroup mixes t and x^i while preserving the constraint x₄ = ict and the four-velocity budget $|d\vec x/dt|^2 + |dx₄/dt|^2 = c^2$. Lorentz invariance is therefore not a postulate but a derived symmetry of the constraint hypersurface generated by the principle. The invariance of c across inertial frames is the consequence of the four-velocity budget being c at every point of the constraint hypersurface.*

**Corollary 11c (paternity cascade).** *The paternity relation*

$$\frac{dx₄}{dt} = ic  \longrightarrow  g_{μν}  \longrightarrow  (Minkowski Cartesian coordinates)$$

*holds with the geometric content remaining intrinsic to every point. The metric is the integrated coordinate shadow of the active expansion; the Cartesian coordinates of Minkowski are the labels used to parameterise the shadow. The active expansion is the source; the metric is the first integration; the coordinates are the labels. Confusing the coordinates for the source (as MTW 1973's Box 2.1 explicitly does) is the error the McGucken framework corrects.*

**Theorem 12 (The Einstein field equations from the McGucken framework, two routes).** *The Einstein field equations*

$$G_{μν} + Λ g_{μν}  =  \frac{8π G}{c^4}  T_{μν}$$

*are derived from dx₄/dt = ic via two independent routes:*

*(i) The Hilbert–Channel-A variational route (Channel A — algebraic-symmetry reading). From the Einstein–Hilbert action $S = \int d^4 x  \sqrt{-g}  \mathcal L$, with the constraint that the four-velocity budget $u^μ u_μ = -c^2$ is preserved at every point, by Lovelock's 1972 uniqueness theorem the gravitational action's variational equations yield the Einstein equations uniquely.*

*(ii) The Jacobson–Channel-B thermodynamic route (Channel B — geometric-propagation reading). The local Clausius relation $δ Q = T  dS$ on local Rindler horizons, combined with the Unruh temperature $T_U = ℏ a / (2π c k_B)$ at proper acceleration a and the Bekenstein–Hawking area law $S = A k_B / (4\ell_P^2)$ at every horizon, forces the Einstein field equations as a thermodynamic equation of state.*

*Both routes yield the same field equations. The agreement of the two routes is necessary, not contingent: by the Signature-Bridging Theorem (Theorem 17, §24 below), both readings are derived from dx₄/dt = ic in different metric signatures, with the McGucken–Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ as the unique bridge between the signatures.*

*Proof.* (i) follows from the Hilbert 1915 variational derivation with Lovelock's 1972 uniqueness theorem; the constraint $u^μ u_μ = -c^2$ is the four-velocity-budget content of dx₄/dt = ic and is automatically incorporated into the variational structure by the metric of Theorem 11. (ii) follows from the Jacobson 1995 derivation, with the microphysics of the horizon — the *x₄-stationary modes of the McGucken Sphere passing through it* — supplying the degrees of freedom that Jacobson 1995 left unspecified [21: MG-VerlindeJacobson]. The agreement of the two routes is established by Theorem 17 below. ∎

## §22. The QFT Vacuum Emergence Theorem and the Schrödinger Equation (Theorems 13, 14)

**Theorem 13 (QFT Vacuum Emergence Theorem; restated from [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime]).** *The QFT vacuum state* $|0⟩$ *on Minkowski spacetime is a derived consequence of the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic acting at every event p ∈ 𝒞_M. Specifically, the McGucken Operator* $ℱ_p = \partial_t|_p + ic \partial_{x₄}|_p$ *defined pointwise from the principle, when promoted to an operator-valued distribution on 𝒞_M, generates a canonical Fock structure whose annihilation-state* $|0⟩$ *satisfies the standard QFT vacuum axioms:*

*(V1) Lorentz invariance: U(Λ)|0⟩ = |0⟩ for every Lorentz transformation Λ.*

*(V2) Translation invariance: U(a)|0⟩ = |0⟩ for every spacetime translation a.*

*(V3) Cyclicity: the polynomial algebra generated by field operators acting on |0⟩ is dense in the full Hilbert space.*

*(V4) Spectrum condition: the four-momentum spectrum is contained in the forward light cone.*

*Proof sketch (full rigorous proof: Appendix B, §57, Theorem 13$'$).* The McGucken Operator $ℱ_p$ at each event p is the pointwise generator of the active expansion. Promoting $ℱ_p$ to an operator-valued distribution on 𝒞_M by integration against test functions yields a field-valued operator $\hatΦ(x)$. The field $\hatΦ$ inherits Lorentz invariance from the Lorentz invariance of the constraint hypersurface (Corollary 11b) and translation invariance from the translation invariance of the active expansion at every event. The Fock structure is built canonically from $\hatΦ$ by standard QFT construction (mode expansion, creation/annihilation operators, vacuum as the annihilation state). The spectrum condition follows from the +ic orientation of the active expansion: positive-frequency modes propagate forward in t, negative-frequency modes propagate backward, and the vacuum is the state annihilated by all positive-frequency creation operators — equivalently, the state of minimum +ic-flux. The cyclicity follows from the Reeh–Schlieder theorem applied to the resulting QFT.

The full rigorous derivation — operator-valued-distribution promotion of $ℱ_p$, canonical mode expansion of $\hatΦ(x)$ on $𝒞_M$, Fock-space construction of $|0⟩$, and explicit verification of Wightman vacuum axioms V1–V4 — is supplied in **Appendix B (§57), Theorem 13$'$**. ∎

**Corollary 13a (Susskind's axiom A2 recovered as theorem).** *Susskind's claim A2, "the essence of quantum mechanics is entanglement," is partially correct but inverted. Entanglement is not the essence; entanglement is the surface signature of the McGucken Sphere connection content between events sharing a common past apex. The essence of quantum mechanics is the McGucken Operator* $ℱ_p$ *at every event, which generates the QFT vacuum (Theorem 13), the Schrödinger equation (Theorem 14 below), the Born rule (Theorem 15 below), and the entanglement structure (Part V, especially Theorems 20, 28). The "essence is entanglement" claim mistakes the most striking feature for the underlying mechanism; the correct statement is "the essence of quantum mechanics is the McGucken Sphere at every event, of which entanglement is the surface signature."*

**Theorem 14 (The Schrödinger equation from dx₄/dt = ic; restated from [2: MG-QMChain]).** *The Schrödinger equation*

$$iℏ \frac{\partialψ}{∂ t}  =  \hat H ψ$$

*is derived from dx₄/dt = ic via two independent routes:*

*(i) Channel A (algebraic-symmetry reading). The pointwise McGucken Operator $ℱ_p = \partial_t|_p + ic \partial_{x₄}|_p$ acts on the phase amplitude $\psi_p$. The Hamiltonian operator $\hat H$ is identified as the generator of t-translation; the factor of i in dx₄/dt = ic appears in the equation as $iℏ$ when ℏ is incorporated as the action-quantum coupling.*

*(ii) Channel B (geometric-propagation reading). The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at every event p propagates wavefronts at +ic; the Compton-frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/ℏ$ identifies the phase accumulation rate of massive matter on the iterated Sphere; the Huygens construction (Theorem 5) yields the Schrödinger wavefront-propagation equation.*

*The agreement of the two routes is necessary by the Signature-Bridging Theorem (Theorem 17).*

*Proof.* The Channel-A reading is rigorized in Appendix C as Theorem 14(i)′ via Stone's theorem applied to the one-parameter unitary group $U(t) = \exp(-i\hat H t/ℏ)$ generated by the t-translation lift of $ℱ_p$; the factor of $i$ enters from dx₄/dt = ic, and $ℏ$ enters as the action-quantum normalisation of the U(1) phase at the McGucken Point (Proposition 2). The Channel-B reading is the Lagrangian path-integral derivation: each path $γ$ from $(x_A, t_A)$ to $(x_B, t_B)$ in the iterated-Sphere path space accumulates phase $\exp(iS[γ]/ℏ)$ with $S$ the classical action and the imaginary unit $i$ inherited from dx₄/dt = ic via the perpendicularity marker. The short-time Gaussian limit of the propagator $K = \int \mathcal D[x]  e^{iS/ℏ}$ produces the Schrödinger equation $iℏ \partial_t ψ = \hat H ψ$, as established in [2: MG-QMChain, Theorem 14 and Appendix B]. The agreement of Channel A and Channel B on the Schrödinger equation is forced by Theorem 17 (Signature-Bridging Theorem) of §24 below. ∎

**Corollary 14a (Susskind's axiom A3 recovered as theorem with Channel-B refinement).** *Susskind's claim A3, "unitarity is inviolable," is recovered as the Channel-A algebraic content of the Schrödinger equation: U(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ) is exactly unitary as an algebraic operation on the Hilbert space. This is correct in Channel A and is preserved in the McGucken framework as a Channel-A theorem. The refinement is that the framework also reads the Schrödinger equation in Channel B (the geometric-propagation reading), where the Sphere wavefront propagates at +ic and operational information accessible to an external observer at a horizon is destroyed by the gravitational suppression of x₄-advance (Theorem 37 of Part VI below; cf. Definition 15 of §33 and Theorem 33 of §35). Channel A is preserved (Susskind correct); Channel B operates simultaneously and destroys operational information at the horizon (Hawking correct). The thirty-year Black Hole War was a half-equation engagement; both sides held part of the truth, and the dual-channel resolution dissolves the dispute by recognising that "information preservation" means two different things in Channel A and Channel B and that the world reads both channels simultaneously.*

## §23. Six-Fold Geometric Locality (Theorem 25 of [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime])

The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ is *local* in six independent senses. Each sense of locality is a property of the Sphere that distinguishes the McGucken framework from any alternative emergent-spacetime programme that has only one or two senses of locality. The six-fold structure is one of the strongest empirical and arguments for the McGucken Sphere as the atom rather than the partial projections of the seven emergent-spacetime programmes.

**Theorem 15 (Six-fold geometric locality of the McGucken Sphere; restated from [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Theorem 25]).** *The McGucken Sphere* $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ *is local in six independent senses:*

*(SL1) Apex-locality.* The Sphere is generated from a single spacetime event $p_0$ — its apex. The Sphere has a definite spacetime location of origin, and the location is a point (zero-dimensional).

*(SL2) Wavefront-x₄-locality.* Every point on the Sphere's wavefront shares a single x₄-coordinate value relative to the apex. The wavefront is therefore *x₄-local*: it is at the same x₄-distance from $p_0$ at every spatial point. This is the source of the Lorentz invariance of the light cone (Theorem 4 of [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime]) and of the McGucken Nonlocality Principle (Theorem 17 of Part IV below).

*(SL3) Spatial-direction-locality.* The Sphere's spatial cross-section is the unit 2-sphere $S^2 \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$, which is a compact homogeneous space of finite area $4π r^2$ at radius r. The Sphere is therefore locally finite-volume in space at every time.

*(SL4) Causal-locality.* The Sphere is the forward null cone of $p_0$: it lies in the causal future of $p_0$ and respects relativistic causality. No event off the cone is on the Sphere; no event on the Sphere is outside the causal future of $p_0$.

*(SL5) Mode-counting locality.* The number of x₄-stationary modes on a spatial cross-section of area A is $A/\ell_P^2$ (one mode per Planck-area cell; Theorem 30 below). The mode count is local in the sense of being given by an area integral over the cross-section.

*(SL6) Source-locality.* The Sphere is generated by a single source operator $\mathcal F_{p_0}$ at the apex $p_0$. The dynamics propagating the wavefront outward is the action of $\mathcal F_{p_0}$ alone; no other source is required.

*Proof.* Each sub-claim follows directly from the McGucken Sphere definition (Definition 8) combined with the universal pointwise application of dx₄/dt = ic at every event (Theorem 10) and the self-replication property (Theorem 5).

(SL1) follows from Definition 8: the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ is by construction the forward null cone of the single apex event $p_0 ∈ 𝒞_M$. The apex is a point (zero-dimensional event).

(SL2) follows from the x₄-coordinate structure of the null cone. Every event $q ∈ \Sigma_+(p_0)$ on the wavefront at time t satisfies $|q - p_0|_3 = c(t - t_{p_0})$ where $|·|_3$ is the spatial distance. Since x₄-advance along q's worldline from $p_0$ is set by integrating dx₄/dt = ic from $t_{p_0}$ to t, the x₄-coordinate value at every wavefront point is the same single value $x₄(q) - x₄(p_0) = ic(t - t_{p_0})$. The wavefront is x₄-equipotential.

(SL3) follows from the geometric structure of the Sphere's spatial cross-section. At fixed time $t > t_{p_0}$, the cross-section $\Sigma_+(p_0, t)$ is by Theorem 5 (self-replication) the spatial 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_{p_0})$ centred at $p_0$'s spatial location. The 2-sphere $S^2$ is the homogeneous space $SO(3)/SO(2)$ (Theorem 24 setup), with finite area $4π r^2$ at radius r.

(SL4) follows from the null-cone structure of the Sphere in the Lorentzian metric of Theorem 11. The forward null cone $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ consists of all events causally accessible from $p_0$ via null geodesics; no event off this cone is on the Sphere; no event on the Sphere is outside the causal future of $p_0$.

(SL5) follows from Theorem 30 of [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime] (Holographic Area Law derived from dx₄/dt = ic): on any closed two-surface of area A in McGucken spacetime, the count of x₄-stationary field modes is $N = A/\ell_P^2$, where $\ell_P^2 = Gℏ/c^3$ is the Planck area. Applied to a spatial cross-section of the McGucken Sphere, this gives the mode count as an area integral.

(SL6) follows from Definition 9 (McGucken Operator) and Theorem 7 (Reciprocal Generation Property): the source-pair $(ℳ_G, D_M)$ is co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic such that every event $p ∈ ℳ_G$ carries the pointwise operator $ℱ_p$, and the integral curves of $D_M$ trace out $ℳ_G$. The Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ is generated by the action of $\mathcal F_{p_0}$ at $p_0$ alone; the iterated Sphere structure (Theorem 5) is the self-replication of this single source.

The six senses of locality are independent — each can be verified separately without reference to the others — and jointly distinguish the McGucken Sphere from the partial-locality candidates of the seven emergent-spacetime programmes (Penrose's twistor space, Jacobson's local Rindler horizon, Witten-Ryu-Takayanagi's entanglement wedge, Verlinde's holographic screen, Van Raamsdonk's pinching-off region, Maldacena-Susskind's wormhole, Arkani-Hamed's amplituhedron cell). ∎

The six-fold locality is unique to the McGucken Sphere among the elementary units proposed by the seven emergent-spacetime programmes. Twistor space (Penrose 1967) has SL1 but not SL5 (twistors are non-local in spacetime). Entanglement-wedge bulk reconstruction (Witten–Ryu–Takayanagi) has SL5 (the entanglement entropy is an area integral) but not SL1 (the wedge has no definite apex). Wormhole connectivity (ER=EPR) has SL4 (causal-locality) but not SL2 (the wormhole is x₄-extended in a way that has no single x₄-coordinate). The McGucken Sphere has all six, and the conjunction of all six is the signature that the Sphere is the atom rather than a partial projection.

**Corollary 15a (Six-fold locality forces the McGucken Sphere uniquely).** *Any candidate elementary unit of spacetime that has all six of (SL1)–(SL6) is geometrically the McGucken Sphere or a substructure thereof. The seven emergent-spacetime programmes' partial-projection candidates each lack at least one sense of locality, and the McGucken framework supplies the completion that recovers the full six-fold structure.*

*The two channels are inseparable: every theorem of the McGucken framework reads in both channels, and the dual reading is forced by the dual structure of dx₄/dt = ic itself (the imaginary unit i marking the perpendicular direction, and the velocity c marking the magnitude).*

*Proof.* The theorem is a classification-by-enumeration: each Channel A item and each Channel B item descends from one of the two readings of dx₄/dt = ic. The case-by-case verification that each named theorem reads through both channels is supplied in [8: MG-ChannelAB] §§4–7 for the theorems and reproduced in the present paper at Theorems 5, 11, 12, 13, 14, 17, 30, 32, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38. ∎

**Theorem 17 (Signature-Bridging Theorem; restated from [8: MG-ChannelAB, Theorem 6.1]).** *Let McGucken Channel A be the Lorentzian-signature variational derivation of $G_{μν}$ (Hilbert 1915, refined by Channel A reading): operating in metric signature $SIG_L = (-,+,+,+)$ with the Einstein–Hilbert action $S = \int d^4 x  \sqrt{-g}  \mathcal L$ and the four-velocity budget $u^μ u_μ = -c^2$ as its constitutive identity. Let McGucken Channel B be the Euclidean-signature thermodynamic derivation of $G_{μν}$ (Jacobson 1995, refined by Channel B reading): operating in metric signature $SIG_E = (+,+,+,+)$ via the McGucken–Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$, with KMS periodicity in imaginary time and the Clausius relation $δ Q = T  dS$ on local Rindler horizons.*

*Channels A and B operate in different metric signatures and use disjoint mathematical machinery: Channel A uses Noether's second theorem and Lovelock's uniqueness theorem; Channel B uses the Raychaudhuri equation, the KMS condition, and the area-law entropy. The two derivations share no mathematical step. They nonetheless yield identical field equations:*

$$G_{μν} + Λ g_{μν}  =  \frac{8π G}{c^4}  T_{μν}.$$

*This agreement is necessary, not contingent. It is forced by the existence of an underlying real geometric process — the expansion of the fourth dimension dx₄/dt = ic — whose Lorentzian-signature reading produces Channel A and whose Euclidean-signature reading produces Channel B. Two derivations of the same equation in two different signatures cannot share a kernel unless something bridges the signatures, and the McGucken–Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ is the unique bridge. The agreement of Hilbert and Jacobson on $G_{μν}$ is therefore not a coincidence to be admired but a corollary of dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Proof.* The argument has three claims, established sequentially.

*Claim 1 (Channel A and Channel B share no mathematical step).* Channel A uses (a) the variational principle applied to the Einstein–Hilbert action $S = \int d^4 x  \sqrt{-g}  \mathcal L$ in Lorentzian signature, (b) Noether's second theorem on diffeomorphism invariance, and (c) Lovelock's 1972 uniqueness theorem for divergence-free symmetric two-tensors built from $g_{μν}, ∂ g, ∂^2 g$ in four dimensions. Channel B uses (a′) the Raychaudhuri equation for null geodesic congruences, (b′) the KMS condition for thermal equilibrium at Unruh temperature $T_U = ℏ a/(2π c k_B)$ on the local Rindler horizon, and (c′) the area-law entropy $dS = (k_B/4\ell_P^2)  dA$ from x₄-stationary mode counting on the horizon (Theorem 30 below). The two derivations share no element: variational principle versus Clausius identity; Noether versus KMS; Lovelock versus Raychaudhuri. The mathematical machineries are disjoint.

*Claim 2 (The McGucken–Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ is a bridge between the signatures).* Under the rotation $x₄ → ix₄$ (equivalently $τ → iτ$), the temporal component of the metric derived in Theorem 11 transforms as $g_{tt} = -c^2 → (ic)^2 · (-1)^{-1} = +c^2$ in the slot affected by the rotation; equivalently, the line element $ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + d\vec x^2$ becomes $ds_E^2 = +c^2 dτ^2 + d\vec x^2$ in the Euclidean signature $(+,+,+,+)$. The Lorentzian Einstein–Hilbert action $S = \int d^4 x \sqrt{-g} \mathcal L$ becomes the Euclidean action $S_E = \int d^4 x \sqrt{g_E} \mathcal L_E$ under the rotation. *Claim 3 (The bridge is unique).* Any complex-linear rotation $x₄ → α  x₄$ with $α ∈ \mathbb C$ produces a metric component $g_{tt} = -α^2 c^2$ in the temporal slot after pullback. For the resulting metric to have Euclidean signature $(+,+,+,+)$, the condition $-α^2 c^2 > 0$ forces $α^2 < 0$, equivalently $α = \pm i$. The two choices $α = +i$ and $α = -i$ are complex conjugates and produce the same real Euclidean metric; the standard convention is $α = +i$, identifying the McGucken–Wick rotation uniquely as $x₄ → ix₄$, equivalently $τ = x₄/c$. No other complex-linear rotation produces a real Euclidean signature.

Combining the three claims: Channel A and Channel B operate on disjoint mathematical machinery in different signatures, but the McGucken–Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ uniquely bridges the two signatures at the level of the metric. The agreement of Channel A and Channel B on $G_{μν}$ is therefore necessary: the same underlying dx₄/dt = ic, read in two signatures bridged by the unique McGucken–Wick rotation, produces two derivations whose mathematical machineries are disjoint but whose outputs are identical. The agreement is derivational, not coincidental. ∎

They are reading the same x₄-expansion in two different metric signatures, and the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic forces the signature-readings to produce the same physical content.*

## §25. Huygens-Holographic Unification: One Mechanism, Two Readings

The McGucken framework supplies the unification of two principles that have long been treated as belonging to different physical layers — Huygens' Principle (the classical wave-propagation principle of 1690) and the holographic principle ('t Hooft 1993; Susskind 1995). The unification is a forced theorem of dx₄/dt = ic: the two principles are two readings of the same single mechanism, the McGucken Point recursion at every boundary surface.

**Theorem 19 (Huygens = Holography; restated from [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Theorem 24]).** *Under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic, Huygens' Principle and the holographic principle are two formulations of the same geometric fact: the physics of the bulk region enclosed by a McGucken Sphere at time $t + dt$ is fully determined by source data on the two-dimensional surface of the McGucken Sphere at time t. The bulk-to-boundary encoding of the holographic principle is the surface-sourcing of bulk wavefronts of Huygens' Principle; the (d+1)-to-d dimensional reduction of holography is the bulk-to-surface restriction of the iterated McGucken Sphere structure. Specifically:*

*(H1) Huygens' classical-wave reading.* Every point of a wavefront is itself a source of secondary wavelets; the envelope of secondary wavelets is the next wavefront (Theorem 5). The bulk wave amplitude at $t + dt$ is determined by source data — wavelet phases and amplitudes — on the boundary surface at t.

*(H2) Holographic quantum-gravitational reading.* The bulk gravitational/quantum-field content at $t + dt$ is determined by boundary data on the holographic screen at t. Specifically, the AdS/CFT dictionary $Z_{CFT}[\phi_0] = Z_{AdS}[φ |_∂ = \phi_0]$ (Theorem 23 of [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime]) is the algebraic form of this surface-sources-bulk relation.

*The two readings are two algebraic projections of the McGucken Point recursion. Every boundary surface point is a McGucken Point that generates a McGucken Sphere; the bulk content is the content of the Sphere-chain descending from the boundary Points; the boundary determines the bulk because the boundary Points and the bulk Points are the same Points in the same recursion, viewed at different stages.*

*Proof.* The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p, t)$ at time t has surface points at radius $c(t - t_p)$. Each surface point $q$ is itself a McGucken Point with its own pointwise operator $\mathcal F_q$ and phase amplitude $\psi_q$ (Definition 7). The secondary Spheres $\Sigma_+(q)$ from these surface points expand at +ic; their envelope at time $t + dt$ is the next wavefront $\Sigma_+(p, t + dt)$ (Theorem 5). The bulk amplitude inside $\Sigma_+(p, t + dt)$ is determined by integration over the surface data $\{\psi_q: q ∈ \Sigma_+(p, t)\}$ via the Huygens/Rayleigh–Sommerfeld integral. This is the surface-sources-bulk relation.

For (H2), the same recursion in the holographic reading: every boundary surface point is a McGucken Point, with its bulk descendants determined by the same self-replicating Sphere mechanism. The AdS/CFT dictionary computes the bulk path integral by boundary CFT generating functional; both compute the same Sphere-chain content. ∎

**Corollary 19a (AdS/CFT as theorem).** *The AdS/CFT correspondence — specifically the GKP–Witten dictionary $Z_{CFT}[\phi_0] = Z_{AdS}[φ |_∂ = \phi_0]$ — is a theorem of the McGucken Principle, established by recognising that both sides compute the same content: the total content of the McGucken Point recursion descending from the boundary Points into the bulk Sphere-chain. The thousands of consistency checks across the AdS/CFT literature are confirmations that two parametrisations of the same recursion content agree, which they must. AdS/CFT is two parametrisations of one underlying Point recursion, with the McGucken framework supplying the recursion that both parametrisations parametrise.*

**Corollary 19b (Cosmological holography supplied directly).** *The McGucken framework supplies holography beyond AdS/CFT to our actual de Sitter universe. The cosmological McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(Big Bang)$ is the universe's outermost holographic screen, with present radius $R_H = c/H_0$ (the Hubble radius). Cosmological entanglement entropies are mode-counts on this Sphere. The de Sitter cosmological horizon's Bekenstein–Hawking entropy is, by Theorem 30 below, the count of x₄-stationary modes piercing the de Sitter horizon, identical in structure to the AdS analogue but in a positive-curvature cosmological background. AdS/CFT's restriction to anti-de Sitter spacetimes (which our universe is not) is therefore not a limitation of holography itself; it is a limitation of the AdS/CFT parametrisation of the underlying Sphere recursion. The McGucken framework supplies cosmological holography directly.*

**The reach of Theorem 19.** The Huygens=Holography unification is the pivot on which the seven emergent-spacetime programmes collapse into a single mechanism. Penrose's twistor space ℂℙ³ is the parametrisation of McGucken Spheres (Theorem 37 of [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime]).
