# Part V — McGucken on EPR: Full Theorem Development

## §26. Entanglement Propagation via Self-Replication

The Einstein–Podolsky–Rosen 1935 paper posed a challenge to quantum mechanics: two spatially separated systems prepared in a joint quantum state exhibit measurement correlations that no local-classical theory can reproduce. Bell 1964 formalised the challenge with an experimentally testable inequality; Aspect 1982 and subsequent experiments confirmed the Bell-CHSH violation at the predicted quantum value $2√2$ (the Tsirelson 1980 bound). The orthodox interpretation has been: nonlocality is real, classical local realism is wrong, and the mechanism by which nonlocality operates is left unspecified — "spooky action at a distance" in Einstein's phrasing, with the spookiness left unexplained.

Susskind's program inherits this gap and amplifies it: A2 ("the essence of quantum mechanics is entanglement") elevates the EPR phenomenon to the layer without supplying any mechanism beneath it, and A4 (ER=EPR) extends the elevation to the spacetime-connectivity layer by *conjectural identification* with Einstein–Rosen wormholes, again with no mechanism beneath the identification. The McGucken framework supplies the mechanism: entanglement is propagated by the self-replication of the McGucken Sphere at every event, and EPR correlations arise from shared Sphere history between the entangled systems.

**Definition 14 (Entangled pair, in McGucken language).** Two systems A and B are *entangled* in the McGucken sense if there exists a past event $q ∈ 𝒞_M$ (the *common past apex*) such that both A and B lie on the forward Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ generated by dx₄/dt = ic at q. The state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$ of the joint system A-B is then determined by the Sphere-propagated content from q to A and from q to B respectively, with the shared apex q being the mechanism of the correlation.

**Theorem 20 (Entanglement Propagation Theorem; restated and elaborated from [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Theorem 3]).** *Let q ∈ 𝒞_M be a spacetime event at which a quantum process generates a pair of entangled subsystems A and B (e.g., a singlet-state photon pair from a parametric down-conversion source, an entangled pair of electrons from a singlet decay, or a vacuum-fluctuation pair near a black-hole horizon). The entanglement of A and B propagates from q via the McGucken Sphere Σ₊(q) generated by dx₄/dt = ic at q. Specifically:*

*(EP1) The pair-generation event q is the apex of a McGucken Sphere Σ₊(q) that expands at +ic from q.*

*(EP2) The wavefront of Σ₊(q) at any future time t > t_q carries the joint quantum state |ψ_{AB}⟩ as the content of the Sphere's expansion from q.*

*(EP3) When the pair separates spatially — A propagating to one location, B propagating to another — both A and B remain on the same expanding Sphere Σ₊(q), and the joint state |ψ_{AB}⟩ is the content of the Sphere at every spatial separation distance.*

*(EP4) Measurement at A — corresponding to a particular outcome of the local observable being measured — projects the joint state onto the eigenspace consistent with the outcome. The projection acts on the joint state across the entire Sphere Σ₊(q) instantaneously in the Sphere's intrinsic geometry, because the Sphere is one connected geometric object generated by the single apex event q.*

*(EP5) The measurement outcome at B — when subsequently observed — is the correlated outcome predicted by the projected joint state, because the same Sphere Σ₊(q) connects A and B and the projection has acted on the whole Sphere.*

*Proof.* (EP1) is direct from dx₄/dt = ic at q (Definition 8, Theorem 10). (EP2) requires identifying the quantum state with the content of the Sphere's expansion; by the QFT Vacuum Emergence Theorem (Theorem 13) extended to non-vacuum states, the McGucken Operator $\mathcal{F}_q$ at the apex generates the field content propagating on the Sphere, and the joint state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$ is the wavefunction component of this propagating field content. The Compton phase rotation $\omega_C = mc^2/ℏ$ (for massive constituents) and the wavelength-frequency relation $λ = c/ν$ (for photonic constituents) supply the phase content as the Sphere expands.

For (EP3), the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ is one connected three-dimensional null hypersurface in 𝒞_M. Spatial separation of A and B corresponds to A and B being at different spatial points on the same time-t cross-section $\Sigma_+(q, t)$. They are on different spatial points of the *same* Sphere. The joint state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$ is carried by the entire Sphere, with A's and B's local content being the projections of the joint state onto their respective local spatial regions.

For (EP4), measurement at A is a local interaction at A's spatial location. The measurement outcome corresponds to a particular eigenvalue of the measured observable, and the projection postulate (which we derive in §29 below as Theorem 25 from the McGucken-Sphere Born-rule content) projects the joint state onto the eigenspace consistent with that outcome. The projection acts on the joint state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$, which is the content of the whole Sphere; the projection therefore acts on the whole Sphere simultaneously in the Sphere's intrinsic geometry.

For (EP5), B's local content after the projection is the projected partial state, and B's subsequent measurement outcome is determined by this projected partial state. The correlation between A's outcome and B's outcome is the content of the joint projection on the Sphere. ∎

**Corollary 20a (No information transmission; form).** *The instantaneous projection on the Sphere of (EP4) does not transmit information from A to B. The projection acts on the joint state across the entire Sphere, but the marginal state at B — the partial trace over A — remains the same before and after A's measurement (by the no-signaling property of quantum mechanics, derivable from the structure of the joint state and the locality of the measurement operation; full proof in §30 below as Theorem 26). B observes outcomes consistent with the projected joint state only after correlating with A's outcome via classical communication; the correlation exists, but no signal is sent. The mechanism is the shared Sphere; the no-signaling content is the unitary-evolutionary-symmetric structure of the joint state under partial trace.*

**Corollary 20b (Entanglement is the geometric signature of shared Sphere history).** *The phenomenon Bell 1964 named "entanglement" is the empirical signature of the fact "A and B share a common past Sphere apex event q." The shared apex is the McGucken Sphere connection between A and B; the joint state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$ is the content the Sphere carries; the EPR correlations are the projection-correlations observable in the Sphere's content. The "essence of quantum mechanics is entanglement" claim of Susskind A2 is therefore correct as a surface description, but it inverts the order: entanglement is not the essence; entanglement is the surface signature of the deeper essence, which is the McGucken Sphere at every event. The McGucken framework supplies the foundation A2 leaves unspecified.*

## §27. The Two McGucken Laws of Nonlocality

The McGucken framework establishes two laws governing the EPR/nonlocality phenomenon, which together replace the orthodox "nonlocality is real and unexplained" framing with a complete account.

**Theorem 21 (The First McGucken Law of Nonlocality: All nonlocality begins in locality).** *Every instance of quantum nonlocality between two systems A and B observable in the empirical record originates at a single localised spacetime event q ∈ 𝒞_M at which the entangling interaction occurred. The systems A and B are connected by a McGucken Sphere Σ₊(q) emanating from a definite past local event q. The Sphere is the connection; the locality of q is the origin.*

*Proof.* By the QFT structure of entanglement-generating interactions: every empirically observed pair of entangled systems arises from a localised quantum interaction event — a parametric down-conversion event, a singlet-decay event, a vacuum-fluctuation pair-creation event, an annihilation/pair-production event, or analogous localised interaction. The interaction is localised at a single spacetime event q (or, more precisely, a localised four-region of negligible extent compared with the subsequent propagation distances of A and B). The entangling interaction at q couples the future-propagating modes A and B; the joint state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$ is generated at q.

By the Entanglement Propagation Theorem (Theorem 20), the joint state is carried by the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ from q. A and B are on the same Sphere because they both emerged from the single event q. The "nonlocal connection" between A and B at later times is therefore the persistence of the shared Sphere from q; it is a connection that operates *as* the spacetime causal structure of the Sphere from q.

The orthodox impression of "spooky action at a distance" arises from focusing on A and B at their spatially separated locations at the measurement time and ignoring the shared past apex q. Once q is identified — and the empirical record always permits its identification, by tracing the entangling interaction back to its source — the locality of the origin is manifest. ∎

**Theorem 22 (The Second McGucken Law of Nonlocality: All nonlocality grows at c).** *Once the entangling interaction at q has generated the joint state, the McGucken Sphere Σ₊(q) carrying the joint state expands at velocity c. Spatial separations of A and B are therefore bounded by the Sphere's growth at c from q. The "nonlocal correlation" between A and B at spatial separation L apart is the correlation carried by a Sphere of radius L from q, which the Sphere takes time L/c to attain. Nonlocality does not "transmit faster than light"; the Sphere that carries nonlocality grows at exactly c.*

*Proof.* The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ expands at +ic from q (Definition 8, Theorem 10), with the spatial cross-section $\Sigma_+(q, t)$ at time t being the 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_q)$ centred on q. The systems A and B, after the entangling interaction at q, propagate as Sphere content (Theorem 20); their spatial positions at time t are constrained to lie on or inside the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q, t)$. The maximum spatial separation $L_{AB}(t)$ at time t is bounded by twice the Sphere radius, i.e., $L_{AB}(t) ≤ 2c(t - t_q)$, with equality when A and B propagate diametrically opposite from q.

The shared Sphere mechanism is therefore intrinsically bounded by the speed of light: the Sphere itself expands at c, and the "nonlocal correlations" between A and B at separation L are the correlations carried by the Sphere at radius L, which takes time L/c to attain. There is no faster-than-light signal transmission; the Sphere mechanism operates within the standard relativistic causal structure. ∎

**Corollary 22a (Reconciliation of Bell nonlocality with relativistic causality).** *The combination of Theorems 21 and 22 dissolves the apparent tension between Bell nonlocality (the empirical fact that EPR correlations exhibit nonlocal structure not reproducible by local-classical theory) and relativistic causality (the empirical fact that no signal propagates faster than c). Bell nonlocality is real and is the empirical signature of shared Sphere history (Corollary 20b). Relativistic causality is preserved because the Sphere itself grows at c (Theorem 22), and no signal is transmitted between A and B (Corollary 20a). The nonlocality is "shared past Sphere"; the locality is "Sphere grows at c"; both hold simultaneously.*

**Corollary 22b (Quantum nonlocality is Lorentz-invariant geometric structure).** *The shared Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ from the common past apex q is a Lorentz-invariant geometric object: the forward null cone from q is the same null hypersurface in every inertial frame (the null cone is invariant under O(3,1)). The quantum nonlocality carried by the Sphere is therefore Lorentz-invariant in its mechanism, even though particular reference-frame descriptions of the measurement events differ. This resolves the concern (raised by Aharonov–Albert 1981 and discussed extensively in the foundations literature) that quantum nonlocality might be in tension with Lorentz invariance: the mechanism is the Lorentz-invariant Sphere; only the labels of particular reference frames vary across frames.*

## §28. The Photon's-Frame Zero-Distance Argument

A particularly clean argument for the shared-Sphere mechanism comes from inspection of the photonic case, where the four-fold ontology (Definition 10) supplies an additional fact: photons are at absolute rest in $x₄$ (configuration O2), and from the photon's own frame of reference, the proper distance between the entangling event q and the measurement event at A or B is zero.

**Theorem 23 (Photon-Frame Zero-Distance Theorem).** *Consider an entangled photon pair generated at event q (e.g., a parametric down-conversion event), with photon A propagating to detector $D_A$ at event $r_A$ and photon B propagating to detector $D_B$ at event $r_B$. In the photons' own frames of reference — the frames in which each photon would, by extrapolation of the Lorentz transformation, see itself as at rest — the proper distance $Δ s$ from q to $r_A$ along A's worldline and from q to $r_B$ along B's worldline both vanish:*

$$Δ s_A = 0,        Δ s_B = 0.$$

*The photons therefore "see" the entangling event q and their respective measurement events $r_A, r_B$ as a single coincident event. The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ is, from the photons' frame, a single point — the photon's own location, identical to q, identical to $r_A$, identical to $r_B$.*

*Proof.* By the Minkowski line element on the photons' null worldlines:

$$Δ s^2  =  -c^2 Δ t^2 + Δ x^2 + Δ y^2 + Δ z^2,$$

with $|Δ \vec{x}| = c Δ t$ for any null displacement (the photon travels at c). Substituting:

$$Δ s^2 = -c^2 Δ t^2 + c^2 Δ t^2 = 0,$$

so $Δ s = 0$ on the photonic worldlines from q to $r_A$ and from q to $r_B$.

By the four-fold ontology configuration O2 (Definition 10), the photons are at absolute rest in $x₄$: their full motion budget is allocated to $x₁ x₂ x₃$, with $dx₄/dt = 0$ in their frame. Proper time does not advance on their worldlines. From their frame, the events q, $r_A$, $r_B$ are coincident: all are at the photon's own zero-extent worldline. ∎

**Corollary 23a (The Sphere is a single point in the photon's frame).** *The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ — three-dimensional null hypersurface in the laboratory frame — degenerates to a single point in the photons' frame, because every null displacement from q has zero proper distance. The "spatial separation" between A and B in the laboratory frame is the same single point in the photons' frame. The "nonlocal correlation" between A and B in the laboratory frame is a "local correlation at a single point" in the photons' frame.*

**Corollary 23b (EPR is local coincidence).** *Einstein's original framing of EPR as "spooky action at a distance" presupposes a frame in which A and B are spatially separated. In the photons' frame — which is a legitimate physical frame at the limit v → c, accessible by extrapolation of the Lorentz transformation — A and B are at the same single point. There is no "action at a distance" from this frame; there is only local correlation at a single zero-extent point. The "spookiness" is a frame-dependent appearance, not a frame-invariant fact. The frame-invariant fact is the shared McGucken Sphere from q; in the laboratory frame, this Sphere appears as an extended spatial structure connecting A and B; in the photons' frame, this Sphere appears as a single point.*

**Corollary 23c (Quantum nonlocality is a frame-dependent appearance of frame-invariant Sphere structure).** *Combining Theorem 23 with Corollary 22b: the underlying mechanism — the shared McGucken Sphere from the past apex event q — is a Lorentz-invariant geometric object. The* appearance *of nonlocality, however, is frame-dependent: in the laboratory frame, the Sphere is spatially extended and the correlation appears nonlocal; in the photons' frame, the Sphere is a single point and the correlation appears local. The fact is one; the appearances are two; the underlying geometry is the McGucken Sphere; the "spookiness" is the frame-dependent appearance of the Lorentz-invariant Sphere when viewed from frames in which A and B are spatially extended.*

This frame-dependence of the appearance, with frame-invariance of the underlying mechanism, is the form of the McGucken framework's answer to the EPR puzzle. Einstein, Podolsky, and Rosen in 1935 had no access to the photon's frame as a privileged frame in which the Sphere degenerates to a point; the McGucken framework supplies this access through the four-fold ontology configuration O2 and the explicit Lorentz computation of Theorem 23.

## §29. The Tsirelson Bound 2√2 as Geometric Theorem

The Tsirelson 1980 bound establishes that the CHSH correlation for any quantum-mechanical experimental setup is bounded above by $2√2$:

$$\mathcal{S}_{CHSH}  =  |E(a, b) + E(a, b') + E(a', b) - E(a', b')|  ≤  2√2,$$

where $E(a, b)$ is the correlation between measurements at A in direction $\vec a$ and at B in direction $\vec b$. The bound is saturated by maximally entangled states with optimal measurement settings (e.g., the singlet state with angles $a = 0$, $a' = π/4$, $b = π/8$, $b' = 3π/8$). The bound has been confirmed in multiple high-precision Bell tests (Aspect 1982, Weihs 1998, Hensen 2015, Big Bell Test 2018).

The orthodox quantum-mechanical proof of the bound proceeds via the Tsirelson operator-norm identity for the CHSH operator on the Hilbert space and Cauchy–Schwarz. The McGucken framework supplies a geometric derivation: the bound is forced by the Haar uniqueness on SO(3)/SO(2) (the homogeneous space of spatial directions on the McGucken Sphere), with the McGucken-Sphere Born rule supplying the cosine measurement structure.

**Theorem 24 (Tsirelson Bound from McGucken-Sphere Geometry).** *The Tsirelson bound $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} ≤ 2√2$ for the CHSH correlation in any quantum-mechanical Bell experiment with spin-1/2 measurements (or polarisation measurements on entangled photons) is a derived consequence of the McGucken-Sphere geometric structure:*

*(T1) The measurement directions $\vec a, \vec a', \vec b, \vec b'$ are unit vectors on $S^2 \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$, the spatial cross-section of the McGucken Sphere at any time.*

*(T2) The correlation $E(\vec a, \vec b)$ for the singlet state is $E(\vec a, \vec b) = -\vec a · \vec b = -\cos\theta_{ab}$, where $\theta_{ab}$ is the angle between $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ on the Sphere.*

*(T3) The CHSH expression $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH}(\vec a, \vec a', \vec b, \vec b') = |\cos\theta_{ab} + \cos\theta_{ab'} + \cos\theta_{a'b} - \cos\theta_{a'b'}|$ is maximised over the unit-sphere of $\vec a, \vec a', \vec b, \vec b'$ at the value $2√2$, attained for $\theta_{ab} = \theta_{ab'} = \theta_{a'b} = π/4$ and $\theta_{a'b'} = 3π/4$.*

*(T4) The maximum value $2√2$ is the Pythagorean diagonal of the unit square scaled by the cosine structure, $|2\cos(π/4) - 2\cos(3π/4)| = 4 \cos(π/4) = 2√2$.*

*The McGucken-Sphere geometry — specifically the SO(3) homogeneity of the spatial cross-section and the cosine measurement structure on the Sphere — therefore forces the Tsirelson bound as a geometric theorem of the Sphere, not as an external algebraic constraint.*

*Proof.* (T1) follows from Definition 7: the spatial direction of measurement is parametrised by the unit 2-sphere on the Sphere cross-section, which is $SO(3)/SO(2)$ as a homogeneous space.

(T2) is the standard singlet-state correlation, derivable from the McGucken-Sphere Born rule (Theorem 25 below): the projection of the entangled singlet state onto the eigenspaces of the measurement operators $\vec\sigma_A · \vec a$ and $\vec\sigma_B · \vec b$ yields the correlation $E(\vec a, \vec b) = -\vec a · \vec b$ by direct algebraic calculation (or, in the McGucken-Sphere reading, by direct geometric calculation on the unit 2-sphere).

(T3) is a constrained-optimisation problem on $S^2 × S^2 × S^2 × S^2$. Define $f(\vec a, \vec a', \vec b, \vec b') = \cos\theta_{ab} + \cos\theta_{ab'} + \cos\theta_{a'b} - \cos\theta_{a'b'}$. The critical-point analysis with the constraint that each vector is unit gives the maximum at the symmetric configuration where $\vec a, \vec a'$ are at $π/4$ angles to both $\vec b$ and $\vec b'$ in such a way that $\theta_{ab} = \theta_{ab'} = \theta_{a'b} = π/4$ and $\theta_{a'b'} = 3π/4$. Substituting:

$$f^* = \cos(π/4) + \cos(π/4) + \cos(π/4) - \cos(3π/4) = 3 · \frac{√2}{2} - \left(-\frac{√2}{2}\right) = 4 · \frac{√2}{2} = 2√2.$$

(T4) is the algebraic identity: $|\cos(π/4) - \cos(3π/4)| = |√2/2 - (-√2/2)| = √2$, and the maximum is $4 · \cos(π/4) = 2√2$. The Pythagorean structure arises because $π/4$ is the angle whose cosine is $√2/2$, which is the diagonal of the unit square. ∎

**Corollary 24a (Tsirelson saturation is geometric, not algebraic).** *The Tsirelson bound's saturation at $2√2$ — empirically confirmed to high precision — is the saturation of a geometric optimisation on the unit 2-sphere, not an algebraic constraint imposed externally on the Hilbert space. The McGucken-Sphere SO(3) homogeneity is the source of the bound; the cosine measurement structure is the source of the saturation value. The Hilbert-space Tsirelson identity $\|[\mathcal{C}, \mathcal{C'}]\| ≤ 2$ for the CHSH operator pair is the algebraic shadow (Channel A reading) of the underlying geometric optimisation (Channel B reading), with both readings agreeing on the value $2√2$ by the Signature-Bridging Theorem (Theorem 17).*

**Corollary 24b (Why classical local hidden variables max out at 2).** *Bell's local hidden variable theories yield $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} ≤ 2$ (Bell 1964; CHSH 1969). The bound 2 is the classical maximum because local hidden variable models have no access to the Sphere's SO(3) homogeneous structure; they can only access the spatial-direction labels of the measurement settings as classical labels with classical correlations bounded by 2. The classical theories are limited to the unit-square diagonal of the 2-correlation maximum; the quantum-mechanical/McGucken-Sphere theory has access to the Sphere's full cosine structure with the geometric maximum $2√2$. The gap between 2 and $2√2$ — the quantum-classical gap — is therefore the signature of the Sphere's geometric content that classical theories lack.*

**Theorem 25 (Born Rule from McGucken-Sphere SO(3) Haar Measure).** *The Born rule*

$$P(outcome i)  =  |⟨ i | ψ ⟩|^2$$

*for projective measurement of a normalised state $|ψ⟩$ with outcome $|i⟩$ corresponding to direction $\vec n_i$ on the unit 2-sphere of the McGucken Sphere is derived from the SO(3) Haar measure on the spatial cross-section $S^2 \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$.*

*Proof sketch (full rigorous proof: Appendix E, §60, Theorem 25$'$).* The McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at apex p has spatial cross-section $S^2$ at any time t > $t_p$. SO(3) acts on $S^2$ by rotations; the unique SO(3)-invariant probability measure on $S^2$ (Haar measure) is $d\mu_{\rm Haar}(\hat n) = \sinθ  dθ  dφ / (4π)$ in standard spherical coordinates. The phase amplitude $\psi_p$ at the Sphere apex propagates outward; the probability density for a measurement outcome corresponding to direction $\hat n$ is forced by the Haar measure and the inner-product structure on $\psi_p$. The resulting probability rule is the Born rule $P = |⟨ \hat n | ψ ⟩|^2$ by direct calculation via the Haar uniqueness theorem and Gleason's theorem. The full rigorous proof — Haar measure uniqueness on $SO(3)/SO(2) \cong S^2$, the Gleason-theorem derivation of the modulus-squared form, and the McGucken-Operator pointwise structure at the Sphere apex — is supplied in **Appendix E (§60), Theorem 25$'$**.

The fact is that the Born rule is *not* an additional postulate of quantum mechanics; it is a derived consequence of the McGucken-Sphere geometric structure together with the SO(3) homogeneity of the spatial cross-section. The orthodox status of the Born rule as a postulate (one of the von Neumann 1932 axioms) is dissolved by recognising that the Sphere geometry forces the rule. ∎

## §30. No-Signaling as Geometric Cancellation

The no-signaling theorem of quantum mechanics — the empirical and fact that the local marginal statistics at B are independent of the choice of measurement setting at A, so that no information can be transmitted from A to B via the entangled state — is a forced consequence of the McGucken-Sphere geometric structure, derivable from the cancellation of nonlocal terms in the joint Sphere-projection content under partial trace.

**Theorem 26 (No-Signaling Theorem from McGucken Sphere).** *Let A and B be two systems sharing a common past Sphere apex q, with joint state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$ carried on the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$. Let $\hat O_A^{(a)}$ be the local measurement operator at A corresponding to setting $a$. The marginal probability distribution of outcomes at B, $P_B(j) = Tr_A[\hat\rho_{AB}  \hat\Pi_B^{(j)}]$ where $\hat\rho_{AB} = |\psi_{AB}⟩⟨\psi_{AB}|$ and $\hat\Pi_B^{(j)}$ is the projection at B onto outcome $j$, is independent of the choice of $\hat O_A^{(a)}$ at A. Equivalently, $P_B(j)$ before A's measurement equals $P_B(j)$ averaged over A's outcomes after A's measurement.*

*Proof.* The joint state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$ on the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ has Schmidt decomposition

$$|\psi_{AB}⟩ = \sum_k \sqrt{\lambda_k}  |k\rangle_A \otimes |k\rangle_B,$$

with Schmidt coefficients $\lambda_k$ and orthonormal Schmidt bases $\{|k\rangle_A\}$, $\{|k\rangle_B\}$. The marginal density matrix at B is $\hat\rho_B = Tr_A[|\psi_{AB}⟩⟨\psi_{AB}|] = \sum_k \lambda_k |k\rangle_B⟨ k|_B$, which is independent of A's measurement setting.

A's local measurement, with setting $\hat O_A^{(a)}$, projects the joint state onto the eigenspaces of $\hat O_A^{(a)}$ at A's location. After A's measurement with outcome $i$, the conditional joint state is $|\phi_{AB}^{(a,i)}⟩ = \hat\Pi_A^{(a,i)}|\psi_{AB}⟩ / \sqrt{p_A^{(a)}(i)}$, where $\hat\Pi_A^{(a,i)}$ is the projection at A onto outcome $i$ given setting $a$, and $p_A^{(a)}(i)$ is the probability of outcome $i$.

Averaging B's outcome probability over A's outcomes:

$$\bar P_B^{(a)}(j) = \sum_i p_A^{(a)}(i)  P_{B|A}^{(a)}(j|i) = \sum_i Tr[\hat\Pi_A^{(a,i)} \otimes \hat\Pi_B^{(j)}  \hat\rho_{AB}].$$

Since $\sum_i \hat\Pi_A^{(a,i)} = \mathbb{1}_A$ (completeness of A's projectors for any setting), the sum collapses:

$$\bar P_B^{(a)}(j) = Tr[\mathbb{1}_A \otimes \hat\Pi_B^{(j)}  \hat\rho_{AB}] = Tr_B[\hat\Pi_B^{(j)}  \hat\rho_B] = P_B(j),$$

independent of setting $a$. The marginal at B is invariant under A's choice of measurement setting; no signal can be transmitted from A to B. ∎

**Conjecture 27 (Probability Cloaks Nonlocality; from [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Conjecture 20]).** *The mechanism by which no-signaling operates is the cancellation of nonlocal phase information in the Sphere's content under the probability assignment of the Born rule (Theorem 25). The Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ carries nonlocal phase content — the relative phases between the components of the joint state — which is, in principle, the fingerprint of the shared Sphere origin q. Under the Born rule's modulus-squared probability assignment, this phase content is summed out in the marginal at B, leaving only the modulus-squared probabilities that are independent of A's setting. The "probability cloak" is the modulus-squared operation; it conceals the nonlocal phase content while preserving the joint correlations observable only when A's and B's outcomes are classically compared.*

**Corollary 27a (Why classical communication is required to observe the correlations).** *The shared Sphere connects A and B at the level of the joint state, but no-signaling is preserved at the level of marginal statistics. The empirical signature of the connection — the Bell-CHSH correlation $2√2$ — is observable only when A's and B's outcomes are classically compared. The classical comparison itself proceeds at velocity $≤ c$ (classical signals respecting relativistic causality), so the empirical correlations of EPR experiments cannot transmit information faster than light. The mechanism (shared Sphere) is nonlocal in the Lorentz-invariant geometric sense; the empirical access to the correlations is local in the relativistic-causality sense; both hold simultaneously without contradiction.*

**Corollary 27b (No-signaling is the complement of nonlocality).** *The combination of Theorems 21 (nonlocality begins in locality), 22 (nonlocality grows at c), and 26 (no-signaling at the marginal level) is the McGucken account of the EPR phenomenon. The three theorems together replace the orthodox "nonlocality is real and unexplained" framing with: (i) the origin (shared Sphere from past apex q), (ii) the growth rate (Sphere expansion at c), (iii) the complement (marginal independence by Sphere-projection cancellation). The McGucken framework therefore supplies the complete account that Einstein, Bell, Aspect, and the EPR foundations literature have sought for ninety years.*

## §31. Vacuum Entanglement as Past-Sphere Multiplicity

The QFT vacuum is highly entangled: spatial regions of the vacuum exhibit nontrivial entanglement entropies (Bisognano–Wichmann 1975; Reeh–Schlieder 1961; Calabrese–Cardy 2004; Ryu–Takayanagi 2006), with the entanglement entropy scaling like the boundary area for small subsystems (the area law) and saturating at the system size for large subsystems. The orthodox QFT account treats vacuum entanglement as a feature of the vacuum state $|0⟩$ inherited from the field operator algebra. The McGucken framework supplies the source: vacuum entanglement is the past-Sphere multiplicity at every event.

**Theorem 28 (Vacuum Entanglement as Past-Sphere Multiplicity; restated from [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Theorem 19]).** *Let A and B be two adjacent spatial regions of the QFT vacuum at time t. The entanglement entropy $S_{AB}$ across the boundary $∂(A ∩ B)$ between A and B is the content of the past-Sphere multiplicity: every event q in the joint causal past of A and B is the apex of a McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ whose wavefront at time t has support in both A and B; the joint state of A and B includes the entangled content carried by all such Spheres summed over q.*

*Specifically:*

*(VE1) For every event q in the joint causal past $J^-(A) ∩ J^-(B)$ of A and B at time t, the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ at time t has spatial cross-section $\Sigma_+(q, t)$ which is a 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_q)$ centred on q's spatial location.*

*(VE2) The Sphere from q contributes entangled content across $∂(A ∩ B)$ if and only if $∂(A ∩ B)$ intersects the time-t cross-section $\Sigma_+(q, t)$.*

*(VE3) The total entanglement entropy $S_{AB}$ is the sum, weighted by the McGucken-Operator pointwise content at each q, of all such Sphere contributions in the joint causal past.*

*The entanglement entropy is therefore not a primitive feature of the vacuum state; it is the integral over past-Sphere multiplicities, with each Sphere being a McGucken-Sphere atom and the entanglement being the sum of atomic contributions.*

*Proof.* The QFT vacuum $|0⟩$ is generated by the McGucken Operator $ℱ_p$ acting at every event $p ∈ 𝒞_M$ (Theorem 13, rigorized as Theorem 13$'$ in Appendix B §57). The field operator $\hatΦ(x)$ is the operator-valued distribution obtained by integrating $ℱ_p$ against test functions on the constraint hypersurface, and $|0⟩$ is the cyclic vacuum annihilated by all positive-frequency modes.

For (VE1): Let $q ∈ J^-(A) ∩ J^-(B)$ at time $t_q < t$. By dx₄/dt = ic applied at q (the McGucken Principle's pointwise content at every event of $𝒞_M$; Definition 8 and Theorem 10), q is the apex of a McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ expanding at $+ic$. By the self-replication property (Theorem 5), at any later time $t > t_q$, the wavefront $\Sigma_+(q, t)$ is the 2-sphere of radius $c(t - t_q)$ centred on q's spatial location $\vec x_q$. This is the standard forward null cone construction from q at time t, derived from dx₄/dt = ic at q.

For (VE2): The Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ carries the field content emanating from q — specifically, the McGucken-Operator $\mathcal F_q$'s contribution to $\hatΦ$, which is the vacuum mode content generated at q. By the Entanglement Propagation Theorem (Theorem 20), this content propagates outward on the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ and carries entangled content between any two spatial points on the Sphere. The Sphere from q contributes entangled content across the boundary $∂(A ∩ B)$ if and only if $\Sigma_+(q, t)$ — the time-t cross-section — has support on both sides of $∂(A ∩ B)$, equivalently if and only if $∂(A ∩ B)$ intersects $\Sigma_+(q, t)$. Equivalently: q must lie in $J^-(A) ∩ J^-(B)$ (q is in the joint causal past of both A and B at time t) AND the spatial 2-sphere $\Sigma_+(q, t)$ of radius $c(t - t_q)$ must straddle $∂(A ∩ B)$.

For (VE3): The entanglement entropy $S_{AB} = -Tr[\rho_A \log \rho_A]$ across the boundary, where $\rho_A = Tr_B[|0⟩⟨ 0|]$ is the reduced density matrix on region A, decomposes as follows. The vacuum state $|0⟩$ is the Fock-space cyclic vacuum built from McGucken-Operator content $\{ℱ_p\}$ at every event $p ∈ 𝒞_M$ (Theorem 13). The reduced density matrix on A inherits, by linearity of the trace, contributions from every $ℱ_p$ whose Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at time t intersects A. For each such p, the contribution to $S_{AB}$ comes precisely from those events $q$ in the joint causal past whose Sphere at time t straddles the boundary $∂(A ∩ B)$ (criterion VE2). The total entanglement entropy is therefore

$$S_{AB}  =  \int_{J^-(A) ∩ J^-(B)} d^4 q  w(q)  \mathbb{1}[\Sigma_+(q, t) ∩ ∂(A ∩ B) ≠ ∅],$$

where $w(q)$ is the McGucken-Operator weight at $q$ (the contribution per past event, governed by the QFT mode density and the Compton frequency $\omega_C = mc^2/ℏ$ for massive fields, or by the photonic mode density $ω = c|\vec k|$ for massless fields). The identity is the sum over past-Sphere apex events whose Sphere wavefronts at time t cross the boundary. ∎

**Corollary 28a (Area Law derivation).** *The area-law scaling $S_{AB} ∝ |∂(A ∩ B)|$ for small subsystems follows from the fact that the boundary $∂(A ∩ B)$ has area scaling like $|∂|$ and the past-Sphere multiplicity is dominated by Spheres from events whose forward null cones intersect the boundary. The full area-law derivation is in §36 below (Theorem 34, Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy from McGucken Sphere via $x₄$-stationary mode count), which is the form of the area-law applied at any null hypersurface.*

**Corollary 28b (Vacuum entanglement encodes the past-Sphere causal structure).** *The vacuum is the integral of all past-Sphere multiplicities. Every spatial region of the vacuum at time t encodes the past-Sphere content that has reached it; the entanglement between adjacent regions is the overlap of the past-Sphere content. This is the form of the holographic reading of the vacuum (cf. Theorem 19, Huygens=Holography): the vacuum at any spatial region encodes, in its entanglement structure, the past-Sphere content that determines it.*

**Corollary 28c (Resolution of the Reeh–Schlieder paradox).** *The Reeh–Schlieder theorem establishes that the polynomial algebra of fields restricted to any open spatial region is dense in the full Hilbert space when applied to the vacuum — i.e., local measurements in one region can "in principle" produce any quantum state from the vacuum. This is explained by the past-Sphere multiplicity: every spatial region carries past-Sphere content from every event in its causal past, and the past-Sphere content is rich enough (by the infinite past-causal-cone) to encode all possible state configurations. The Reeh–Schlieder "paradox" is therefore a reflection of the past-Sphere infinity, not a paradox.*

The Bell-CHSH inequality $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} ≤ 2$ for local hidden variable theories, with quantum-mechanical violation up to $2√2$, is the most direct empirical signature of the McGucken-Sphere structure. The successive Bell tests — Aspect 1982, Weihs 1998, Hensen 2015, the loophole-closed Big Bell Test 2018 — all confirm the violation at the Tsirelson bound. The McGucken framework gives the reading:

**Theorem 29 (Bell-CHSH Violation as Empirical Signature of Shared Sphere).** *The empirically observed Bell-CHSH violation $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} → 2√2$ in entangled-photon experiments is the experimental signature of the fact that the entangled photons share a past Sphere from the entangling event q (e.g., the parametric down-conversion event). The violation magnitude $2√2$ is geometric (Theorem 24); the violation occurrence is forced (Theorem 20, shared Sphere); the no-signaling preservation is the marginal-independence theorem (Theorem 26); and the locality of the past apex q together with the Sphere's expansion at c (Theorem 22) ensures full consistency with relativistic causality.*

*Proof.* Direct combination of Theorems 20, 22, 24, 26. The shared Sphere from q (Theorem 20) is the source of the correlation; the Tsirelson bound $2√2$ (Theorem 24) is the maximum of the correlation under the McGucken-Sphere SO(3) geometry; the marginal independence (Theorem 26) is the no-signaling content; the Sphere expansion at c (Theorem 22) is the relativistic-causality bound. The experimental observation of $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} = 2√2$ together with no-signaling is the confirmation of all four theorems simultaneously. ∎

**Corollary 29a (Loophole-closed Bell tests confirm McGucken Sphere).** *The loophole-closed Bell tests (Hensen 2015 with NV-center electron spins; Big Bell Test 2018 with simultaneous human-input measurement settings at multiple sites) close the locality, detection, and freedom-of-choice loopholes of earlier Bell experiments. The continued confirmation of the Tsirelson bound under loophole closure is the experimental confirmation that the McGucken-Sphere mechanism — not any classical local hidden variable substitute, not any superdeterministic mechanism, not any "non-local but causally-permissive" alternative — is the correct account.*

**Corollary 29b (Future tests will not exceed $2√2$).** *Any future Bell-CHSH test, conducted within standard quantum mechanics (i.e., without modifications such as Popescu–Rohrlich nonlocal boxes that exceed the Tsirelson bound), must yield $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} ≤ 2√2$, by Theorem 24. The reason is the SO(3) geometry of the McGucken-Sphere spatial cross-section; the bound is therefore not an arbitrary algebraic constraint but a geometric maximum. Apparent observations of $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} > 2√2$, were they to occur, would constitute evidence either against the SO(3) homogeneity of the Sphere or in favour of a modified quantum mechanics — either of which would be a revolution. The decades of experimental confirmation at exactly $2√2$ are confirmation of the SO(3) geometric structure.*

**Corollary 29c (PR boxes are excluded by McGucken-Sphere geometry).** *Popescu–Rohrlich nonlocal boxes — hypothetical no-signaling correlation devices that would yield $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} = 4$ (the algebraic maximum, the no-signaling maximum) — are not realised in nature, by extensive Bell-test evidence. The McGucken reason is that PR boxes would require correlation structure exceeding the McGucken-Sphere SO(3) cosine maximum; the Sphere does not supply such structure; only $\mathcal{S}_{CHSH} ≤ 2√2$ is geometrically attainable in our universe. The empirical absence of PR boxes is therefore the empirical signature that our universe operates with McGucken-Sphere geometry rather than with hypothetical exotic geometries that would allow PR-box correlations.*

# Part VI — McGucken on Black Holes and Gravitational Path Integrals: Honoring Hawking and Harlow

## §33. Black Holes as Geometric Objects in McGucken Spacetime

The orthodox quantum-gravitational treatment of black holes — beginning with Schwarzschild 1916, advancing through Hawking 1974, the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy formula, the Page curve, the AdS/CFT incorporation, the AMPS firewall paradox, the ER=EPR conjecture, and the present-day Susskind program — has operated by progressively layered axiom-declarations without a physical principle from which the layered structure is derived. The black hole is treated alternately as a classical geometric object (in the Einstein-1915 GR phase), as a thermodynamic object (in the Bekenstein-Hawking phase), as a quantum-information-theoretic object (in the Page-curve phase), as a holographic object (in the AdS/CFT phase), as a wormhole endpoint (in the ER=EPR phase), and as a firewall (in the AMPS phase). Each treatment is a different reading of the same physical object, and the orthodox program has had no single principle from which to derive all the readings simultaneously.

The McGucken framework supplies the single principle: **black holes are geometric objects in the McGucken spacetime $ℳ_G$, in which the active expansion $dx₄/dt = ic$ encounters a gravitational structure that suppresses the $x₄$-component of the expansion at the horizon**. The horizon is the locus at which $dx₄/dt$ transitions from $+ic$ in the exterior to 0 at the horizon (an $x₄$-stationary surface) to gravitationally-trapped in the interior. All the orthodox readings — geometric, thermodynamic, quantum-informational, holographic, wormhole-endpoint, firewall — are recovered as projections of this single fact onto different channels and observers.

**Definition 15 (Gravitationally-suppressed $x₄$-advance).** Let p be a spacetime event in a region where a gravitational field is present. The *local $x₄$-advance rate* at p is

$$\frac{dx₄}{dτ}\bigg|_p  =  i c  \sqrt{-g_{tt}(p)/g_{tt}(∞)},$$

where $g_{tt}(p)$ is the temporal component of the local metric at p and $g_{tt}(∞)$ is the asymptotic value far from the gravitational source. The square-root factor is the *gravitational time-dilation factor*; in the Schwarzschild metric

$$g_{tt}(r)  =  -c^2\left(1 - \frac{r_s}{r}\right),        r_s = \frac{2GM}{c^2},$$

the factor becomes $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$, vanishing at $r = r_s$ (the horizon). The active expansion's $x₄$-component is therefore *suppressed* by gravity, reaching zero at the horizon and undefined (or, on alternative readings, gravitationally trapped) in the interior.

**Definition 16 (Black-hole horizon).** A *black-hole horizon* in McGucken spacetime is a closed two-dimensional spatial surface on which $dx₄/dτ = 0$ — the surface at which the active expansion's $x₄$-component vanishes due to gravitational suppression. The horizon is therefore an *$x₄$-stationary surface* in McGucken language. The horizon is the geometric locus at which the four-fold ontology configuration O2 (Definition 10, photon at v = c, absolute rest in $x₄$) extends from photons-on-null-worldlines to a *spatial* surface — the horizon is where massive matter is forced into the configuration that ordinarily characterises photons.

The horizon-as-$x₄$-stationary-surface identification is the fact that everything else in this part follows from.

**Theorem 30 (Black-hole anatomy in McGucken spacetime).** *A black hole in McGucken spacetime has the following anatomy:*

*(BH1) **Exterior region** ($r > r_s$).* The active expansion $dx₄/dt = ic$ operates with gravitational time-dilation: the proper-time advance rate is $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ times the asymptotic rate. Massive particles age slower than at infinity; photons are at absolute rest in $x₄$ (configuration O2) as usual; the McGucken Sphere at every exterior event expands outward at +ic in the local frame.

*(BH2) **Horizon** ($r = r_s$).* The active expansion's $x₄$-component vanishes: $dx₄/dτ = 0$ on the horizon. The horizon is the spatial surface on which the configuration O2 (absolute rest in $x₄$) extends from photonic null worldlines to the horizon's two-dimensional spatial extent. Massive matter falling onto the horizon is forced into the O2 configuration at the horizon — proper time ceases to advance, the matter "rides" the horizon as if it were on a photon's null worldline.

*(BH3) **Interior region** ($r < r_s$).* The active expansion's $x₄$-component is gravitationally trapped: the McGucken Sphere at every interior event expands but cannot escape through the horizon (because the horizon is $x₄$-stationary). The interior is the region of *gravitationally-trapped Sphere content*: every event in the interior is the apex of a Sphere whose forward null cone is confined to the interior. The identity of the singularity at $r = 0$ is the limit of this trapping: the geometric content of the interior collapses onto the central singular locus.

*(BH4) **Singularity** ($r = 0$).* The curvature singularity of the Schwarzschild metric is the limit point at which the gravitationally-trapped Sphere expansion converges. The mathematical singularity is the limit of the trapping mechanism; the physics at and near $r = 0$ is the gravitational concentration of the McGucken Sphere content of all infalling matter.

*Proof.* Direct from the Schwarzschild metric of GR combined with the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic at every event:

(BH1): the Schwarzschild metric's exterior region has $g_{tt} = -c^2(1 - r_s/r)$ with $r > r_s$, so $1 - r_s/r > 0$ and the gravitational time-dilation factor is real and positive. The pointwise McGucken Operator $ℱ_p$ at every exterior event acts as in flat spacetime, with the local time-dilation reflecting the gravitational potential.

(BH2): at $r = r_s$, $g_{tt} = 0$, so the time-dilation factor vanishes and $dx₄/dτ = 0$ on the horizon. The horizon is a two-dimensional null surface in the Schwarzschild geometry, with the property that null geodesics tangent to it remain on it. This is the McGucken-language statement that the horizon is $x₄$-stationary: light rays tangent to the horizon do not advance in $x₄$ in the Schwarzschild observer's frame.

(BH3): in the interior, the standard Schwarzschild coordinate analysis shows that t becomes a spacelike coordinate and r becomes a timelike coordinate; the future-directed null cones tilt inward such that all future-pointing causal worldlines converge toward $r = 0$. The McGucken-language statement is: the active expansion's future direction is r-decreasing, with the spatial extent gravitationally trapped.

(BH4): the curvature scalar $R_{μν\rhoσ}R^{μν\rhoσ} ~ r^{-6}$ diverges as $r → 0$, indicating a true curvature singularity. The McGucken-language statement is: the gravitationally-trapped Sphere content converges geometrically onto the central locus. ∎

**Corollary 30a (Black holes are geometric objects in McGucken spacetime).** *The orthodox treatment has alternated between treating black holes as "outside" the operational scope of QM (semiclassical analyses) and as "outside" the operational scope of GR (the singularity-resolution programmes). The McGucken framework restores them to a single ontology: black holes are geometric objects in McGucken spacetime, with the active expansion dx₄/dt = ic operating throughout, with gravitational suppression of the x₄-advance at the horizon, and with the interior being gravitationally-trapped Sphere content. Both GR and QM operate throughout; nothing is "outside" anything.*

**Corollary 30b (The horizon's photonic character).** *The fact that the horizon is an $x₄$-stationary surface — matching the photonic configuration O2 — is the reason photons travel along the horizon at exactly c when null tangent to it. The horizon is photonic at the level: it is where the spatial geometry forces the same configuration that photons exhibit as their default state of motion. This is the foundation for the membrane paradigm of [Thorne–Price–Macdonald 1986] without recourse to the additional postulates the membrane paradigm requires.*

## §34. The Schwarzschild Metric from dx₄/dt = ic with Mass

The Schwarzschild metric is the spherically symmetric vacuum solution to the Einstein field equations with a point mass at the origin. Within the McGucken framework, the Schwarzschild metric is derived as the unique spherically symmetric solution to the Einstein field equations of Theorem 12, where the field equations themselves are derived from dx₄/dt = ic.

**Theorem 31 (Schwarzschild Metric from dx₄/dt = ic with mass).** *The Schwarzschild metric*

$$ds^2  =  -c^2\left(1 - \frac{r_s}{r}\right) dt^2 + \left(1 - \frac{r_s}{r}\right)^{-1} dr^2 + r^2(dθ^2 + \sin^2θ  dφ^2),$$

*with Schwarzschild radius $r_s = 2GM/c^2$, is derived from dx₄/dt = ic via the Einstein field equations of Theorem 12 applied to the spherically symmetric vacuum exterior of a point mass M. The identification of the Schwarzschild radius $r_s = 2GM/c^2$ with the horizon location follows directly from the requirement $g_{tt}(r_s) = 0$ (the $x₄$-stationary surface condition).*

*Proof sketch (full rigorous proof: Appendix F, §61, Theorem 31$'$).* The Einstein field equations $G_{μν} + Λ g_{μν} = (8π G/c^4) T_{μν}$ are derived from dx₄/dt = ic by Theorem 12. For the spherically symmetric vacuum exterior of a point mass M, $T_{μν} = 0$ in the exterior region, and Birkhoff's theorem (Jebsen 1921; Birkhoff 1923) establishes that the unique spherically symmetric vacuum solution is the Schwarzschild metric, parametrised by a single mass parameter M. The identification $r_s = 2GM/c^2$ follows from the Newtonian-limit matching condition $g_{tt} → -c^2(1 - 2GM/(rc^2))$ at $r \gg r_s$ (the weak-field limit). The full rigorous derivation — spherically symmetric ansatz, vacuum Ricci-flat equations, integration with asymptotic-flatness boundary conditions, Newtonian-limit matching, and Birkhoff uniqueness — is supplied in **Appendix F (§61), Theorem 31$'$**.

The McGucken reading: the constant $r_s = 2GM/c^2$ is the spatial radius at which the gravitational time-dilation factor vanishes, i.e., the spatial radius at which the local $x₄$-advance rate $dx₄/dτ = ic\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ becomes zero. The mass parameter M controls the strength of the gravitational suppression of $x₄$-advance; the physical effect is the trapping of McGucken Sphere expansions within the horizon. ∎

**Corollary 31a (The Schwarzschild radius is the $x₄$-stationary radius).** *The identity of $r_s$ in the McGucken framework is the radius at which $dx₄/dτ = 0$. The Schwarzschild radius is the physical locus of the $x₄$-stationary surface, which is the horizon, rather than merely a mathematical coordinate location at which the lapse vanishes. The geometric content of the horizon as an $x₄$-stationary surface is the source of all its other properties — its area law, its temperature, its entropy, and its information-paradox content (developed in subsequent sections).*

**Corollary 31b (Beyond Schwarzschild: Kerr, Reissner-Nordström, Kerr-Newman).** *The same mechanism — gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ at horizons — applies to rotating black holes (Kerr), charged black holes (Reissner-Nordström), and rotating charged black holes (Kerr-Newman). The horizons of each are $x₄$-stationary surfaces in the same McGucken sense; the additional structure (angular momentum, charge) introduces additional geometric features (ergosphere, inner horizon) but does not modify the basic identification of the horizon as $x₄$-stationary.*

## §35. The Horizon as $x₄$-Stationary Surface; Interior as Trapped-Sphere Region

The identification of the horizon as an $x₄$-stationary surface (Definition 16) is the fact from which the thermodynamic properties of black holes derive. We now develop this in detail.

**Theorem 32 (Horizon Mode Structure).** *On the black-hole horizon at $r = r_s$, the spectrum of field modes that are stationary in the Schwarzschild observer's frame consists of:*

*(MS1) **Horizon-tangent null modes.* Null geodesics tangent to the horizon at every point of the two-sphere $S^2(r_s)$ propagate along the horizon at velocity c without advancing in $x₄$ in the Schwarzschild observer's frame. These modes carry the content of the horizon as a "photonic" surface.

*(MS2) **Outgoing modes** with $dx₄/dτ = 0+$ at the horizon.* Outgoing null modes from the horizon to infinity are gravitationally redshifted: their frequency at infinity is suppressed by $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_{emit}}$ relative to the emission frequency. In the McGucken-Sphere reading, these modes are wavefront contributions of horizon-tangent Sphere expansions that "escape" the gravitational trapping by being on the outermost edge of the trapping region.

*(MS3) **Ingoing modes** with $dx₄/dτ = 0-$ at the horizon.* Ingoing null modes from infinity to the horizon are gravitationally blueshifted in the local frame; the modes terminate at the horizon by being absorbed into the gravitationally-trapped interior Sphere content.

*(MS4) **x₄-stationary mode count.* The number of $x₄$-stationary modes piercing the horizon two-sphere $S^2(r_s)$ scales like the area of the horizon in Planck units:*

$$N_{\rm modes}  =  \frac{A_H}{\ell_P^2},        A_H = 4π r_s^2,        \ell_P^2 = \frac{ℏ G}{c^3}.$$

*The mode count is the source of the Bekenstein-Hawking area law (§36 below, Theorem 34).*

*Proof.* (MS1)–(MS3) follow from standard Schwarzschild mode analysis combined with the McGucken identification of $dx₄/dτ = ic\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ at radius r. Specifically:

*(MS1).* The Schwarzschild metric (Theorem 31, rigorized as Theorem 31$'$ in Appendix F §61) has $g_{tt} = -c^2(1 - r_s/r)$, vanishing at $r = r_s$. The null condition $g_{μν} u^μ u^ν = 0$ for a tangent vector $u^μ$ at $r = r_s$ with $u^r = 0$ (purely angular) reduces to $r_s^2(\dotθ^2 + \sin^2θ  \dotφ^2) = 0$ only for trivial $u^μ = 0$; non-trivial horizon-tangent null geodesics have $u^t ≠ 0$ and $u^φ ≠ 0$ (or $u^θ$) with the constraint $r_s^2(\dotθ^2 + \sin^2θ  \dotφ^2) = 0$ holding in the limit, which forces these geodesics to be the generators of the horizon two-sphere as a null hypersurface. In the McGucken-Sphere reading, these are the surface generators of the McGucken Sphere at horizon events: the Sphere wavefronts whose $x₄$-advance is suppressed to zero by $dx₄/dτ = ic\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}|_{r = r_s} = 0$, leaving the wavefront propagating tangentially along the horizon at the spatial light speed c. The "photonic surface" character is the content of the horizon being the locus where the McGucken-Sphere wavefronts have zero $x₄$-advance (Definition 16, $x₄$-stationary surface).

*(MS2).* Outgoing null geodesics from $r = r_{emit} > r_s$ to infinity carry photon four-momentum with frequency $\omega_{emit}$ at emission and frequency $\omega_∞$ at infinity. The gravitational redshift formula $\omega_∞ = \omega_{emit}\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_{emit}}$ (standard GR result; e.g., Wald 1984 §6.3) is the integrated $x₄$-advance suppression: a photon emitted with proper-frequency $\omega_{emit}$ on the local McGucken-Sphere at $r_{emit}$ has $dx₄/dτ$-advance suppressed by $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_{emit}}$ relative to flat spacetime, and the integrated suppression along the outgoing geodesic to infinity produces the observed redshift. At $r_{emit} → r_s^+$, the redshift factor $\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_{emit}} → 0$, and the outgoing mode's frequency at infinity vanishes — the source of the "infinite redshift" at the horizon for stationary observers.

*(MS3).* Symmetric to (MS2): ingoing null geodesics from infinity to $r = r_{abs} > r_s$ undergo gravitational blueshift in the local frame at $r_{abs}$, with frequency ratio $\omega_{abs}/\omega_∞ = 1/\sqrt{1 - r_s/r_{abs}}$. The ingoing modes terminate at the horizon ($r → r_s^+$) by being absorbed into the gravitationally-trapped interior Sphere content (Theorem 33 IT1–IT3 below): no null geodesic from outside can cross the horizon and return.

*(MS4).* The number of $x₄$-stationary modes on the horizon two-sphere is computed by counting the field-theoretic modes whose wavefronts on the McGucken Sphere at horizon events have $dx₄/dτ = 0$. By Theorem 30 of [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime] (Holographic Area Law derived from dx₄/dt = ic via the $x₄$-stationary mode count on closed two-surfaces), the number of such modes scales as the area of the surface in Planck units:

$$N_{\rm modes}  =  \frac{A}{\ell_P^2},        \ell_P^2 = \frac{Gℏ}{c^3}.$$

The reason: each mode occupies a Planck-area cell on the surface, because the Compton wavelength of the field at the $x₄$-stationary regime is set by the Planck scale $\ell_P$ via the Compton-frequency identification $\omega_C = mc^2/ℏ$ saturating at the horizon. Applied to the horizon area $A_H = 4π r_s^2$, this gives $N_{\rm modes} = 4π r_s^2/\ell_P^2$. The detailed mode-counting derivation, including the Compton-phase content and the McGucken-Sphere wavefront structure at the horizon, is in [37: MG-Hawking] §§3–4 and [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Theorem 30]. ∎

**Theorem 33 (Interior as Gravitationally-Trapped Sphere Region).** *In the black-hole interior ($r < r_s$), the McGucken Spheres generated at every interior event are gravitationally trapped:*

*(IT1) **Forward null cones tilt inward.* Every event q in the interior generates a Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ whose forward null cone is, by the interior Schwarzschild causal structure, confined to the interior. No null geodesic from q can reach the horizon outward.

*(IT2) **Recursive entrapment.* Every Sphere point on $\Sigma_+(q)$ is itself a McGucken Point whose own Sphere is also gravitationally trapped. The recursive Sphere structure (Theorem 5) is preserved, but every Sphere in the recursion is confined to the interior.

*(IT3) **Convergence onto singularity.* The integrated geometric content of all trapped Spheres converges, as $r → 0$, onto the central singularity. The mathematical singularity at $r = 0$ is the limit of the recursive trapping.

*(IT4) **Information character.* The information carried by infalling matter is, in Channel A (algebraic-symmetry reading), preserved by the unitary evolution of the joint quantum state under the Schrödinger equation (Theorem 14(i)) extended to curved spacetime. In Channel B (geometric-propagation reading), the operational accessibility of this information to an external observer is destroyed at the horizon by the gravitational trapping of the interior Sphere content.

*The dual-channel reading of the information content is the foundation for the dual-channel resolution of the Hawking information paradox in §39 below (Theorem 37).*

*Proof.* The interior of the Schwarzschild geometry ($r < r_s$) has metric

$$ds^2  =  -c^2(1 - r_s/r)  dt^2 + (1 - r_s/r)^{-1}  dr^2 + r^2  dΩ^2,$$

derived from dx₄/dt = ic via Theorem 12 and the Schwarzschild solution (Theorem 31, rigorized as Theorem 31$'$ in Appendix F §61). For $r < r_s$, the coefficient $1 - r_s/r < 0$, so $g_{tt} > 0$ and $g_{rr} < 0$: t becomes spacelike and r becomes timelike. The future-directed timelike direction in the interior is $-r$ (decreasing r), and the future light cone tilts toward $r = 0$.

For (IT1): Let $q = (t_q, r_q, \theta_q, \phi_q)$ be an interior event with $r_q < r_s$. The forward null cone from q satisfies the null condition $g_{μν} u^μ u^ν = 0$, which (in interior Schwarzschild coordinates) gives $u^r < 0$ for future-directed null rays — every future-pointing null geodesic from q has $r$ decreasing. By the standard interior Penrose diagram (e.g., Hawking-Ellis 1973 §5.5; MTW 1973 §31), all future-directed timelike and null geodesics from any interior event reach the central singularity $r = 0$ in finite proper time without ever crossing back through $r = r_s$ outward. In McGucken language, the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ at apex q is the forward null cone of q, which by the interior causal structure is confined to the interior region $\{r < r_s\}$. No Sphere wavefront from an interior event can reach the horizon outward.

For (IT2): By Theorem 5 (self-replication of the McGucken Sphere), every point $q' ∈ \Sigma_+(q)$ is itself a McGucken Point with its own pointwise operator $\mathcal F_{q'}$ and Sphere $\Sigma_+(q')$ (the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic applies pointwise at every event of $𝒞_M$, including interior events). For every interior $q'$, by (IT1), $\Sigma_+(q')$ is itself gravitationally confined to the interior. The recursive Sphere generation of Theorem 5 therefore preserves the trapping at every layer of recursion: every Sphere in the recursion descending from $\Sigma_+(q)$ is confined to the interior.

For (IT3): The interior Schwarzschild geometry's future-pointing congruence focuses onto the spacelike singularity at $r = 0$. By the Raychaudhuri focusing theorem for timelike congruences in the strong-energy-condition regime (Hawking-Ellis 1973 §4.4) — and equivalently by direct integration of the radial geodesic equation in the interior Schwarzschild coordinates — every interior timelike geodesic reaches $r = 0$ in finite proper time. ## §36. Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy from $x₄$-Stationary Mode Count

The Bekenstein-Hawking area law

$$S_{\rm BH}  =  \frac{k_B A_H}{4 \ell_P^2}$$

**Theorem 34 (Bekenstein-Hawking Entropy from McGucken Sphere; restated and elaborated from [35: MG-Bekenstein]).** *The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of a black-hole horizon at $r = r_s$ is*

$$S_{\rm BH}  =  k_B · N_{\rm modes} · \frac{1}{4}  =  \frac{k_B A_H}{4 \ell_P^2},$$

*where $N_{\rm modes} = A_H/\ell_P^2$ is the number of $x₄$-stationary modes piercing the horizon (Theorem 32, MS4), $k_B$ is Boltzmann's constant, and the factor of 1/4 arises from the McGucken–Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ applied to the Schwarzschild metric via the on-shell Euclidean Gibbons-Hawking-York action (Theorem 36$'$ in Appendix G §62 — the corrected derivation replacing the retracted Theorem 36 of §38).*

The 1/4 factor in the Bekenstein-Hawking formula is established by the on-shell Euclidean action method of Gibbons-Hawking 1977 applied to the McGucken-Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ of the Schwarzschild metric. (ii) The on-shell Euclidean Gibbons-Hawking-York boundary action evaluates to $I_E = β M c^2/2 = 2π r_s M c$ (units of action), the factor of $1/2$ arising from the renormalised GHY boundary integral.

(iii) The thermodynamic relation $S/k_B = (β⟨ H⟩ - I_E)/ℏ = (β Mc^2 - β Mc^2/2)/ℏ = β Mc^2/(2ℏ) = 2π r_s Mc/ℏ$, with $β = 4π r_s/c$ in time units.

## §37. The Hawking Temperature from the Euclidean Cigar

The Hawking temperature

$$T_H  =  \frac{ℏ c^3}{8π G M k_B}  =  \frac{ℏ c}{4π r_s k_B}$$

is the temperature of the Hawking radiation emitted by a Schwarzschild black hole of mass M. Hawking's 1974 derivation proceeded via QFT on the Schwarzschild background, with the Bogoliubov transformation between the asymptotic-future and asymptotic-past mode bases yielding the thermal spectrum.

A cleaner derivation proceeds via the Euclidean cigar geometry: the Schwarzschild metric, Wick-rotated to imaginary time $\tau_E = it$, becomes a Euclidean-signature manifold whose smooth-extension requires periodic identification of $\tau_E$ with period $β = 1/(k_B T_H)$. The smoothness condition fixes the temperature uniquely.

**Theorem 35 (Hawking Temperature from Euclidean Cigar; restated from [23: MG-Thermodynamics, Theorem 16]; rooted in McGucken-Wick rotation).** *The Hawking temperature of a Schwarzschild black hole is*

$$T_H  =  \frac{ℏ \kappa}{2π c k_B},        \kappa = \frac{c^2}{2 r_s} = \frac{c^4}{4 G M},$$

*where $\kappa$ is the surface gravity at the horizon. The derivation proceeds via the McGucken–Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ applied to the Schwarzschild metric, yielding the Euclidean cigar geometry near the horizon. The smoothness condition at the cigar tip ($ρ = 0$ in cigar coordinates) requires the periodic identification $\tau_E ~ \tau_E + β$ with $β = 2π/\kappa$, giving $T_H = 1/(k_B β) = \kappa/(2π k_B)$ (in natural units; restoring $ℏ c$ gives $T_H = ℏ \kappa/(2π c k_B)$).*

*Proof sketch (full rigorous proof: Appendix H, §63, Theorem 35$'$).* Apply the McGucken–Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ to the Schwarzschild metric: in the Schwarzschild coordinates $(t, r, θ, φ)$, the substitution $t → -i\tau_E$ converts $g_{tt} = -c^2(1 - r_s/r)$ to $g_{ττ} = c^2(1 - r_s/r)$, making the metric positive-definite (Euclidean signature). Near the horizon, expand in $ρ = \sqrt{4 r_s (r - r_s)}$ and the angular variable $\phi_E = (c/2 r_s) \tau_E$: the metric becomes

$$ds_E^2 ≈ dρ^2 + ρ^2  d\phi_E^2 + r_s^2  d\Omega_2^2,$$

which is the metric of a two-dimensional Euclidean plane (the $ρ$-$\phi_E$ plane, the "cigar tip") times the horizon two-sphere. Smoothness at $ρ = 0$ requires $\phi_E$ to have period $2π$, which gives $\tau_E$ period $4π r_s/c = 2π/\kappa$. The inverse-temperature is $β = 2π/\kappa$, so $T_H = 1/(k_B β) = \kappa/(2π k_B)$ (in natural units; standard restoration gives $T_H = ℏ \kappa/(2π c k_B)$).

The McGucken reading is that the Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ is *not* a formal operation imposed externally; it is a coordinate change on the real four-dimensional Euclidean manifold whose existence is forced by dx₄/dt = ic (the active expansion's $x₄$-coordinate $x₄ = ict$ becomes Euclidean time $τ$ under the change of variables). The Hawking temperature is the temperature of the McGucken-Sphere content at the horizon, with the periodic identification arising from the $x₄$-stationary structure of the horizon. ∎

**Corollary 35a (Surface gravity as $x₄$-suppression rate).** *The surface gravity $\kappa$ at the horizon has the reading: $\kappa$ measures the rate at which $g_{tt}$ — equivalently, the gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ = ic\sqrt{1 - r_s/r}$ — varies in the radial direction at the horizon. Specifically, for the Schwarzschild geometry with timelike Killing vector $χ^a = (\partial_t)^a$ of norm $χ^a \chi_a = g_{tt} = -c^2(1 - r_s/r)$, the surface gravity in SI acceleration units is*

$$\kappa_{SI}  =  \frac{1}{2}\left|\frac{d(-g_{tt})}{dr}\right|_{r = r_s}  =  \frac{1}{2}\left|\frac{d}{dr}\Bigl[c^2(1 - r_s/r)\Bigr]\right|_{r=r_s}  =  \frac{1}{2}·\frac{c^2 r_s}{r^2}\bigg|_{r=r_s}  =  \frac{c^2}{2 r_s}  =  \frac{c^4}{4 GM},$$

*equivalent to the inverse-time scale $\tilde\kappa = \kappa_{SI}/c = c/(2r_s)$ used in the Euclidean-period analysis (Appendix H §63). The Hawking temperature is the rate at which the $x₄$-stationary content of the horizon thermalises with the exterior under the Euclidean periodicity, $T_H = ℏ\kappa_{SI}/(2π c k_B) = ℏ\tilde\kappa/(2π k_B)$.*

**Corollary 35b (Unruh temperature from McGucken-Wick rotation).** *The Unruh temperature for a uniformly accelerated observer in flat spacetime, $T_U = ℏ a/(2π c k_B)$, is derived by the same McGucken–Wick mechanism applied to the Rindler wedge. ## §39. The Hawking Information Paradox: Dual-Channel Resolution

The Hawking information paradox is the deepest dispute in the post-1976 black-hole literature. Hawking's 1976 claim — that the formation and evaporation of a black hole results in the operational destruction of the quantum information carried by the infalling matter, observable as the thermal (mixed) state of the outgoing Hawking radiation — directly contradicts the orthodox unitarity axiom A3 of Susskind's program. The thirty-year Black Hole War was the defense of A3 against Hawking's claim. The McGucken framework supplies the dual-channel resolution: both sides held part of the truth; the dispute was a half-equation engagement; the full resolution requires the dual reading of dx₄/dt = ic in both channels simultaneously.

**Theorem 37 (Hawking Information Paradox: Dual-Channel Resolution).** *The Hawking information paradox is resolved by the dual-channel reading of dx₄/dt = ic applied to the black-hole evaporation process:*

*(IR1) **Channel A** (algebraic-symmetry reading): The full quantum state of the joint system [infalling matter + Hawking radiation + ambient spacetime] evolves unitarily under the Schrödinger equation (Theorem 14(i)) extended to curved spacetime. The Hilbert-space unitarity U(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ) is preserved exactly. Susskind's A3 is correct in Channel A.*

*(IR2) **Channel B** (geometric-propagation reading): The operational accessibility of the infalling information to an external observer is strictly reduced at the horizon by the gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ (Definition 15). Information carried by infalling matter becomes gravitationally trapped in the interior (Theorem 33, IT4); the Hawking radiation emitted to infinity carries thermal spectral content (Theorem 35) that, for the external observer, is operationally distinguishable from the unitary content of the infalling state. The operational information accessible to the external observer is operationally destroyed at the horizon. Hawking's 1976 claim is correct in Channel B.*

*(IR3) **The two channels operate simultaneously.* dx₄/dt = ic carries both channels at every event by the Dual-Channel Theorem (Theorem 16). The two readings are two projections of the same physical mechanism at the horizon. The thirty-year Black Hole War — which posed the two channels as mutually exclusive — was a half-equation engagement.*

*(IR4) **The dual-channel reading is the fact, not a compromise.* The McGucken framework does not "compromise" between Susskind and Hawking by partially agreeing with each. The framework supplies the fact that both channels are correct, simultaneously, because the world reads both channels at every event. The thirty-year war's mistake was not on either side; it was on both sides agreeing that one channel had to win.*

*Proof.* (IR1) follows from Theorem 14(i): the Schrödinger equation is derived from dx₄/dt = ic via the Channel-A reading, with the unitary group U(t) = exp(−iĤt/ℏ) as the algebraic generator. Extension to curved spacetime preserves the unitarity at the level of the full joint state; the full state of the system [infalling matter + Hawking radiation + ambient spacetime] is unitary throughout the evaporation process.

(IR2) follows from Theorem 33(IT4) combined with the horizon's $x₄$-stationary character (Definition 16): the operational accessibility of the infalling information to the external observer requires that the information be encoded in modes accessible to the external observer. By the gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ at the horizon, the modes carrying the infalling information are trapped in the interior; only the thermal Hawking radiation reaches the external observer. The thermal spectrum (Theorem 35) carries no operational information about the infalling state's specific microstructure; the operational accessibility of the infalling information at the external observer is therefore destroyed.

(IR3) follows from the Dual-Channel Theorem (Theorem 16): dx₄/dt = ic admits both readings simultaneously. The horizon process therefore reads in both channels: Channel A preserves the joint unitary state; Channel B destroys the operational information accessible to the external observer. Both readings are correct simultaneously.

(IR4) is a philosophical clarification: the dual-channel framework is the fact about how dx₄/dt = ic operates, not a compromise position negotiated between two contending parties. The orthodox framing of the dispute as "either Hawking or Susskind" was a error of the framing, not of either physicist. The rhetorical mechanism that produced the framing was the Cheerleader Move (Theorem 3): A3 was installed as a axiom by repeated declaration without derivation, so any operational challenge to A3 became an attack on the axiomatic foundation, and Susskind's program could not engage Hawking's claim at the level (because there was no level beneath A3 within the program). Hawking's 1976 claim was a empirical observation about Channel B that could not be engaged within a program committed to Channel A as the axiom. ## §40. The Gravitational Path Integral Knows More: Honoring Daniel Harlow's Call for a Deeper Foundation

In the Sean Carroll *Mindscape* podcast episode 349 (March 30, 2026, *Daniel Harlow on What Quantum Gravity Teaches Us About Quantum Mechanics*), Daniel Harlow — Susskind's Stanford PhD student, now Associate Professor of Physics at MIT, Packard Fellow, and New Horizons in Physics Prize laureate — articulates with rare candor a asymmetry that the orthodox program has identified without explaining. The candor is heroic; the call for a deeper foundation is the opening this paper exists to honor. This chapter identifies the source of the asymmetry as the dual-channel architecture of dx₄/dt = ic, applies the existing Dual-Channel Theorem (Theorem 16, §24) to the gravitational path integral, and supplies the deeper foundation Harlow has explicitly requested.

### §40.1 The three concentrated quotes that name the asymmetry

**(H1) At 30:05 of the podcast** — the admission:

> *"In ordinary quantum mechanics, these approaches are equivalent. There's no big mystery. You can pick either one and use it. … But in gravity, the situation is more mysterious, because in gravity, the path integral approach is not something that you can derive from the really big matrix approach. … It's somehow stronger. It knows things that the canonical approach doesn't know. For example, it knows the number of degrees of freedom of a black hole."*

**(H2) At 30:55** — the Gibbons–Hawking 1977 example:

> *"By using the path integral approach to gravity, just summing over all the geometries to get from the initial state to the final state, if you sum over it in the way that seems most natural, it actually knows how many states the black hole has, even though if you tried to actually count those states by going to the canonical formalism, it wouldn't work."*

**(H3) At 35:30** — the entropy admission:

> *"In ordinary statistical mechanics, if you want to know the entropy of an ideal gas, you have to count the states. … But somehow the gravitational path integral knows the entropy of a black hole without doing any state counting. It just tells you, 'Here's the answer.' And the answer is correct."*

Harlow then likens the path integral to the Oracle at Delphi (32:00–34:19) — correct answers without comprehensible derivation, with the lesson at risk of misinterpretation — and admits at 34:42:

> *"I'm always wanting something that's more fundamental from which I can realize the consequences of the path integral rather than sort of having it be the end of the story."*

**The orthodox program has identified a asymmetry it cannot explain.** In quantum mechanics without gravity, canonical and path-integral formalisms are mathematically equivalent — the Trotter product formula (Reed–Simon, *Methods of Modern Mathematical Physics*, Vol. II, Theorem VIII.31) is the standard rigorous derivation. In gravity they are not. The path integral knows more. The orthodox question — *why?* — has no answer within the orthodox framework. **The McGucken framework answers it in one line: because the path integral is the Channel-B reading, the canonical formalism is the Channel-A reading, and gravity is the regime in which the dual-channel architecture of dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 16 (Dual-Channel Theorem, §24)) becomes empirically inequivalent because the spacetime metric is itself in dynamical play.**

This section develops that answer by direct application of Theorem 16 and the existing corpus theorems on which it depends. No new theorems are introduced in this chapter; the identification is an application of the existing corpus.

It is the Channel-A reading of the same physics in the operator-algebra vocabulary.

These are not two independent theorems. They are one application of Theorem 16 to two formalisms used in physics. The path-integral formalism reads Channel B; the canonical formalism reads Channel A; both readings exist simultaneously at every event by Theorem 16; in non-gravitational settings the readings produce numerically equivalent matrix elements (by the standard Trotter product derivation that connects the two formalisms in the absence of dynamical gravity).

### §40.3 Why the two formalisms are equivalent without gravity (the H1 part of Harlow's observation)

When the spacetime metric $g_{μν}$ is fixed and non-dynamical — equal to the Minkowski metric $\eta_{μν}$ throughout, with no metric perturbations sourced by matter content — the canonical and path-integral formalisms produce numerically identical matrix elements. This is the standard fact that Harlow describes at 30:05: *"in ordinary quantum mechanics, these approaches are equivalent."*

The rigorous statement is the Trotter product formula. Let $\hat H$ be a self-adjoint Hamiltonian on Hilbert space $ℋ$, bounded below, with $\hat H = \hat T + \hat V$ where $\hat T = \hat p^2/(2m)$ and $\hat V = V(\hat q)$. Then for $t > 0$ and $N → ∞$:
$$⟨ q_f \mid e^{-i\hat H t/ℏ} \mid q_i ⟩  =  \lim_{N→∞} \prod_{k=1}^{N-1} \int dq_k \prod_{k=0}^{N-1} ⟨ q_{k+1} \mid e^{-i\hat T Δ t/ℏ} e^{-i\hat V Δ t/ℏ} \mid q_k ⟩,$$
where $Δ t = t/N$, $q_0 = q_i$, $q_N = q_f$. The right-hand side, in the continuum limit, is the Feynman path integral
$$\int_{q(0)=q_i}^{q(t)=q_f} \mathcal D[q]   \exp\!\left(\frac{i}{ℏ} \int_0^t L(q, \dot q)   dt'\right),$$
with $L = m\dot q^2/2 - V(q)$ the Lagrangian, obtained from the time-sliced product by Gaussian integration on each slice. The derivation is rigorous on bounded operators (Reed–Simon, Vol. II, Theorem VIII.31) and extends by quadratic-form methods to a wide class of $\hat H$.

the equivalence is the content of Theorem 16 specialised to the case where the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at every event $p$ is the same Sphere — that is, where the spacetime metric is the fixed Minkowski metric and the Sphere structure is kinematically given rather than dynamically responsive. In that regime, the Channel-B geometric content (the Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at each $p$) is the same content the Channel-A operator algebra already reads (the fixed unitary group on fixed Hilbert space); the two readings see the same physics from two sides and produce numerically equivalent matrix elements. There is no extra content in the Channel-B reading on non-dynamical background, which is why the path integral "knows" only what the canonical formalism already knows when gravity is absent.
