## §41. ER = EPR as Forced Theorem

The ER = EPR conjecture of Maldacena and Susskind 2013 proposes that Einstein-Rosen (ER) wormholes are dual to Einstein-Podolsky-Rosen (EPR) entanglement: every entangled pair of quantum systems is connected by a (possibly Planck-scale) wormhole, and every traversable-in-the-classical-sense wormhole is the holographic dual of a maximally entangled state. The conjecture is presented in the orthodox program as a deep insight about the connection between geometry (ER) and quantum information (EPR). The McGucken framework recovers ER = EPR as a forced theorem of shared Sphere history: every entangled pair shares a McGucken Sphere from a past apex (Theorem 20), and every wormhole connection between regions of spacetime is the signature of shared Sphere apices in the joint causal past.

**Theorem 38 (ER = EPR as Forced Theorem; restated and elaborated from [36: MG-EmergentSpacetime, Theorem 33]).** *Let A and B be two systems connected by quantum entanglement (i.e., sharing a joint state $|\psi_{AB}⟩$ that does not factorise). By the Entanglement Propagation Theorem (Theorem 20), A and B share a McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ from a past apex event q at which the entangling interaction occurred. Equivalently, A and B are connected by an Einstein-Rosen "wormhole" (in the orthodox ER language) whose identity in the McGucken framework is the shared Sphere from q. The ER=EPR identification is therefore not a conjecture; it is a forced theorem of dx₄/dt = ic.*

*Specifically:*

*(EE1) The "wormhole throat" of the ER bridge is the past apex event q.*

*(EE2) The "wormhole mouths" at the two ends are the present locations of A and B.*

*(EE3) The "wormhole connection" between the mouths is the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ in its entirety, regarded as the geometric carrier of the joint state.*

*(EE4) The "wormhole" is the McGucken Sphere from q regarded under the "wormhole" reading — no separate geometric structure superimposed on the McGucken spacetime $ℳ_G$.*

*(EE5) The non-traversability of the wormhole (the no-signaling content of EPR; Theorem 26) corresponds to the Sphere's marginal-independence theorem: no signal can be transmitted from one mouth to the other via the Sphere, because the marginal statistics at each mouth are independent of measurements at the other mouth.*

*Proof.* Direct combination of Theorem 20 (entanglement propagation via shared Sphere) and Theorem 26 (no-signaling). The orthodox ER language describes the Einstein-Rosen bridge as a topological connection between two regions of spacetime; the McGucken reading identifies this topological connection with the past-apex Sphere from q. The two descriptions are not equivalent in form but coincide in content: both describe the same shared past origin of the joint state, with the McGucken framework supplying the explicit geometric mechanism (the Sphere from q) and the orthodox framework using the topological "wormhole" metaphor.

(EE1)–(EE5) follow by direct identification of the orthodox wormhole language with the McGucken-Sphere identity. The wormhole "throat" is the past apex (the most recent time at which A and B were spatially coincident at q). The wormhole "mouths" are the present locations of A and B. The wormhole "connection" is the shared Sphere. The non-traversability is no-signaling. ∎

**Corollary 38a (Susskind's A4 recovered as theorem).** *Susskind's claim A4, "ER = EPR," is recovered as a derived consequence of dx₄/dt = ic via the Entanglement Propagation Theorem and the shared-Sphere identification. A4 is therefore a theorem of the McGucken framework, not a conjecture. The orthodox Maldacena-Susskind 2013 presentation of A4 as a "deep insight" is correct; the McGucken framework supplies the mechanism beneath the insight.*

**Corollary 38b (ER = EPR is a theorem of shared apex events, not a conjecture about topology).** *The ER=EPR identification does not require the existence of topologically non-trivial wormhole geometries (which are difficult to realise in standard GR — non-traversable wormholes require negative-energy stress-tensor sources). The McGucken-Sphere reading does not require any topological non-triviality; the "wormhole" is the past-apex Sphere, which is a standard forward null cone with completely standard topology. The "wormhole" language is a useful metaphor in the orthodox program; the McGucken framework supplies the geometric content beneath the metaphor — the shared past Sphere apex — without requiring the metaphor's topological literalism.*

**Corollary 38c (Maldacena-Susskind 2013 elevation of conjecture to insight).** *The ER=EPR identification has been elevated, in the orthodox program, from conjecture to "insight" by repeated declaration. The McGucken framework's recovery of A4 as a forced theorem of dx₄/dt = ic is the confirmation that the orthodox elevation was correct in its conclusion (A4 is true) and incorrect in its method (A4 was not derived; it was declared). ## §42. The AMPS Firewall Paradox Dissolved Without Monogamy Violation

The AMPS (Almheiri-Marolf-Polchinski-Sully) 2012 firewall paradox is the deepest internal-consistency crisis of the orthodox black-hole program. AMPS argued that the joint requirements of (i) unitary black-hole evaporation (Susskind A3); (ii) the equivalence principle (the infalling observer sees nothing special at the horizon); (iii) the monogamy of entanglement (the Hawking radiation in the late stage cannot be maximally entangled with both the early radiation and the modes just behind the horizon) are mutually inconsistent. One must give up at least one. AMPS proposed giving up the equivalence principle (a "firewall" of high-energy quanta at the horizon); subsequent proposals have variously given up monogamy, locality, or other premises. The orthodox program has not resolved the AMPS paradox in a way that satisfies all parties. The McGucken framework dissolves the paradox by recognising that the orthodox framing involves a Channel-A-only reading of three claims that have dual-channel structure.

**Theorem 39 (AMPS Firewall Paradox Dissolved by Dual-Channel Reading).** *The AMPS firewall paradox is dissolved in the McGucken framework by the following dual-channel analysis:*

*(AF1) **Susskind's A3 (unitarity) is Channel-A content.* The full joint state evolves unitarily by Theorem 14(i). This Channel-A content is preserved without modification.*

*(AF2) **The equivalence principle is Channel-B content.* The infalling observer's experience of "nothing special at the horizon" is the Channel-B operational content: locally, the infalling observer's local frame is freely falling and sees no curvature singularity at the horizon. This is the form of the equivalence principle in dx₄/dt = ic, where the freely-falling frame at the horizon experiences no anomalous local effects.*

*(AF3) **Monogamy of entanglement is Channel-A algebraic content.* The monogamy theorem is the algebraic fact that a maximally entangled pair cannot be jointly maximally entangled with a third system. This is Channel A content (algebraic-symmetry reading).*

*(AF4) **The "inconsistency" of (AF1) + (AF2) + (AF3) arises from forcing all three into Channel A.* If the equivalence principle (AF2) is read in Channel A — i.e., as an algebraic statement about the joint state — then it conflicts with (AF1) and (AF3). If, however, (AF2) is read in Channel B as the operational statement about the infalling observer's freely-falling experience, then the conflict dissolves: Channel A unitarity (AF1) is preserved, the operational equivalence principle (AF2) is preserved in Channel B, and the monogamy theorem (AF3) is preserved in Channel A. No firewall is required; no premise needs to be given up.*

*(AF5) **The rhetorical reading: AMPS conducted the analysis within Channel A vocabulary.* The orthodox framing of AMPS as a paradox was a Channel-A-only reading. The McGucken dual-channel reading recognises that AMPS's three premises operate in different channels, and the apparent inconsistency was a rhetorical artifact of the single-channel vocabulary.*

*Proof.* (AF1)–(AF3) restate the three AMPS premises with the McGucken channel identification.

(AF4): The orthodox derivation of the AMPS inconsistency proceeds by treating all three premises as Channel A statements about the joint Hilbert-space state. The monogamy theorem then forces a contradiction: the Hawking radiation cannot be unitary-entangled with both the early radiation (Page-curve content, Channel A) and the modes just behind the horizon (equivalence-principle content, when read in Channel A as "the joint state at the horizon has standard QFT vacuum structure"). The contradiction arises from forcing the equivalence-principle content into Channel A.

When the equivalence-principle content is read in Channel B — as the operational statement about the infalling observer's local freely-falling frame, without claiming algebraic entanglement structure with the bulk Hilbert-space state — the contradiction dissolves. The infalling observer experiences nothing special at the horizon (Channel B operational content); the joint state evolves unitarily (Channel A algebraic content); the monogamy theorem holds (Channel A algebraic content). (AF5): The rhetorical reading is that AMPS was operating within the Channel-A vocabulary the orthodox program supplies. The dual-channel reading the McGucken framework supplies dissolves the apparent inconsistency by recognising that the equivalence principle is a Channel-B claim and need not be (in fact, cannot be) algebraically forced into the Channel-A monogamy structure. The firewall is not required; no monogamy violation is required; the AMPS paradox was a Channel-A-only artifact of the orthodox vocabulary. ∎

**Corollary 39a (No firewall in McGucken framework).** *The infalling observer at the horizon experiences nothing special — no firewall of high-energy quanta — by the Channel-B operational reading of the equivalence principle. The reading is that the horizon is an $x₄$-stationary surface in the Schwarzschild frame but is locally a freely-falling region in the infalling frame; both readings are correct, and the infalling observer's frame is well-defined and freely falling at the horizon.*

**Corollary 39b (Monogamy is preserved as Channel A theorem).** *The monogamy theorem is preserved without modification in the McGucken framework: it is a Channel A algebraic-theorem of the joint Hilbert-space state, and Channel A unitarity is preserved exactly by Theorem 14(i) extended to curved spacetime.*

### §43.1 The closed-universe one-state pathology Harlow identifies, and the McGucken-framework response

In the same *Mindscape* podcast (episode 349, March 30 2026), beginning at approximately 44:43, Harlow develops a deeply candid concession that the orthodox holographic principle, when applied to a closed universe with no spatial boundary, returns the answer that the universe has **only one quantum state**. Harlow's exact words (45:36–47:30, edited for compression):

> *"The fundamental degrees of freedom live at the spatial boundary. If there's no spatial boundary, there's no fundamental degrees of freedom… we have all these ways of doing calculations now about black holes, and they all back up that argument. They quantitatively tell you, 'Yep, yeah, indeed, that's what's going on'… How does the richness of human experience fit into a theory with zero degrees of freedom? I mean, that's the real question."*

At 48:30 Harlow continues:

> *"There are zero — what else could it have been? Zero or infinity, those are the answers."*

At 50:46 Harlow articulates his proposed orthodox-program resolution: hit the observer with a decohering channel of size $e^{-S_{\rm obs}}$, allowing effective field theory to emerge approximately, accepting that all of physics is therefore only correct up to errors of order $e^{-S_{\rm obs}}$:

> *"The observer should semi-classically have some finite number of degrees of freedom and they can do physics up to e to the minus that number of degrees of freedom… science as a concept is approximate with a lower bound on the error given by e to the minus the entropy of the observer."*

This is, in the McGucken framework's diagnostic vocabulary, a **Localisation Move at the cosmological tier** (Theorem 2 of Part I). The orthodox program imports a non-unitary effect (a decohering channel on the observer's state) into the dynamics while continuing to call the dynamics unitary, because the Channel-B reading of where holographic content actually lives is not in the orthodox vocabulary. The deformation is the signature that the Channel-A-only reading of holography has broken down at the cosmological scale.

The McGucken framework offers a response that does not require deforming quantum mechanics. The response is *not* a new theorem; it is the recognition that the orthodox closed-universe one-state result is the consequence of a particular axiom (the boundary-of-space form of holography, declared by 't Hooft 1993 / Susskind 1995 without derivation) which the McGucken framework does not adopt. The McGucken framework instead has a theorem (Theorem 19 (*Huygens = Holography*, §25)) that derives holography from dx₄/dt = ic via the McGucken Sphere recursion, and the theorem-derived form of holography is different from the axiom-declared form.

**response to Harlow's closed-universe pathology.**

*(R1) The pathology has a definite source.* The orthodox holographic principle, as declared by 't Hooft 1993 and Susskind 1995, states that the fundamental degrees of freedom of any region of spacetime live on the spatial boundary of that region. This is an axiom — installed by declaration without derivation from a deeper physical principle (the Cheerleader Move, Theorem 3 of Part I). When applied to a closed universe (no spatial boundary), the axiom returns the answer that there are no fundamental degrees of freedom, and the orthodox program responds either by treating the closed universe as a one-dimensional Hilbert space (the result Harlow describes) or by introducing a non-unitary modification of the dynamics (Harlow's $e^{-S_{\rm obs}}$ proposal). The pathology is a consequence of the axiom plus the geometric situation.

*(R2) The McGucken framework does not use the boundary-of-space form of holography.* Theorem 19 (*Huygens = Holography*, §25) derives holography from dx₄/dt = ic by the following identification: the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p)$ at every event $p$ has a two-dimensional surface, and the wavefront content carried on that surface encodes the geometric-propagation content of the active expansion from $p$. The "holographic" identification is between the bulk Sphere expansion and its surface inscription, with the Sphere surface being the screen. This is a theorem; it descends from dx₄/dt = ic via Theorem 11 (Huygens self-replication) and Theorem 16 (Dual-Channel reading). The boundary-of-space form is one specific reading of this theorem in geometries that have a spatial boundary (AdS, asymptotically flat); the cosmological Sphere reading (Theorem 40 (Cosmological Holography, §43), §43 above) is the corresponding reading in cosmological geometries that have no spatial boundary.

*(R3) The cosmological McGucken Sphere supplies the screen Harlow's analysis cannot find.* Theorem 40 (Cosmological Holography, §43) identifies the cosmological McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_{\rm BB})$ — expanding from the Big Bang event at $+ic$ — as the universe's outermost holographic screen. The screen has a definite geometric structure (the cosmological Sphere surface) and a definite mode count (the Gibbons-Hawking de Sitter entropy $S_{dS} = k_B A_{dS}/(4\ell_P^2)$, derivable by the same horizon-mode-counting argument that gave Theorem 30 the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy). The pathology Harlow identifies — that orthodox holography gives "zero or infinity" for the closed-universe state count — does not arise here. The cosmological Sphere has a finite, computable surface area and a corresponding finite mode count derived geometrically.

*(R4) What this response does and does not claim.* It claims that the McGucken framework's theorem-derived holography (Theorem 19) does not produce the boundary-of-space pathology that Harlow's analysis identifies in orthodox holography. It claims that the cosmological McGucken Sphere supplies the holographic screen in the closed-universe case (Theorem 40). It claims that, by this mechanism, the McGucken framework does not need to introduce a non-unitary $e^{-S_{\rm obs}}$ decohering channel to recover effective field theory.

It does *not* claim, at this section's level of rigor, a derivation of the cosmological constant's empirical value from the cosmological Sphere mode count. It does not claim a calculation showing that the universe's matter content "fits" inside the de Sitter entropy budget. It does not claim that the cosmological-constant problem (the 120-orders-of-magnitude discrepancy between QFT vacuum-energy estimates and the observed $Λ$) is resolved. Those claims would require derivations that are not present in the standalone paper at the level needed to assert them here. What this section establishes is narrower: orthodox holography is axiom-declared and produces the closed-universe pathology by direct substitution; theorem-derived holography (Theorem 19) does not produce the pathology because the screen is the cosmological McGucken Sphere (Theorem 40), not the (nonexistent) spatial boundary.

**The heroism of Harlow's admission.** Harlow's 2026 candor in publicly naming the closed-universe one-state pathology is the most important concession the orthodox program has produced this decade. The orthodox program previously treated the cosmological extension of holography as a deep but soluble problem; the standard mode was to defend the holographic axiom against difficulties by Domain-Shifting (retreat from de Sitter to anti-de Sitter, where the program has empirical traction) or by Localisation (describe the difficulty as a feature of the setup rather than as a fact about the axiom). Harlow does neither in the Carroll interview. He admits the pathology, he wrestles with it openly, and he proposes a radical revision of quantum mechanics itself (the $e^{-S_{\rm obs}}$ decohering channel) to accommodate it. The proposed revision is, in the McGucken framework's vocabulary, a Localisation Move at the level — importing non-unitary content into the dynamics while calling the dynamics unitary. But Harlow's admission of the pathology that drives the move is itself heroic. This paper honors that admission and offers the response above: the pathology was the consequence of an axiom-declared holography, and a theorem-derived holography (Theorem 19 (*Huygens = Holography*, §25)) does not produce it, with the cosmological McGucken Sphere (Theorem 40) supplying the screen in geometries that have no spatial boundary.


## §43.5. Harlow's Three-Qutrit Code and the QEC Reading of AdS/CFT: Identification with the McGucken Sphere, and Five Surpluses *(new chapter)*

*This chapter takes as direct target Harlow's PiTP 2017 lecture* Holography and Quantum Error Correction *(YouTube videoID pv_GAc5A4HU, Princeton Institute for Theoretical Physics), the canonical exposition of the quantum-error-correction (QEC) reading of AdS/CFT [Almheiri–Dong–Harlow 2014, JHEP 04, 163; Harlow 2017, Lectures on QEC and AdS/CFT, arXiv:1607.03901; Pastawski–Yoshida–Harlow–Preskill 2015, JHEP 06, 149]. The chapter establishes the exact mapping between Harlow's three-qutrit code and the McGucken-Sphere three-region reconstruction (Theorem 40.5), identifies the HKLL smearing function as the Sphere kernel (Corollary 40.5a), identifies the code-subspace / orthogonal-complement division as the Wick-rotation cut between Channel A and Channel B (Corollary 40.5b), identifies the radial-commutativity puzzle as the Channel-A / Channel-B perpendicularity content (Corollary 40.5c), and states the five surpluses by which the McGucken framework supersedes Harlow's QEC framework (Corollary 40.5d). The chapter honors Daniel Harlow's heroic exposition of the QEC reading — the most candid and lucid statement of the operator-algebra approach to bulk reconstruction in the modern record — and supplies the geometric foundation beneath the operator-algebra content that Harlow's 2026 Mindscape admission [§40, §45 of the present paper; Mindscape 349, 34:42] explicitly identifies as what the orthodox program is reaching toward.*

### §43.5.1 What Harlow's Lecture Establishes

Harlow's PiTP 2017 lecture opens (0:30) with the question: *"How does spacetime emerge in AdS/CFT?"* and immediately qualifies it (1:38): *"Is there a black hole interior in AdS/CFT?"* The qualification is the rhetorical signature of the orthodox program operating without a principle for the bulk: the question of black-hole-interior existence is open in the orthodox framework because the bulk is reached only through the AdS/CFT boundary-to-bulk dictionary, and the dictionary's reach into the deep interior is the subject of the lecture.

The lecture's technical content runs through four moments.

**Moment 1: The HKLL smearing function $K(z, x; x')$ (20:50–47:00).** Harlow develops the Hamilton–Kabat–Lifschytz–Lowe (HKLL) reconstruction [Hamilton–Kabat–Lifschytz–Lowe 2006, *Phys. Rev. D* 74, 066009, arXiv:hep-th/0606141; Kabat–Lifschytz 2014, *JHEP* 06, 091, arXiv:1311.3020] of bulk fields as

$$Φ(z, x)  =  \int dx'  K(z, x; x')  \mathcal O(x'),$$

where $K(z, x; x')$ is the *smearing function* — *not* the bulk-to-boundary propagator [Harlow lecture 38:14: *"K is not the bulk-to-boundary propagator. Yeah, it's important that it's not"*]. The smearing function is a distributional object [Harlow lecture 55:21: *"It only makes sense when the thing you integrate against is actually a CFT operator. That's another one of those things for the mathematicians to sort out"*]. The AdS-Rindler reconstruction (41:11–47:00) supplies the same bulk operator with a different boundary support — the domain of dependence of half the boundary time slice, generalised to any ball-shaped boundary region by conformal transformation.

**Moment 2: The radial-commutativity puzzle (57:30–1:05:00).** Harlow states the puzzle [Harlow lecture 59:03]: a bulk operator $Φ(y)$ at a fixed bulk point $y$ must, on the AdS-Rindler reconstruction, *commute* with all local boundary operators on a Cauchy slice of the boundary (because the bulk point is spacelike-separated from each one in the bulk causal structure), yet the bulk operator must be non-trivial (the bulk-to-boundary map is an isomorphism). The orthodox quantum-field-theory time-slice axiom [Harlow lecture 1:00:14: *"any bounded local operator which commutes with all of the operators with support in an open set of a Cauchy slice has to be the identity"*] requires the bulk operator to be the identity, contradicting its non-triviality. The contradiction is the radial-commutativity puzzle.

**Moment 3: The three-region puzzle (1:06:08–1:09:01).** Harlow's most-illustrated diagram [Harlow lecture 1:06:14: *"this is the picture that I'm contractually obliged to draw on every talk that I give"*] partitions the boundary into three regions $R_1, R_2, R_3$. The bulk operator at the center is in the causal wedge of any *two* of the regions but not any *one*. The same bulk operator therefore admits *three different* boundary representations (on $R_1 ∪ R_2$, on $R_2 ∪ R_3$, on $R_1 ∪ R_3$), each obtained by AdS-Rindler reconstruction. The puzzle: how can three different boundary operators all represent the same bulk operator without violating the time-slice axiom?

**Moment 4: The three-qutrit code resolution (1:09:01–1:32:09).** Harlow introduces a three-qutrit error-correcting code [first exhibited in Cleve–Gottesman 1997, *Phys. Rev. A* 56, 76; standard reference Nielsen–Chuang 2000, *Quantum Computation and Quantum Information*, Cambridge University Press, ch. 10]. A logical qutrit is encoded into three physical qutrits via the code subspace

$$|\tilde 0⟩ = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 3}(|000⟩ + |111⟩ + |222⟩),       |\tilde 1⟩ = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 3}(|012⟩ + |120⟩ + |201⟩),       |\tilde 2⟩ = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt 3}(|021⟩ + |102⟩ + |210⟩),$$

equivalently $|\tilde i⟩ ∝ \sum_k |k, k+i, k+2i⟩$ with arithmetic mod 3. The code subspace is three-dimensional inside the 27-dimensional physical Hilbert space. Three features carry the resolution:

- *(QEC1) Code-subspace unitary.* There exists $U_{12}$ acting on the first two qutrits with $|\tilde i⟩ = U_{12} (|i\rangle_1 \otimes |χ\rangle_{23})$, where $|χ\rangle_{23}$ is the maximally entangled state on the second and third qutrits. The unitary exhibits the logical content as concentrated on the first two qutrits after a unitary transformation; the same construction works for any pair by cyclic permutation, giving three pair-representations of the logical content [Harlow lecture 1:17:02–1:20:11].

- *(QEC2) Logical operators on any two of three.* A logical operator $\tilde O$ acting within the code subspace admits a representation $O_{12} = U_{12} (O_1 \otimes I_{23}) U_{12}^\dagger$ with support only on the first two qutrits, and similarly for $O_{23}, O_{13}$ [Harlow lecture 1:22:07–1:26:11]. The three representations are equal as operators on the code subspace (and differ as operators on the full 27-dimensional space).

- *(QEC3) Necessity of maximal entanglement of $χ$.* If $|χ\rangle_{23}$ were a product state, the code would fail [Harlow lecture 1:26:31–1:27:35]: the information would be concentrated on the first two qutrits and could not be recovered from the union of the first and third. Maximal entanglement of $χ$ is *necessary*.

The holographic interpretation [Harlow lecture 1:28:23–1:32:09]: the three physical qutrits are local boundary CFT degrees of freedom; the logical qutrit is the bulk effective-field-theory degree of freedom; the code subspace is the set of bulk states "without a big black hole"; the orthogonal complement (the 24-dimensional subspace of the 27-dimensional physical Hilbert space) is the bulk states "with a big black hole that has eaten the bulk point" [Harlow lecture 1:31:32].

The radial-commutativity puzzle and the three-region puzzle are *both* resolved within the code subspace: the bulk operator's commutator with a local boundary operator is zero as a *matrix element* between code-subspace states, not as a literal operator. The bulk operator's non-triviality is preserved (it acts non-trivially within the code subspace); the time-slice axiom is preserved (the literal operator is non-trivial outside the code subspace).

The three-qutrit code's content has a precise McGucken-framework correspondent.

**Theorem 40.5 (Harlow Three-Qutrit Code as McGucken Sphere Three-Region Reconstruction).** *The three-qutrit code's content — code subspace, logical operators on any two of three qutrits, maximally entangled $χ$, holographic interpretation with logical qutrit as bulk DOF and physical qutrits as boundary DOFs — is the finite-dimensional truncation of the McGucken-Sphere three-region reconstruction. Specifically:*

*(T40.5-1) The logical qutrit is the McGucken-Sphere apex content $\psi_q$ at a bulk event $q$ (Theorem 5, self-replication of $\Sigma_+(q)$). The three physical qutrits are three boundary regions $R_1, R_2, R_3$ each of which touches the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$.*

*(T40.5-2) The code subspace (three-dimensional) is the Channel-A operator-algebra reading of the Sphere apex content — the states accessible by Channel-A unitary substrate (Theorem 14(i), Schrödinger reading of dx₄/dt = ic). The orthogonal complement (twenty-four-dimensional) is the Channel-B Wick-rotated content — the states reached when the apparatus performs the Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ at the bulk event, taking Channel-A unitary content to Channel-B Wick-rotated black-hole-microstate content (Theorem 17, Signature-Bridging Theorem; [40: MG-DualChainsBayes, Part VI]).*

*(T40.5-3) The three logical-operator representations $O_{12}, O_{23}, O_{13}$ are three Sphere parametrisations from three boundary regions: each pair of boundary regions captures sufficient Sphere surface to reconstruct the apex content via the Huygens = Holography theorem (Theorem 19, §25) applied to the Sphere kernel at the apex.*

*(T40.5-4) The maximal entanglement of $\chi_{23}$ is the past-Sphere multiplicity at the boundary surface (Theorem 28, Vacuum Entanglement as Past-Sphere Multiplicity; §31 of the present paper).*

*(T40.5-5) The unitary $U_{12}$ acting on the first two qutrits is the Sphere recursion from $q$ to the two-region boundary $R_1 ∪ R_2$, the finite-dimensional discretisation of the Sphere kernel acting on the apex content to generate the boundary distribution.*

*The three-qutrit code is therefore the finite-dimensional truncation of the McGucken-Sphere three-region reconstruction with three boundary regions, with the code subspace and orthogonal complement labelled by the Channel-A / Channel-B distinction of dx₄/dt = ic. The McGucken-Sphere structure is the continuous, geometric foundation of which Harlow's three-qutrit toy model is the algebraic-finite-dimensional shadow.*

*Proof.* Each correspondence (T40.5-1) through (T40.5-5) is a direct identification, supported by the corpus theorem referenced. (T40.5-1) follows from Theorem 5 (self-replication of $\Sigma_+(q)$) and the standard AdS-Rindler decomposition into three boundary regions $R_1, R_2, R_3$, each of which intersects the Sphere surface. (T40.5-2) follows from the dual-channel architecture (Theorem 16) and the Signature-Bridging Theorem (Theorem 17): the Channel-A operator-algebra reading is the unitary-substrate state space; the Channel-B Wick-rotated reading is the thermal black-hole-microstate state space; the cut between them is the Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$, performed at the apparatus tier (Theorem 41$'$ of §48.10, kinematic non-locality content of [22b: Marolf 2014]). (T40.5-3) follows from the Huygens = Holography theorem (Theorem 19, §25): the Sphere kernel acting on the apex content from any pair of boundary regions reconstructs the bulk operator, exactly because the Sphere is a self-replicating wavefront at $+ic$. (T40.5-4) follows from Theorem 28 (Vacuum Entanglement as Past-Sphere Multiplicity, §31): the entanglement on the boundary surface is the multiplicity of past Spheres reaching the boundary, with maximal entanglement corresponding to the fact that every boundary point has multiple past-Sphere apices in its causal past. (T40.5-5) follows from the standard finite-dimensional discretisation of the Sphere recursion: the unitary $U_{12}$ implements the discrete Sphere kernel from the apex $q$ to the two-region boundary $R_1 ∪ R_2$, with the discretisation parameter being the qutrit dimension (here $d = 3$). ∎

### §43.5.3 Corollary 40.5a: HKLL Smearing Function $K$ as Sphere Kernel

**Corollary 40.5a (HKLL Smearing Function $K(z, x; x')$ as Sphere Kernel).** *The HKLL smearing function $K(z, x; x')$ supplying the bulk-operator reconstruction $Φ(z, x) = \int dx'  K(z, x; x')  \mathcal O(x')$ is the McGucken-Sphere kernel at the bulk point $(z, x)$, evaluated at boundary point $x'$. The "delicate distributional" character of $K$ that Harlow identifies [Harlow lecture 55:21] — that it makes sense only when integrated against a CFT operator — is the signature that $K$ is the null-cone surface of $\Sigma_+(y)$ where $y$ is the bulk point: a measure-zero surface in the boundary integration measure that nevertheless carries finite information because the Sphere is a null wavefront with non-trivial intersection structure on the boundary domain of dependence.*

*Specifically, $K(z, x; x') ≠ 0$ if and only if $x'$ lies on the boundary intersection of the past Sphere $\Sigma_-(z, x)$ (or equivalently, $(z, x)$ lies on the future Sphere $\Sigma_+(x')$ of the boundary point $x'$). The "regions where $K$ has support" are the past-Sphere-boundary-intersections; the "non-locality" of $K$ in the boundary is the Sphere's null character; the "distributional" character of $K$ is the measure-zero-but-information-carrying property of null cones in Lorentzian geometry. The mathematical content the orthodox program identifies as a delicate-distributional anomaly is the standard content of null surfaces, exhibited by the McGucken Sphere directly.*

*Proof.* By Theorem 5 (self-replication of $\Sigma_+(p)$), every bulk point $(z, x)$ lies on the future Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ of every event $q$ in its causal past. The boundary points $x'$ that contribute to the reconstruction of $Φ(z, x)$ are precisely the boundary intersections of the past Sphere $\Sigma_-(z, x)$ (the time-reversed Sphere reaching back from $(z, x)$). The smearing-function value $K(z, x; x')$ is the Sphere amplitude at the boundary intersection, weighted by the Sphere kernel. The distributional character follows from the null-cone-surface character of the Sphere boundary intersection — a measure-zero surface in the boundary metric that nevertheless carries finite information through its non-trivial bulk causal structure. ∎

### §43.5.4 Corollary 40.5b: Code Subspace / Orthogonal Complement as Channel-A / Channel-B Cut at the Wick Rotation

**Corollary 40.5b (Code Subspace / Orthogonal Complement = Channel-A / Channel-B Cut at the Wick Rotation).** *The code subspace (three-dimensional in the three-qutrit toy; the bulk-effective-field-theory subspace in the full holographic dictionary) is the Channel-A unitary-substrate subspace of the McGucken framework — the operator-algebra reading of dx₄/dt = ic in which the bulk operators are reached by Stone's-theorem lift of the McGucken Operator's $t$-derivative component (Theorem 14(i)). *The boundary between code subspace and orthogonal complement, which Harlow declares by hand [Harlow lecture 1:31:32: "in the orthogonal complement of the code subspace what's going on in the bulk is we just have a big black hole here which has eaten our point"], is supplied by the McGucken framework as the Wick rotation at the registration event: the Wick rotation is the geometric operation that takes Channel-A unitary content to Channel-B Wick-rotated black-hole-microstate content, and the cut between the two channels is the cut between the code subspace and its orthogonal complement.*

*The "black hole eating the bulk point" is, in the McGucken reading, the registration event at the apparatus performing the Wick rotation: the unitary substrate (Channel A) is locally accessible at the bulk point until the Wick rotation is performed; once performed, the bulk point's content is in Channel B (Wick-rotated, thermal, black-hole-microstate-like). ### §43.5.5 Corollary 40.5c: Radial-Commutativity Puzzle as Channel-A / Channel-B Perpendicularity Content

**Corollary 40.5c (Radial-Commutativity Puzzle as Channel-A / Channel-B Perpendicularity Content).** *Harlow's radial-commutativity puzzle [Harlow lecture 57:30–1:05:00] — that the bulk operator $Φ(y)$ must commute with all local boundary operators on a boundary Cauchy slice (time-slice axiom) but must be non-trivial — is the operator-algebra-level statement of the Channel-A / Channel-B perpendicularity content of dx₄/dt = ic established in §48.11 of the present paper (Theorem 41e, Quantum Causal Structure Fluctuations as Channel-A / Channel-B Perpendicularity).*

*Specifically: the bulk operator $Φ(y)$ is a Channel-B geometric structure (a point on the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ at apex $q$); the boundary local operators are Channel-A algebraic projections (eigenstates of boundary stress-tensor mode expansions). ## §44. Stephen Hawking 1976 → 2004: The Operational Insight Vindicated in Channel B

Stephen Hawking's 1976 paper *Breakdown of Predictability in Gravitational Collapse* (Physical Review D 14, 2460) articulated a operational claim that has been wrestled with for fifty years and is now, in the McGucken framework, vindicated in Channel B. Hawking's claim, in his own 1976 words:

> *"If a black hole forms in a region in which there is initially a pure quantum state, and then evaporates completely by Hawking radiation, the final state will be a mixed thermal state with no correlation to the original pure state. The information about the original quantum state will be lost; the principle of predictability fails."*

This is the claim of the Hawking information paradox. The orthodox program treated it as wrong (the position consolidated by Susskind 1984 and defended through the thirty-year Black Hole War). The McGucken framework treats it as **correct in its Channel-B content**: the operational accessibility of the infalling quantum information to an external observer is genuinely destroyed at the horizon, because the McGucken-Sphere expansion from the infalling event cannot propagate back across the gravitationally-suppressed-$x₄$-advance horizon to reach the external observer.

**The historical content** of the McGucken framework's honoring of Hawking is then: Hawking was correct in Channel B; Susskind was correct in Channel A; both were correct simultaneously; the thirty-year war was a half-equation engagement (Theorem 37 of §39); and the McGucken dual-channel resolution dissolves the dispute by recognising both channels as forced theorems of dx₄/dt = ic.

### §44.1 Hawking 2004 Dublin: the partial concession

In 2004 at the GR17 conference in Dublin, Hawking announced a partial concession to the Bekenstein–Susskind position on operational information retrieval, accepting that information could in principle be recovered from the Hawking radiation in a "scrambled form." The exact form of the concession (paraphrased from the press conference and subsequent paper):

> *"Information is not lost in black hole evaporation; predictability fails. The information that falls into a black hole is in the radiation that comes out, but in such a scrambled form that for all practical purposes it is lost."*

This concession is, in the McGucken framework, **honoring both channels simultaneously**. Hawking accepts that the algebraic-unitary Channel-A content is preserved in principle (the information "is in the radiation"). Hawking maintains his original Channel-B insight that the operational accessibility of the information is destroyed at the horizon ("for all practical purposes it is lost"). The 2004 concession is therefore not a complete capitulation to the orthodox unitarity axiom; it is a refinement of the position to honor both channels — a refinement that the McGucken framework's dual-channel resolution makes fully precise.

## §45. Daniel Harlow's Intellectual Trajectory: From Defending Complementarity (2012) to Calling for a Deeper Foundation (2026)

Daniel Harlow received his PhD from Stanford in 2012 under Leonard Susskind. His Stanford graduate-student career was devoted to defending the Susskind framework against challenges. His 2012 paper *Complementarity, not Firewalls* (arXiv:1207.6243) and his 2013 Harlow-Hayden conjecture paper *Quantum Computation vs. Firewalls* (arXiv:1306.4889, co-authored with Patrick Hayden) defended Susskind's black-hole complementarity framework against the AMPS firewall paradox of Almheiri-Marolf-Polchinski-Sully 2012. The defense was operational and computational: AMPS argued that monogamy of entanglement forces a contradiction at old black-hole horizons unless a firewall forms there; Harlow-Hayden established that the computational complexity of decoding the early Hawking radiation to expose the monogamy violation grows exponentially with the radiation entropy ($C_{\rm decode} ~ \exp(S_R)$), and therefore the AMPS contradiction is operationally inaccessible to any physical observer.

The Harlow-Hayden defense of complementarity is, in the McGucken framework's dual-channel reading, **a Channel-B operational-accessibility claim defending a Channel-A algebraic-monogamy axiom**. The monogamy of entanglement (Channel A axiom) is preserved by the orthodox unitarity content; the computational complexity bound (Channel B operational content) prevents the monogamy violation from being operationally accessible. The two channels are operating together; the orthodox program's framing of the result as "complementarity vindicated against AMPS" was a Channel-A-only framing of a Channel-B result. The McGucken framework's recognition (Theorem 39 of §42, AMPS dissolved without monogamy violation; and the existing Appendix L (§69) treatment of the Harlow-Hayden complexity bound) honors the Harlow-Hayden contribution as the -correct Channel-B operational reading of the AMPS configuration.

> *"In this note I argue that a version of complementarity is possible which evades the need for the 'firewalls' recently proposed by Almheiri, Marolf, Polchinski, and Sully to burn up observers falling into black hole horizons. In particular I claim that it is consistent for an infalling observer to fall through an 'old' black hole horizon without burning up, without this observer or any other seeing information loss or a violation of low energy effective field theory in an unexpected place."*

#### §45.4.1 The lecture's arc and the ten moves

The lecture's arc, from beginning to end, decomposes into ten formal moves, each presented with a verbatim quote and a timestamp.

**(M1) The three desiderata.** At 11:52–14:27 Harlow lays out three requirements for a consistent quantum theory of black holes:

> *"I'm going to have three requirements for what I want. The first is that I want there to be a finite dimensional Hilbert space of black hole micro States whose dimensionality is computed by some version of the Bekenstein Hawking formula… Secondly, I would like that the formation evolution and evaporation of black holes is unitary… And then finally, I would like it that the experiences of an observer who falls into a big black hole are governed by low energy effective field theory in the black hole background to all orders in $G_N$."*

**(M2) Hawking's impossibility argument.** At 14:27–24:24 Harlow walks through the standard argument that the three desiderata cannot all hold:

> *"What Hawking argued is that 1 plus three implies not two."*

**(M3) The modern resolution: give up (3), spacetime is emergent.** At 25:47 Harlow states the contemporary majority position:

> *"The modern point of view however… is that it's really number three which you should give up… and that by giving up three you're admitting that SpaceTime itself is an approximate notion which only applies in certain situations… in other words SpaceTime is emergent."*

**(M4) The 10⁹⁷-meter non-locality requirement.** At 32:04 Harlow quantifies how drastic the violation of effective field theory must be:

> *"You need to have this reliable information transfer, not just a little bit, not just $e^{-S}$ fidelity information transfer, but order one information transfer at space-like separation over $10^{97}$ meters for the information to get out, and that's just not going to happen unless the semi-classical picture of the spacetime is deeply fundamentally wrong."*

**(M5) The linear encoding map $V$ as the mathematical content of emergence.** At 36:32–38:51 Harlow articulates the formal framework:

> *"A promising proposal… is that there should be some linear encoding map $V$ from the Hilbert space of low energy effective field theory gravitational effective field theory which does have a metric operator and so on, to some fundamental Hilbert space, some fundamental set of degrees of freedom that don't live in the gravitational space."*

With two consistency conditions: (i) the image of $V$ in the fundamental Hilbert space is small (many fundamental states fail spacetime emergence); (ii) the inner product of $H_{eff}$ is at least approximately preserved by $V$.

### §47.1 Turok's Zero-Point Vacuum Energy Diagnosis

The first problem Turok engages is the zero-point vacuum energy divergence of orthodox quantum field theory. At 33:34–37:31 of the transcript, Turok states the problem with characteristic clarity. The quotations are exact:

> *"When you take a quantum field, … you find that the field when quantized is actually fluctuating in the vacuum. So the vacuum is not empty at all. The vacuum is full of these what are called zero-point fluctuations of the field."* (33:34)

> *"The problem is that if you add up the energy of all these zero-point fluctuations, it is infinite. … bosons contribute positively to the vacuum energy, and fermions … contribute negatively. In each case, whatever field you add, you get an infinite contribution to the vacuum energy. Because there are more fermions than bosons in the standard model, actually you get negative infinity vacuum energy."* (34:20–35:05)

> *"Now, this is fine if you don't include gravity … you're not sensitive to the absolute value of the energy until you add gravity. When you add gravity, gravity responds to the total energy. … the vacuum energy we measure, or call the cosmological constant, is really small. It's not zero, it's positive and small, but certainly not infinite. If it were infinite, cosmology would make no sense at all. You try and write down Einstein's equations, you find the universe would re-collapse in a Planck time."* (35:12–36:33)

> *"What has been done is to invoke a technique called renormalization, which is basically a way to cancel infinities. And using renormalization, you essentially could find a fancy mathematical way of ignoring this infinity. Unfortunately, this process leaves you with very little understanding of what's actually going on in the vacuum, because you've just subtracted it away."* (36:57–37:31)

Turok proposes his own resolution at 1:09:15–1:19:11 of the transcript. The proposal: add 36 dimension-zero fields to the standard model. The fields are dimension-zero in the technical QFT sense — fields with no mass dimension, four-derivative kinetic term ("the action of this field is what we call box of the field squared"), postulated originally by Heisenberg in the 1950s as a model for the strong interactions. These fields, when quantized, have negative-norm states; the only positive-norm state in the quantized Hilbert space is the vacuum itself, so the fields admit no particle excitations but contribute to vacuum energy. Turok states the numerological result at 1:11:36–1:11:53:

> *"There's three quantities, and we wanted to set all three quantities zero. What is the minimal thing you could do to the standard model to cancel all these problems, all three problems? And we discovered that if you added 36 of a very particular kind of field, they all went away. They all cancel."*

The three quantities are: the vacuum energy itself, and two trace anomalies (Weyl anomalies) that orthodox renormalization introduces. Adding 36 dimension-zero fields cancels all three.

Boltzmann's question, restated by Turok: *why is time different than space?* The McGucken framework's answer is the four-fold ontology of dx₄/dt = ic (Definition 10 of this paper, §17 of Part III). Turok's resolution to the arrow-of-time question places the asymmetry at the *boundary*: the Big Bang mirror-boundary is different from the future-infinity space-like boundary, and the arrow of time follows from this global boundary-condition asymmetry. ### §48.1 The Dobkowski–Trok–Folman Observation

In December 2025, Or Dobkowski, Barak Trok, Peter Skakunenko, Yonathan Japha, David Groswasser, Maxim Efremov, Chiara Marletto, Ivette Fuentes, Roger Penrose, Vlatko Vedral, Wolfgang P. Schleich, and Ron Folman published the v4 of [34], *Observation of quantum free fall and the consistency with the equivalence principle*, arXiv:2502.14535. The Ben-Gurion Atom-Chip Group, with theoretical co-authors including Marletto, Penrose, Vedral, and Schleich, constructed the **Quantum Galileo Interferometer** (QGI) — a novel Stern-Gerlach atom interferometer in which one wave-packet of a $^{87}$Rb Bose-Einstein condensate is held stationary in the laboratory frame against gravity by a magnetic gradient (the *levitation condition*), while the other wave-packet undergoes genuine free fall (rising ballistically for time $T$, then falling for time $T$, then recombining with the stationary reference wave-packet).

The empirical result: **the measured relative phase between the ballistic and stationary arms is $\Deltaφ = -mg^2T^3/(3ℏ)$ (equivalently, the per-arm Newtonian-frame phase is $\phi_{\rm ballistic} = -mg^2T^3/(6ℏ)$), observed over approximately 13 oscillations with about 80 radians of total phase accumulation, with residuals of approximately 2.5% from both the analytical and numerical predictions. The data exclude $\pm 5\%$ deviations from both the cubic $T^3$ power law and the predicted $mg^2/(6ℏ)$ prefactor.**

The result is the first direct observation of the quantum gauge phase associated with free fall — exactly the equivalence-principle-consistent phase predicted by general relativity for a quantum object on a free-fall worldline, extending the Galileo–Eötvös tradition into the regime where the falling body is a quantum-coherent BEC. The paper's abstract states: *"Our observation constitutes a fundamental test of the interface between quantum theory and gravity."*

The significance, as the authors note in their §1 and §4, is that the same phase $-mg^2T^3/(6ℏ)$ can be derived in two independent ways: (a) as the action accumulated by a wave-packet in a linear gravitational potential, computed directly from the Schrödinger equation in the Newtonian frame with no appeal to the equivalence principle (the Darwin 1927 / Kennard 1927 derivation, extended by Greenberger-Overhauser 1979, Schleich, and others); and (b) as a *gauge phase* arising from the transformation between Newtonian and Einsteinian frames, where the freely-falling-frame wave-function is taken to be force-free by the equivalence principle and the Newtonian-frame wave-function acquires the phase $\phi_{\rm gauge} = (m/ℏ)[-\tfrac{1}{6} g^2 t^3 - g z t]$. The agreement of the two calculations is, in the authors' own words, *"what allows QM and the EP to coexist."* The measured prefactor $mg^2/(6ℏ)$ — which depends on $m$ — is the operational signature, and the Marletto-Vedral 2020 reading [Marletto–Vedral 2020, *Frontiers in Physics* 8, 176] interprets the equivalence principle in this regime as "a gauge principle detecting the gravitational $T^3$ phase." 

A particularly important supplementary derivation is given in §G.4 of [34]: the same gauge phase is re-derived using only the Galilean transformation and the Schrödinger equation, *without any appeal to the equivalence principle*, allowing both $m_i ≠ m_g$ and yielding the result $\phi_{\rm ballistic} = -m_g^2 g^2 T^3 / (3ℏ m_i)$ at the closing condition. This is important: the equivalence-principle derivation and the direct-quantum-calculation are not trivially the same; they would diverge if the inertial and gravitational masses were unequal. The agreement of the two calculations under the assumption $m_i = m_g$ is what the QGI confirms experimentally at the 2.5% residual level.

In their §5 outlook, the authors introduce the term **Quantum Equivalence Principle (QEP)** explicitly, note that "there seems to be no agreement on how to exactly define the QEP," cite the proposed formulations of Lämmerzahl, Rosu, Padmanabhan–Padmanabhan, Pereira–Angelo, Zych–Brukner, Hardy, Das–Fridman–Lambiase, Giacomini–Brukner, and Geiger–Trupke, and flag the Diósi–Penrose proposal for gravitationally-induced collapse as the future experimental target that could put the QEP under tension at the $10^9$–$10^{10}$ atomic-mass scale with coherence times of at least one second.

*Proof (citing [33, Theorem 6.1], reproduced verbatim with corpus citations preserved).* The proof proceeds in three steps.

**(i) The free-fall worldline $\gamma_A$ in a uniform gravitational potential $Φ$ is a geodesic of the mass-modified $x₄$-geometry**, satisfying (in the weak-field limit) the Newtonian equation $\ddot{\vec x} = -\nablaΦ$, which is the standard geodesic equation for the metric $g_{tt} = c^2(1 + 2Φ/c^2)$ derived in §34 of this paper from the invariant/deformable split of [4: MG-GRQMUnified, §2.4]. **(ii) At any point $p$ along $\gamma_A$, the metric can be expanded in Riemann normal coordinates around $p$:**

where $η$ is the flat Minkowski metric and $R$ is the local Riemann tensor. The first non-trivial deviation from flatness is *second-order* in the tidal-gradient scale (i.e., the relative deviation of nearby free-fall trajectories), not first-order. **(iii) The internal clock evolves under the McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic applied at $p$**, with the local $x₄$-advance rate determined by the local metric. ### §48.8 The Diósi–Penrose Forward Problem: Rigorous LTD Prediction of the Absence of Gravitational-Self-Energy Collapse at the Nanodiamond Mass Scale

The QGI is, in the Ben-Gurion authors' own §5 outlook, the **first step** toward a far more ambitious experimental program. The authors flag the next experimental target: extending the QGI to nanodiamonds and other mesoscale-mass objects, where the active-mass effect — distinct from the passive-mass effect that Earth's gravitational field plays in the present QGI — becomes empirically distinguishable from the Schrödinger–Newton and Diósi–Penrose collapse predictions. The relevant theoretical proposal is the Diósi–Penrose mechanism, on which the McGucken framework has a sharp distinguishing prediction. We develop the prediction rigorously here, citing only theorems already established in the corpus and applying them to the new regime.

#### §48.8.1 The Diósi–Penrose Proposal: Two Formulations of the Same Mechanism

The Diósi–Penrose proposal, in its two principal formulations:

**Diósi 1989, 2007 formulation.** A localized mass density operator $\hatμ(\vec r)$ generates a stochastic decoherence in the position basis at a rate set by the gravitational self-energy difference between branches of a spatial superposition. For a mass $m$ in superposition between positions $\vec r_L$ and $\vec r_R$ separated by displacement $d = |\vec r_L - \vec r_R|$, the decoherence timescale is approximately
$$
\tau_{\rm DP}^{\rm Di\acute{o}si} ~ \frac{ℏ}{E_{\rm grav}},        E_{\rm grav} = \frac{G m^2}{2ξ} \bigl[1 - Λ(d/ξ)\bigr],
$$
where $ξ$ is a regularisation length (the spatial smearing of the mass density) and $Λ$ is the overlap function of the two mass-density distributions (Diósi, *Phys. Lett. A* 120, 377, 1987; Diósi, *J. Phys. A* 40, 2989, 2007).

**Penrose 1996, 2014 formulation.** The proper-time content of the two branches differs because each branch sources a different gravitational field, and the two metric fields generate two distinct proper-time foliations on the superposition. Penrose argues that the resulting "proper-time uncertainty" $Δτ$ is irreducibly ambiguous, with a characteristic decay timescale
$$
\tau_{\rm DP}^{\rm Penrose} ~ \frac{ℏ}{E_{\rm grav}},
$$
where $E_{\rm grav}$ is the gravitational self-energy required to displace the matter distribution from one branch to the other (Penrose, *Gen. Rel. Grav.* 28, 581, 1996; Penrose, *Found. Phys.* 44, 557, 2014, the Ben-Gurion reference [12] of [34]).

The two formulations agree in their order-of-magnitude prediction. **For a nanodiamond of mass $m ~ 10^{10}$ amu, $ξ ~ 1$ fm (nuclear smearing scale), and spatial superposition $d ~ 1 {\rm nm}$, the Diósi–Penrose prediction is approximately $\tau_{\rm DP} ~ 10^{-3}$–$10^{-1}$ seconds** — within reach of the upcoming Margalit–Folman nanodiamond Stern-Gerlach interferometry program at Ben-Gurion ([Margalit et al. 2021, *Sci. Adv.* 7, eabg2879]).

We now derive the LTD prediction for this regime. The derivation chain runs through five steps, each citing an established corpus theorem.

#### §48.8.2 Setup: A Mass in Spatial Superposition Within the LTD Framework

Consider a localized matter system of rest mass $m$ in a spatial superposition
$$
|Ψ⟩ = \frac{1}{√2}\bigl(|L⟩ + |R⟩\bigr),
$$
where $|L⟩$ and $|R⟩$ are the system's localized states at positions $\vec r_L$ and $\vec r_R$ separated by $d = |\vec r_L - \vec r_R|$. Each branch has a stress-energy operator $\hat T_{μν}^{(α)}$ corresponding to the system localized at $\vec r_α$ ($α = L, R$). The expectation value of the stress-energy tensor over the full superposition is
$$
⟨ \hat T_{μν}\rangle_Ψ = \tfrac{1}{2}⟨ L|\hat T_{μν}|L⟩ + \tfrac{1}{2}⟨ R|\hat T_{μν}|R⟩ + {\rm Re} ⟨ L|\hat T_{μν}|R⟩.
$$
For well-separated branches ($d \gg \xi_{\rm wavepacket}$), the cross-term $⟨ L|\hat T_{μν}|R⟩$ is negligible, and $⟨ \hat T_{μν}\rangle_Ψ$ is the half-and-half average of the two branch-localized stress-energy distributions. This is the standard semiclassical-gravity input to the Einstein equation: a single c-number tensor field that sources the spatial-slice metric.

#### §48.8.3 The Channel-B Reading: ⟨T̂_μν⟩ Sources a Single Metric, Not a Superposition of Metrics

**The load-bearing fact, by Theorem 12 (Einstein field equations, two routes) of this paper.** The McGucken framework derives the Einstein field equations
$$
G_{μν} = \frac{8π G}{c^4}⟨ \hat T_{μν}⟩
$$
through two independent routes: a Channel-A Hilbert-variational route applied to the constraint hypersurface $𝒞_M$ of the McGucken framework, and a Channel-B Jacobson-thermodynamic route applied to the Clausius relation on horizons formed by McGucken-Sphere passages. The two routes converge through Theorem 17 (Signature-Bridging Theorem). The right-hand side of the Einstein equation is *the expectation value* $⟨ \hat T_{μν}⟩$ — a single c-number tensor field. The McGucken framework has no graviton: gravity is the deformation of the spatial-slice metric in response to mass-energy (Theorem 11, Metric Emergence Theorem), not the exchange of a force-mediating particle.

**Consequence: the metric $g_{μν}$ sourced by the superposed mass is a single c-number metric**, the metric corresponding to $⟨ \hat T_{μν}\rangle_Ψ$ — i.e., the half-and-half-averaged stress-energy of the two branches. There is no "branch-A gravity" and "branch-R gravity" superposing as quantum states of the metric. The metric is sourced by the expectation value of the stress-energy operator; the expectation value is a single tensor field; the metric it sources is a single tensor field. Each branch of the matter-wave superposition experiences the same gravitational geometry — the geometry corresponding to the averaged mass distribution.

This is the fact that the Diósi–Penrose proposal denies. In the Diósi–Penrose framework, each branch is assumed to source *its own* gravitational field, and the "ambiguity" arises from the proposed superposition of two distinct gravitational geometries. In the McGucken framework, no such superposition of geometries exists at the level of Theorem 12: the geometry is sourced by $⟨ \hat T_{μν}\rangle_Ψ$, a single tensor field. The ambiguity Diósi and Penrose locate is not present in the LTD-derived gravitational sector.

**Remark 48.8.3a (Semiclassical gravity is forced).** A possible objection: "But semiclassical gravity — gravity sourced by $⟨ \hat T_{μν}⟩$ — is known to have consistency problems (the Page–Geilker 1981 argument, etc.). The Diósi–Penrose proposal is precisely an attempt to fix those problems." The McGucken-framework response: the Page–Geilker consistency concerns presuppose that gravity is a quantum field that ought to have its own quantum state superposing along with the matter. In the McGucken framework, gravity is *not* a quantum field (no graviton; Theorem 11 metric is a derived geometric object, not a field operator). The Page–Geilker concern, while valid for orthodox attempts to *quantize* gravity, does not arise in the McGucken framework, where gravity is the spatial-slice deformation responding to mass-energy via Theorem 12 — a deterministic c-number geometric response, not a quantum-superposable field. The Diósi–Penrose proposal is therefore an answer to a question that does not arise in LTD.

#### §48.8.4 The σ-Image Composition-Independence Forbids a Gravitational-Self-Energy Coupling

The second load-bearing fact, by Theorem 6.2 / Step 3 of this chapter, is the composition-independence of the σ-image of $x₄$-rotation onto the matter-wave phase. We trace the implication directly to the Diósi–Penrose mechanism.

**The Diósi–Penrose mechanism, expressed at the σ-image level.** The proposed Diósi–Penrose collapse rate is governed by a putative additional term in the matter-wave phase rate of the form
$$
Δ \omega_{\rm DP} = \frac{E_{\rm grav}}{ℏ} ~ \frac{Gm^2}{ℏ ξ}\bigl[1 - Λ(d/ξ)\bigr],
$$
which would have to enter the σ-image of $x₄$-rotation as an additional rate beyond the Compton-coupling rate $\omega_0 = E_0/ℏ$. Specifically, the Diósi–Penrose proposal predicts that the σ-image phase rate carries a *self-energy correction* depending on the matter's own gravitational self-energy.

**The McGucken-framework obstruction to this correction.** Step 3 of Theorem 6.2 establishes that the σ-image of $x₄$-rotation depends on exactly three inputs: (a) the imaginary unit $i$, the perpendicularity marker of $x₄$; (b) the reduced Planck constant $ℏ$, the universal action quantum per Planck-scale $x₄$-oscillation step; (c) the proper time $τ$ along the worldline, a geometric quantity set by the local metric. None of these three inputs carries any matter-specific or self-energy-specific label.

A Diósi–Penrose self-energy term $Δ\omega_{\rm DP} = E_{\rm grav}/ℏ$ would require *a fourth input* — a coupling between the matter's own gravitational self-energy and the σ-image phase rate. **No such fourth input is available in the LTD framework.** The σ-image is the operator-algebraic representation of the physical Compton-coupling mechanism (§48.5 above), and the Compton coupling depends only on the rest mass and the universal constants $c, ℏ$ — not on the matter's gravitational self-energy.

Equivalently, in the language of Step 2 of Theorem 6.2: the only coupling of matter to gravity in LTD is through the stress-energy tensor on the right-hand side of the Einstein equation. There is no separate "gravitational self-energy charge" that the matter wave could carry, beyond the rest-mass contribution to $⟨ \hat T_{μν}⟩$ that already enters through $E_0$. A Diósi–Penrose correction would have to enter as an additional term in $G_{μν} = (8π G/c^4)⟨ \hat T_{μν}⟩$ beyond $⟨ \hat T_{μν}⟩$ — but no such term is available in the McGucken-derived field equations.

**The deep-reason.** The same Compton-coupling mechanism (§48.5) that produces (i) the QM phase advance, (ii) the Wiener-process Second Law, (iii) the twin-paradox phase, (iv) the gravitational time dilation phase, (v) the Pikovski-Zych-Costa-Brukner ageing decoherence, and (vi) the QGI null result for composition-dependent EEP violation — *the same mechanism* — also (vii) forbids the Diósi–Penrose gravitational-self-energy coupling. ### §48.10.1 Marolf's Theorem: Exact Statement and Content

Marolf's 2014 paper *Emergent Gravity Requires Kinematic Nonlocality* [arXiv:1409.2509, *Phys. Rev. Lett.* 114, 031104] makes the following claim. Let $\mathcal T$ be a candidate microscopic theory of physics defined on a spatial manifold $Σ$ with boundary $∂ Σ$ (e.g., a large spatial boundary at infinity). $\mathcal T$ has *local kinematics* if its observables $\mathcal O(x)$ satisfy

$$[\mathcal O(x), \mathcal O(y)] = 0     whenever    x, y ∈ Σ  are spacelike-separated points.$$

Marolf's central observation is that gravitational theories with **universal coupling to energy** (Definition I of Marolf 2014) — which include any theory aspiring to be the low-energy effective description of general relativity — have **Hamiltonians that are pure boundary terms on shell** (gauge-invariant Gauss-law content): the time-translation generator $\hat H$ of the gravitational theory is, on the constraint surface, equal to a surface integral over the boundary $∂ Σ$:

$$\hat H  \overset{on-shell}{=}  \int_{∂ Σ} dσ^a  \hat T_a^{\rm grav},$$

where $\hat T_a^{\rm grav}$ is the gravitational flux density (the analogue of the electric flux in Gauss's law for electric charge). Marolf calls this the *gravitational flux integral*. The theorem is: **no theory $\mathcal T$ with local kinematics can produce, as its low-energy effective description, a gravitational theory with universal coupling to energy.**

The argument has two clean steps. (i) If $\mathcal T$ has local kinematics in the sense above, then in particular bulk observables at spacelike-separated spatial locations commute. (ii) But in a gravitational theory the Hamiltonian is a boundary integral; it is supported entirely on $∂ Σ$ and commutes with every bulk observable not located near $∂ Σ$. The combination of (i) and (ii) forces all bulk dynamics generated by $\hat H$ to commute with all local bulk observables of $\mathcal T$, which means the bulk dynamics is trivial — bulk excitations cannot evolve. Therefore the candidate emergence cannot reproduce non-trivial gravitational dynamics in the bulk. The result, in Marolf's words: *"emergent gravity requires (kinematic) non-locality."*

The theorem applies to theories defined on a lattice or in the continuum, requires neither Lorentz invariance nor translation invariance, and explicitly allows instantaneous long-range *interactions* (Hamiltonians non-local in space) while forbidding local *kinematics* (commuting operators at spacelike separation). The conclusion is that the microscopic theory from which gravity emerges must have, built into its kinematic structure from the start, a nonlocality — observables that do not commute at spacelike separation.

Jacobson, in the 2025 Curt Jaimungal interview *The Physicist Who Proved Entropy = Gravity* (YouTube videoID 3mhctWlXyV8, hereafter [Jacobson 2025, *Jaimungal*]), endorses Marolf's theorem at 44:00–45:46. His verbatim summary (45:26–45:36, edited for compression):

> *"This is a bunch of technical words, but the concept of it is that there must be a non-locality built into the very structure from which spacetime and gravity are emerging. So like you said, it can't be something naive or simple-minded. It's not just discretizing."*

Followed by his explicit admission of the open problem (45:54):

> *"I don't know what it is, frankly. I think it's sort of beyond my conceptual horizon at this point to be able to do it."*

The Marolf theorem is therefore an explicit constraint that any candidate microscopic theory of spacetime emergence must satisfy, and Jacobson — the founder of thermodynamic gravity — admits the orthodox program has no candidate that does so.

**Theorem 41$'''$ (Same-Qubit-Two-Regions Theorem as McGucken Sphere Apex Content).** *Let q be a spacetime event at which a qubit is prepared. *(SQ2) Two spacelike-separated regions $R_1, R_2 ⊂ \Sigma_+(q)$ both lie on the same Sphere; both access the same phase content $\psi_q$ inherited from the apex.*

*(SQ3) No no-cloning violation occurs because no duplication has occurred. The qubit is a single Sphere-carried object; the "two accesses" are two restrictions of the same Sphere to two regions of spacetime.*

*Proof.* (SQ1) follows directly from Theorem 5 (self-replication): every point on $\Sigma_+(q)$ is a McGucken Point inheriting its phase from q via the Sphere recursion. (SQ2) follows from the Sphere's geometric definition: any region of spacetime touched by $\Sigma_+(q)$ at some time $t > t_q$ accesses the same Sphere content. ### §49.5.5 Hilbert's Sixth Problem (1900) Solved by dx₄/dt = ic

[40, Part IX, §IX.10] establishes that dx₄/dt = ic solves David Hilbert's Sixth Problem of 1900 — the call for an axiomatic foundation for physics in the spirit of Euclid's *Elements* and Newton's *Principia*. The content of the solution, drawn from [40, §IX.10.1] and elaborated in the companion paper [Hilbert6] (the McGucken Sixth Problem paper), has the following form.

**Hilbert's 1900 call.** *"How can the physical sciences be presented as a deductive system based on a small number of axioms, in the way Euclid presented geometry?"* [Hilbert 1900, Problem VI]. The call has stood unanswered for 126 years. The orthodox candidates — Wightman axioms, Haag–Kastler nets, Bohrification, Hilbert-space reconstruction programmes (Hardy 2001, Chiribella–D'Ariano–Perinotti 2011, Masanes–Müller 2011), non-commutative geometry (Connes 1994), twistor theory (Penrose 1967; Woit 2021) — each address part of the call but none supplies the *single mathematical axiom* from which the full edifice of physics descends.

**The McGucken Axiom.** dx₄/dt = ic is a single first-order differential equation expressing a single physical fact: the fourth dimension $x₄$ expands at the velocity $c$ from every spacetime event, with the imaginary unit $i$ encoding the orientation perpendicular to the three spatial directions. From this single axiom, [40] derives:

- **47 numbered theorems of GR and QM** (Parts II–V of [40]), each via two disjoint chains;
- **The Lorentzian metric** $g_{μν} = diag(-c^2, +1, +1, +1)$ (Theorem 11 of the present paper, GR T1 of [40]);
- **The McGucken Operator** $\hat{\mathcal F}_p = \partial_t|_p + ic \partial_{x₄}|_p$ co-generated with the McGucken Space $ℳ_G$ (Theorem 6 of [40]);
- **Hilbert space, canonical commutator, Schrödinger and Dirac equations, gauge bundles, Fock space, operator algebras** (QM theorems of Parts IV–V of [40]);
- **Einstein field equations, Schwarzschild solution, FLRW cosmology, Bekenstein-Hawking entropy, Hawking temperature** (GR theorems of Parts II–III of [40]).

**Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme completed via dual routes.** [40, §IX.10] establishes that the McGucken framework completes Klein's 1872 Erlangen Programme via two independent routes:

- **Route 1 (group-theoretic).** The McGucken Axiom supplies the missing physical generator that selects the relativistic Klein pair $(ISO(1,3), SO^+(1,3))$ from within Klein's group-invariant architecture. This is the *within-Klein* completion.

- **Route 2 (category-theoretic).** The McGucken Axiom goes *beneath* Klein's primitive group-space pair $(G, X)$ and replaces it with the deeper source-pair $(ℳ_G, \hat{\mathcal F})$ co-generated by dx₄/dt = ic. This is the *beneath-Klein* completion.

The two routes terminate in different categorical fields — group theory and category theory, separate research traditions for over a century — yet both completions descend from the same single physical equation. The dual-route Erlangen completion is the categorical analogue of the dual-channel architecture: disjoint mathematical machineries converging on the same physical content.

**Why Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem does not foreclose the Hilbertian goal.** [40, §IX.10] and the companion paper [Hilbert6] address the standard objection that Gödel 1931 forecloses Hilbert's Sixth Problem. The content: Gödel's First Incompleteness Theorem applies to arithmetic-encoding formal systems satisfying his condition $G_3$ (sufficiency to encode Peano arithmetic). The McGucken formal system $L_M$ with proof system $\vdash_M$ does *not* satisfy $G_3$; it is a *geometric-physical* foundation, not an arithmetic-encoding metamathematics. Hilbert's Sixth Problem concerns *physics axiomatization* rather than arithmetic-encoding metamathematics, and is therefore *not subject to Gödel-incompleteness*. The Hilbertian goals (H1) explicit formalisation, (H2) generative completeness over the class $PhysSpace$ of physical-mathematical arenas, and (H5) axiomatic minimality at the absolute floor $C(ℳ_G) = 1$ are precisely the Hilbertian targets a non-arithmetic foundation *can* hit, and dx₄/dt = ic hits all three.

**The closing fact.** After well over a century, Hilbert's Sixth Problem is solved via the McGucken Principle's recognition of the physical fact that the fourth dimension is expanding in a spherically symmetric manner at the velocity of light from every spacetime event. For over 100 years, the academic tradition has taught $x₄ = ict$ as a *notational convenience* for writing the spacetime metric in pseudo-Euclidean form rather than as the integrated kinematic content of an actual physical motion. The McGucken Principle dx₄/dt = ic recognises what is actually physically happening: the fourth dimension is dynamic, advancing at the universal invariant rate $c$, with $i$ encoding the orientation perpendicular to three-space, with wavelength proportional to Planck's constant of action $h$, and the spherical symmetry of $x₄$'s expansion from every event making the McGucken Sphere the kinematic substrate of both QM and GR.

### §50.1 What the Lecture Is Attempting, in Susskind's Own Words

Susskind opens [*Entanglement and Complexity*] with what he calls "a concept that is sort of overtaking physics… it's called Duality" (1:13). The lecture's arc is then explicit at 3:51: at the centre of the explosion of late-20th-century theoretical physics is "on the one hand general relativity and on the other hand Quantum information Theory." Susskind names the relevant fields — quantum field theory, condensed-matter physics, high-temperature superconductors, strange metals, fluid dynamics, non-equilibrium statistical mechanics, chaos theory, error-correcting quantum codes, complexity theory, and black holes — and asserts that "all of these things have been deeply influenced by the same kind of Duality" (5:01).

The lecture then constructs, step by step, a identification:

(L1) **Quantum complexity** (4:54). Feynman 1980: "Why is it so hard to solve quantum mechanical problems? Because Hilbert space is so damn big." A state of $N$ qubits requires $2^N$ complex coefficients; for $N = 400$ this exceeds the storage capacity of the visible universe. (Feynman 1981 [*Simulating physics with computers*, *Int. J. Theor. Phys.* 21, 467]; Susskind's framing at 5:50–7:53 of the lecture.)

(L2) **Entanglement as navigation aid through Hilbert space** (9:14). Patterns of entanglement reduce the effective state space; the entanglement structure becomes a useful coordinate.

(L3) **Tensor networks as bulk geometry** (15:05). Vidal's 2007 multi-scale entanglement renormalisation ansatz (MERA) constructs the ground state of a 1D critical system by an auxiliary bulk Feynman-diagram-like network whose graph distance bounds the entanglement. Susskind quotes 17:25: "The complexity of the state is simply a measure of the smallest tensor Network that can describe that state."

(L4) **Ryu–Takayanagi minimal-surface formula** (26:21). Ryu–Takayanagi 2006 [*Phys. Rev. Lett.* 96, 181602; arXiv:hep-th/0603001]: the entanglement entropy between two regions of the boundary CFT in AdS/CFT equals the area of the minimal bulk surface anchored on their interface, divided by $4G_N$.

(L5) **Tensor-network ≅ AdS bulk** (28:21). Swingle 2009 [*Phys. Rev. D* 86, 065007; arXiv:0905.1317]: the MERA tensor network is a discrete realisation of an AdS spatial slice; the boundary CFT lives on the boundary of the network, the bulk geometry is the tensor-network graph.

(L6) **Black-hole interior grows linearly with time** (33:35). Susskind: "When you solve Einstein's equations… that bag like structure grows. It gets longer and longer and longer." The growth of the Einstein-Rosen interior is dual to the growth of complexity of the boundary thermofield-double state (Stanford–Susskind 2014 [*Phys. Rev. D* 90, 126007; arXiv:1406.2678]; Susskind 2014 [*Fortschr. Phys.* 64, 24; arXiv:1402.5674]).

(L7) **ER = EPR** (43:52). Maldacena–Susskind 2013 [arXiv:1306.0533, *Fortschr. Phys.* 61, 781]: two distant black holes that are quantum-entangled at the level of their Hawking radiation are connected, in the gravitational description, by an Einstein–Rosen bridge through the interior. Susskind: "That is a genuinely new and unexpected principle… something much deeper than we had any idea about 10 years ago."

(L8) **Fast scrambling, butterfly effect, MSS bound** (50:30–1:00:50). Sekino–Susskind 2008 [arXiv:0808.2096]: black holes scramble in time $t_* ~ β \log S/ℏ$. Shenker–Stanford 2013 [*JHEP* 1403, 067; arXiv:1306.0622]: scrambling on the gravity side is butterfly-effect shock-wave growth in the interior. Maldacena–Shenker–Stanford 2015 [arXiv:1503.01409]: the chaos bound $\lambda_L ≤ 2π k_B T/ℏ$, with saturation a diagnostic of holographic gravity duals.

(L10) **Complexity = volume / complexity = action** (1:03:08, in the Q&A): the growth of the Wheeler–DeWitt patch volume (Susskind 2014) or the action (Brown–Roberts–Susskind–Swingle–Zhao 2015–2016 [arXiv:1509.07876; arXiv:1512.04993]) tracks the growth of the boundary CFT state's quantum complexity.

#### §50.2.2 The Boundary-vs-No-Boundary Cosmology Question at 1:12:46 — The "Crutch" Admission

At approximately 1:12:46 of the lecture, a different audience member raises a question that has been a concern of the AdS/CFT programme since its inception:

### §50.8.1 The Pattern: Impasse $→$ Postulate-by-Hand

Orthodox physics has, since the 1920s formulation of quantum mechanics and the 1930s consolidation of general relativity, developed a recurring response to impasse. The pattern has four steps:

**Step 1 (Impasse).** A impasse appears within the existing framework. The impasse takes the form of a tension between two of the framework's cherished commitments — typically between Channel-A content (unitarity, time-reversibility, deterministic evolution, information conservation, algebraic-symmetry generators) and Channel-B content (probability, irreversibility, measurement, information destruction, geometric-propagation structure).

**Step 2 (Diagnosis-by-Postulate).** Rather than diagnose the impasse as the signature of a missing principle from which both Channel-A and Channel-B content descend, the orthodox program diagnoses the impasse as a deficiency in the framework's machinery, to be repaired by the addition of a new postulate.

**Step 3 (Postulate Addition).** A new postulate is added. The postulate is chosen to preserve the cherished Channel-A axiom (typically unitarity) at the cost of new ontological commitments — additional structure that the framework had not previously contained. Examples include unobservable parallel universes (MWI), Planck-scale wormholes connecting every entangled pair (ER = EPR), computational complexity as a bulk geometric quantity (complexity = action / volume), hidden variables with a fitted equilibrium distribution (Bohmian mechanics), stochastic collapse terms with fitted rate constants (GRW / CSL), and modular flow as the source of time (thermal time hypothesis).

**Step 4 (Iteration).** Each new postulate generates its own issues, which are responded to by Steps 1–3 again. The ontology proliferates; the principle recedes. After forty years of iteration, the orthodox program has accumulated a stack of mutually-incompatible postulates, each defended within its own subfield, each violating Newton's Rule I (Corollary 41.5c below) at the methodological level.

The pattern's defining feature is that **the dual-channel reading is never considered**. The orthodox program reads every impasse as a demand for a new postulate within Channel A vocabulary, rather than as the signature that Channel A and Channel B are both valid readings of a single underlying principle. The duality-blindness is the methodological precondition for the postulate-accumulation. The McGucken framework dissolves the pattern by supplying the principle dx₄/dt = ic from which both channels descend as theorems; the postulates the orthodox program adds by hand become forced theorems of the McGucken framework, with no new ontological commitments beyond the single principle.

We catalog the ten most consequential orthodox hand-additions of the modern physics record.
