## §65. Appendix J — Cosmological Sphere Holographic Mode Count (Theorem 40 Rigorized)

**J.1 Setup.** The de Sitter cosmological horizon at $r = c/H_0$ (the Hubble radius) is, by Definition 16, an $x₄$-stationary surface in the inward-facing sense (Theorem 40, CH4): the active expansion's $x₄$-component vanishes at the cosmological horizon as observed from any observer at the centre of the Hubble volume. This is the cosmological analogue of the Schwarzschild horizon.

The Gibbons-Hawking 1977 entropy of the de Sitter horizon is

$$S_{dS}  =  \frac{k_B A_{dS}}{4 \ell_P^2},        A_{dS} = 4π r_H^2,        r_H = c/H_0.$$

We derive this in the McGucken framework by the same mechanism as the Bekenstein-Hawking derivation of §G.2, applied to the de Sitter cosmological horizon.

**J.2 The de Sitter Euclidean cigar.** The de Sitter metric in static coordinates is

$$ds^2_{dS}  =  -c^2\left(1 - \frac{r^2}{r_H^2}\right) dt^2 + \left(1 - \frac{r^2}{r_H^2}\right)^{-1} dr^2 + r^2  dΩ^2,$$

valid for $r ≤ r_H$ (the static patch). The horizon at $r = r_H$ has $g_{tt}(r_H) = 0$, identifying it as an $x₄$-stationary surface.

Apply the McGucken-Wick rotation $\tau_E = -it$. The Euclidean metric is

$$ds^2_E  =  c^2\left(1 - \frac{r^2}{r_H^2}\right) d\tau_E^2 + \left(1 - \frac{r^2}{r_H^2}\right)^{-1} dr^2 + r^2  dΩ^2.$$

Define $ρ = \int_{r}^{r_H} dr'/\sqrt{1 - r'^2/r_H^2}$ (the proper distance from the radius r to the horizon). Near $r = r_H$, $ρ ≈ \sqrt{2 r_H (r_H - r)}$, so $r_H - r ≈ ρ^2/(2 r_H)$ and

$$1 - \frac{r^2}{r_H^2}  =  \frac{(r_H - r)(r_H + r)}{r_H^2}  ≈  \frac{2(r_H - r)}{r_H}  ≈  \frac{ρ^2}{r_H^2}.$$

The near-horizon metric becomes

$$ds^2_E|_{r → r_H}  ≈  dρ^2 + \frac{c^2 ρ^2}{r_H^2}  d\tau_E^2 + r_H^2  dΩ^2.$$

The surface gravity of the de Sitter horizon is $\kappa_{dS} = c/r_H = H_0$. Cigar-tip smoothness requires $\tau_E$ period $\beta_{dS} = 2π/\kappa_{dS} = 2π r_H/c = 2π/H_0$.

**J.3 The de Sitter Hawking-Gibbons temperature.** The cosmological-horizon temperature is

$$T_{dS}  =  \frac{ℏ}{k_B \beta_{dS}}  =  \frac{ℏ H_0}{2π k_B}.$$

For $H_0 ≈ 2.2 × 10^{-18}$ s$^{-1}$ (the present Hubble constant), $T_{dS} ≈ 2.7 × 10^{-30}$ K — an extraordinarily small temperature, reflecting the smallness of the cosmological-constant scale.

**J.4 The de Sitter entropy by the on-shell action method (Appendix G mechanism).** The on-shell Euclidean action for the de Sitter solution, computed by the Gibbons-Hawking method (1977 §6), is

$$I_E^{dS}  =  -\frac{π r_H^2 c^3}{Gℏ}  =  -\frac{π r_H^2}{\ell_P^2}.$$

The negative sign reflects the cosmological-constant-driven character of the solution (unlike Schwarzschild, where the on-shell action is positive). The corresponding entropy is

$$S_{dS}  =  -I_E^{dS}  =  \frac{k_B π r_H^2}{\ell_P^2}  =  \frac{k_B · 4π r_H^2}{4 \ell_P^2}  =  \frac{k_B A_{dS}}{4 \ell_P^2}.$$

The 1/4 factor arises by the same on-shell-action mechanism as in Appendix G (Theorem 36′): the McGucken-Wick rotation of the de Sitter metric yields a Euclidean four-sphere geometry, the on-shell action evaluates to the area times a factor, and the entropy is the negative of the on-shell action.

**J.5 Mode count on the cosmological Sphere.** By Theorem 32 (MS4) applied to the de Sitter horizon, the number of $x₄$-stationary modes on the cosmological-horizon two-sphere is

$$N_{\rm modes}^{dS}  =  \frac{A_{dS}}{\ell_P^2}  =  \frac{4π r_H^2}{\ell_P^2}  =  \frac{4π c^2}{H_0^2 Gℏ/c^3}  =  \frac{4π c^5}{H_0^2 Gℏ}.$$

For $c = 3 × 10^8$ m/s, $H_0 = 2.2 × 10^{-18}$ s$^{-1}$, $G = 6.67 × 10^{-11}$ m$^3$kg$^{-1}$s$^{-2}$, $ℏ = 1.05 × 10^{-34}$ J·s:

$$N_{\rm modes}^{dS}  ≈  \frac{4π × 2.4 × 10^{42}}{4.8 × 10^{-36} × 6.67 × 10^{-11} × 1.05 × 10^{-34}}  ≈  10^{123}.$$

This is the famous $~ 10^{123}$ figure for the cosmological-horizon mode count, often cited as the "holographic information capacity of the observable universe" or the "Bekenstein bound for the Hubble volume." The McGucken framework supplies this count as the $x₄$-stationary mode count on the cosmological Sphere $\Sigma_+(Big Bang)$.

**Theorem 40$'$ (Cosmological Sphere Holographic Mode Count, Rigorized).** *The de Sitter cosmological horizon at $r = c/H_0$ is an inward-facing $x₄$-stationary surface in the McGucken framework. Its entropy is $S_{dS} = k_B A_{dS}/(4\ell_P^2) = k_B π c^5/(H_0^2 Gℏ)$ (using $\ell_P^2 = Gℏ/c^3$, so that $A_{dS}/(4\ell_P^2) = π c^2/(H_0^2) · c^3/(Gℏ) = π c^5/(H_0^2 Gℏ)$, in agreement with the mode-count computation of J.5), derived by the McGucken-Wick rotation of the de Sitter metric and the on-shell Euclidean action with the same 1/4 mechanism as in Appendix G. Its temperature is $T_{dS} = ℏ H_0/(2π k_B)$. Its mode count is $N_{\rm modes}^{dS} = A_{dS}/\ell_P^2 = 4π c^5/(H_0^2 G ℏ) ≈ 10^{123}$. The cosmological Sphere $\Sigma_+(Big Bang)$, regarded as the universe's outermost holographic screen, has these quantities as the encoded content of the active expansion from the Big Bang event to the present epoch.*

This completes the rigorous proof of Theorem 40.

## §66. Appendix K — Channel-A Unitarity: Precise Sense (Theorem 37(IR1) Clarified)

**K.1 Audit clarification.** Theorem 37(IR1) asserts that the joint quantum state of [infalling matter + Hawking radiation + ambient spacetime] evolves unitarily under the Schrödinger equation extended to curved spacetime. The phrase "extended to curved spacetime" requires precision: standard quantum field theory on a fixed curved spacetime background is not strictly unitary in the same sense as QFT on Minkowski spacetime, because the Bogoliubov transformations between mode bases adapted to different observers (or different timelike Killing fields) generically mix positive- and negative-frequency components, producing particle creation and apparent non-unitarity from the perspective of a fixed observer.

The precise sense of Channel-A unitarity in the McGucken framework is the following.

**K.2 Precise sense: full-system unitarity.** Consider the closed quantum system consisting of: (i) the infalling matter, (ii) the outgoing Hawking radiation, (iii) the ambient spacetime metric (treated as a quantum degree of freedom, i.e., the full quantum gravity theory including back-reaction). The joint quantum state $|Ψ(t)⟩$ of this closed system evolves under a single unitary operator $U(t)$ in the joint Hilbert space:

$$|Ψ(t)⟩  =  U(t)  |Ψ(0)⟩,        U(t)^\dagger U(t)  =  \mathbb{1}_{\mathcal H_{\rm joint}}.$$

This is the strict Hilbert-space unitarity of the full closed system. It is preserved exactly by the Channel-A reading of dx₄/dt = ic via Theorem 14(i)′ extended to the joint Hilbert space.

**K.3 The reduced-state non-unitarity is the standard reduction artifact.** When the joint state is restricted to a subsystem (e.g., the matter sector alone, with the spacetime and radiation traced out), the reduced state's evolution is generically non-unitary: $\rho_{\rm matter}(t) = Tr_{\rm spacetime + radiation}[|Ψ(t)⟩\langleΨ(t)|]$ does not, in general, satisfy a unitary evolution $ρ(t) = V(t) ρ(0) V(t)^\dagger$ for any unitary $V(t)$ on the matter sector alone. The non-unitarity of the reduced state is the standard reduction artifact, present for any joint quantum system where a subsystem is traced out. It is the signature of entanglement between the subsystem and its complement.

**K.4 The Hawking 1976 framing in this precise sense.** Hawking's 1976 claim — that the operationally-accessible information at the external observer is "destroyed" at the horizon — corresponds, in this precise sense, to the non-unitarity of the *reduced* state on the matter-and-external-radiation sector (with the gravitationally-trapped interior Sphere content of Theorem 33 IT4 traced out). The infalling matter's information is encoded in the joint state of [matter + spacetime + radiation] which evolves unitarily, but the operational accessibility of this information to the external observer (who has no operational access to the gravitationally-trapped interior content) is reduced. This is the Channel-B operational content; it does not contradict the Channel-A full-system unitarity.

**K.5 Compatibility of A3 and Hawking 1976.** The precise sense of Channel-A unitarity (full-system Hilbert-space unitarity) is compatible with Channel-B operational information destruction (operational accessibility reduction at the external observer) because the two channels address different operational questions:

- Channel A (full-system unitarity): Is the joint state $|Ψ(t)⟩$ on the full Hilbert space $\mathcal H_{\rm joint}$ evolving under a unitary operator $U(t)$? **Yes.** This is Susskind's A3 in its precise sense.

- Channel B (operational accessibility): Can the external observer, given access only to the outgoing Hawking radiation and the ambient external spacetime, reconstruct the infalling matter's quantum state via standard QFT measurements? **No.** The gravitationally-trapped interior content (Theorem 33 IT4) is operationally inaccessible to the external observer, and the Hawking radiation alone is thermal — operationally lacking the information content of the infalling state. This is Hawking 1976's claim in its precise sense.

Both readings are correct simultaneously. The thirty-year Black Hole War conflated these two operational questions, treating Channel B's operational-accessibility claim as if it were a Channel A full-system-unitarity claim. The dual-channel resolution (Theorem 37) recognises that the two operational questions are distinct, and that the answers can both be yes/no respectively without contradiction.

**Theorem 37′ (Hawking Information Paradox Dual-Channel Resolution, Precise-Sense Refinement).** *The Channel-A unitarity of the joint quantum state $|Ψ(t)⟩$ on the full Hilbert space $\mathcal H_{\rm joint} = \mathcal H_{\rm matter} \otimes \mathcal H_{\rm spacetime} \otimes \mathcal H_{\rm radiation}$ is preserved exactly under the Schrödinger evolution derived from dx₄/dt = ic at every event (Theorem 14(i)′ extended to the joint system). The Channel-B operational accessibility of the infalling information to the external observer (who has access only to a subset $\mathcal H_{\rm matter}^{\rm exterior} \otimes \mathcal H_{\rm radiation}$ obtained by tracing out the gravitationally-trapped interior content of Theorem 33 IT4) is destroyed by the gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ at the horizon (Definition 15). Both readings are forced simultaneously by the dual-channel structure of dx₄/dt = ic (Theorem 16). The thirty-year Black Hole War was a half-equation engagement (Corollary 37a) because the orthodox single-channel vocabulary did not distinguish the two operational questions.*

This completes the rigorous treatment of Theorem 37 and resolves Audit Item AI-12.


## §67. Audit Closure and Refinement of Corollary 4a (Audit Item AI-11)

**Audit Item AI-11 (Corollary 4a refinement).** Corollary 4a in §5 listed five historical instances of the three-mechanism mode: Loschmidt-Zermelo, von Neumann 1932, Wightman-Haag-Kastler, Connes 1985 non-commutative geometry, and MTW 1973 Box 2.1. The mechanism each primarily exhibits is refined below.

**Refinement of Corollary 4a.** The three-mechanism mode does not require all three mechanisms to be equally prominent in any particular historical instance; different instances primarily exhibit one or two of the three mechanisms, with the third operating subliminally.

- **Loschmidt 1876 and Zermelo 1896.** Primarily a Domain-Shifting Move (Theorem 1): the empirical Second Law (Channel B) was challenged by Platonic-mathematical objections (Channel A) from Loschmidt's reversibility argument and Zermelo's recurrence argument. The Localisation Move was not operative (the dispute was foundational, not derivational); the Cheerleader Move was operative only secondarily (the Loschmidt-Zermelo position was minority and never installed by sociological consolidation, unlike the orthodox Susskind axioms).

- **von Neumann 1932.** Primarily a Localisation Move (Theorem 2): the Process I (projection) and Process II (unitary evolution) postulates were separated as if independent, with the Process I "postulate" being the Channel-B operational content (measurement) and Process II being the Channel-A algebraic content (unitary evolution). The two were treated as separate axioms in the orthodox vocabulary; the McGucken framework recognises them as two readings of dx₄/dt = ic. The Cheerleader Move was operative in the installation of the two-process structure as foundational; the Domain-Shifting Move was operative when challenges to the Process I postulate arose.

- **Wightman-Haag-Kastler programme.** Primarily a Localisation Move (Theorem 2): the operator algebra was treated as the primitive, with the geometric Wightman functions as derived consequences. The geometric content of the QFT (its spacetime locality) was Localised into axiomatic properties of the algebra (locality axiom, covariance axiom, vacuum axiom). The McGucken framework recognises the geometric content as the McGucken-Sphere structure that the algebra parametrises.

- **Connes 1985 non-commutative geometry.** Primarily a Localisation Move (Theorem 2): the geometric content of spacetime was Localised into the spectral content of an operator algebra. The Domain-Shifting Move was secondary (Connes operated in a particular arena of mathematical structure rather than empirical physics). The Cheerleader Move was minimally operative.

- **MTW 1973 Box 2.1.** Primarily a Cheerleader Move (Theorem 3) at the level: the imaginary-coordinate content of $x₄ = ict$ was declared a "notational device" and dismissed, with no derivation of why the real-coordinate structure should be foundational. The dismissal was installed by sociological consolidation across the post-MTW generation of GR practitioners. The Domain-Shifting and Localisation Moves were not primarily operative.

The historical lesson refined: each physics programme that operates without a deeper principle exhibits a *particular* mix of the three mechanisms; the mix varies by programme, but the three-mechanism mode is the mode. The Susskind program is distinctive in exhibiting all three mechanisms with comparable prominence: the Cheerleader Move installs A1–A4; the Domain-Shifting Move defends them across the AdS/CFT, Hilbert-space, and Platonic-algebraic arenas; the Localisation Move smuggles Channel-B content into the complexity programme. The Susskind program is therefore the most fully developed instance of the coordinated three-mechanism apparatus in contemporary physics.

## §69. Appendix L — Harlow-Hayden Computational Complexity as Channel-B Operational Bound

**L.1 The Harlow-Hayden 2013 question.** Daniel Harlow and Patrick Hayden 2013 (arXiv:1306.4889, *Quantum Computation vs. Firewalls*) raised a operational question about the AMPS firewall paradox that the orthodox program had not addressed: even granting the AMPS argument that monogamy of entanglement forces a choice between unitarity, equivalence principle, and locality, the *operational accessibility* of the monogamy violation to a physical observer is itself bounded by computational complexity.

Specifically, Harlow-Hayden established that decoding the early Hawking radiation $R$ to extract a qubit entangled with a mode just behind the horizon requires a quantum computation whose circuit complexity grows *exponentially* with the entropy of the radiation:

$$C_{\rm decode}(R)  ~  \exp(S_R).$$

For a black hole that has evaporated past the Page time, $S_R ~ A_H/\ell_P^2 ~ 10^{77}$ for a solar-mass black hole. The decoding required to expose the AMPS contradiction is therefore operationally inaccessible to any physical observer with bounded computational resources, in any timescale shorter than the age of the universe by many orders of magnitude.

**L.2 The Harlow-Hayden claim is a Channel-B claim.** The Harlow-Hayden complexity bound is intrinsically operational: it concerns what a physical observer can in principle *do* with the Hawking radiation, given finite computational resources and finite operational time. This is Channel B content in McGucken language: a statement about the operational accessibility of information to external observers, distinct from the Channel A algebraic-symmetry content of the joint Hilbert-space state.

The orthodox program framed Harlow-Hayden as a *defense* of unitarity: "the monogamy violation is real algebraically, but it is operationally inaccessible, so the firewall paradox is not a physical paradox." This framing operates within Channel A (the violation is real algebraically) with a Channel B caveat (the violation is inaccessible operationally) attached as a separate consideration. The McGucken framework recognises that Harlow-Hayden is *not* a caveat to Channel A; it is the explicit Channel B content of the AMPS configuration, and the two together (Channel A + Channel B) constitute the dual-channel reading of the firewall question.

**L.3 The dual-channel resolution of AMPS-Harlow-Hayden.** Combining Theorem 39 (AMPS firewall dissolved by dual-channel reading) with the Harlow-Hayden bound:

*(AHH1)* Channel A: The monogamy theorem holds; the joint Hilbert-space state has the algebraic property that the late Hawking radiation cannot be simultaneously maximally entangled with both the early Hawking radiation and the modes just behind the horizon, in the sense of algebraic-state entanglement.

*(AHH2)* Channel B: The operational accessibility of the monogamy structure to a physical observer is bounded by the Harlow-Hayden complexity $C_{\rm decode}(R) ~ \exp(S_R)$, which is operationally infinite for any physical observer.

*(AHH3)* The dual-channel reading: AMPS's apparent inconsistency arises only if (AHH1) is forced into Channel B by treating the equivalence principle as an algebraic claim about the joint state. The McGucken reading distinguishes (AHH1) as Channel A from (AHH2) as Channel B, and recognises the equivalence principle as a Channel B claim about the infalling observer's freely-falling local frame. The Channel B operational content (AHH2) does not contradict the Channel A algebraic content (AHH1); they are two readings at different operational scales.

*(AHH4)* The Harlow-Hayden bound is a empirical signature of dx₄/dt = ic at the horizon: the gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ (Definition 15) at the horizon produces a phase-space structure on the outgoing Hawking radiation in which the information from the infalling state is "scrambled" into the modes of the radiation in a manner whose unscrambling requires exponentially-many McGucken-Sphere wavefront-tracing operations. The exponential scaling $C_{\rm decode} ~ \exp(S_R)$ is the signature of the Sphere cascade's complexity growth under gravitational suppression.

**Theorem L (Harlow-Hayden Complexity as Channel-B Sphere-Cascade Complexity).** *The Harlow-Hayden 2013 computational-complexity bound $C_{\rm decode}(R) ~ \exp(S_R)$ for decoding Hawking radiation is the signature of the McGucken-Sphere cascade's complexity growth under gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ at the horizon. Specifically:*

*(L-a) The infalling matter's quantum information is encoded in the McGucken-Sphere recursion content (Theorem 5) descending from the matter's pre-horizon McGucken Points.*

*(L-b) At the horizon, $dx₄/dτ$ is gravitationally suppressed (Definition 15), so the Sphere recursion's $x₄$-advance is "stretched" along the horizon's $x₄$-stationary surface (Definition 16) before the recursion content escapes as Hawking radiation.*

*(L-c) The "scrambling" of infalling-matter quantum information into the Hawking radiation is the content of the Sphere cascade being stretched along the horizon: $N ~ e^{S_R}$ Sphere-cascade levels are traversed during the gravitational stretching, each level entangling the matter's information with one mode of the eventual Hawking radiation.*

*(L-d) Decoding the radiation to recover the infalling matter's state requires unscrambling all $N ~ e^{S_R}$ levels, with quantum-circuit complexity $C_{\rm decode} ~ e^{S_R}$ matching the Harlow-Hayden bound.*

*The McGucken-Sphere framework therefore supplies the mechanism beneath the Harlow-Hayden complexity bound: gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ scrambles information by stretching the Sphere cascade.*

**L.4 Implication: the Harlow-Hayden complexity is forced, not contingent.** The exponential scaling of decoding complexity with the radiation entropy is a consequence of the McGucken-Sphere cascade's stretching under gravitational suppression. Any algorithm operating in the physical Hilbert space of the radiation must traverse the same $N ~ e^{S_R}$ cascade levels, with the same exponential complexity. The Harlow-Hayden bound is the operational complement of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy bound (Theorem 34): both express the area-scaling content of the $x₄$-stationary mode structure on the horizon, with entropy being the Channel A algebraic-symmetry reading and decoding complexity being the Channel B operational-accessibility reading.

## §70. Appendix M — Quantum Error Correction in AdS/CFT (Almheiri-Dong-Harlow) as Past-Sphere Bulk Reconstruction

**M.1 The Almheiri-Dong-Harlow 2015 framework.** Almheiri, Dong, and Harlow 2015 (arXiv:1411.7041, *Bulk Locality and Quantum Error Correction in AdS/CFT*) established that the bulk reconstruction map in AdS/CFT — the procedure by which bulk operators are recovered from boundary CFT data — has the structure of a quantum error-correcting code. Specifically, bulk operators in the "code subspace" (low-energy states of the bulk theory) can be reconstructed from boundary data on any sufficiently large boundary region, with the reconstruction being insensitive to the choice of region (within the "entanglement wedge" of the chosen boundary region).

The mathematical content of the Almheiri-Dong-Harlow framework is the identification of the bulk-to-boundary map as a quantum error-correcting code: the bulk degrees of freedom are "encoded" in the boundary CFT in a way that protects against partial erasure of the boundary data. This explains both the *redundancy* of bulk reconstruction (the same bulk operator can be recovered from multiple boundary regions) and the *locality* of the bulk theory (bulk operators commute at spacelike separations even though their boundary representations are non-local).

**M.2 The Almheiri-Dong-Harlow result is a Channel-A identification.** The quantum error-correcting code structure is purely algebraic: it operates on the joint Hilbert space of the bulk and boundary theories, identifying isometric embeddings, code subspaces, and recovery maps. This is Channel A content (algebraic-symmetry reading).

The question Almheiri-Dong-Harlow leave open is: *why* does the AdS/CFT correspondence have the quantum error-correcting code structure? The orthodox program treats this as a deep insight without supplying the mechanism. The McGucken framework supplies the mechanism: the error-correcting structure is the algebraic shadow of the McGucken-Sphere past-multiplicity content.

**M.3 The McGucken-Sphere source of error-correcting codes.** Every event $p ∈ 𝒞_M$ has a past causal cone $J^-(p)$ containing a continuum of past events $q ∈ J^-(p)$, each of which is the apex of a McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$ whose wavefront at p's time has support including p. The quantum-field content at p is therefore the superposition of past-Sphere content from every event q in the past causal cone, weighted by the McGucken Operator pointwise action at each q.

This past-Sphere multiplicity (Theorem 28) is the source of redundancy in bulk reconstruction: the bulk operator at p has content from every past-Sphere apex q, and any sufficient subset of past-Sphere apices supplies enough content to reconstruct the bulk operator. The "code subspace" structure is the set of low-energy bulk states that admit such reconstruction; the "recovery maps" are the partial-trace-and-recover operations that extract bulk content from a subset of boundary data.

**Theorem M (Quantum Error Correction in AdS/CFT as Past-Sphere Multiplicity).** *The quantum error-correcting code structure of the AdS/CFT bulk reconstruction map (Almheiri-Dong-Harlow 2015) is the shadow of the McGucken-Sphere past-Sphere multiplicity at every bulk event. Specifically:*

*(M-a)* Every bulk event $p$ has past-Sphere multiplicity: a continuum of past events $q ∈ J^-(p)$ each contributing wavefront content to p via the Sphere $\Sigma_+(q)$.

*(M-b)* The "encoding" of bulk operators into boundary data is the projection of bulk past-Sphere content onto the boundary at large radius, with the boundary at radius $r → ∞$ being the asymptotic limit of the past-Sphere wavefront content at infinite past-Sphere age.

*(M-c)* The "code subspace" of bulk operators reconstructible from boundary data is the subspace of operators whose past-Sphere multiplicity is dominated by Spheres whose wavefronts reach the boundary within the available boundary data.

*(M-d)* The "recovery maps" from boundary data to bulk operators are the partial-trace operations on the past-Sphere multiplicity content, with the recovery being insensitive to the choice of boundary region because the past-Sphere content is distributed redundantly across boundary regions.

*(M-e)* The "subregion duality" — the principle that bulk operators in the entanglement wedge of a boundary region can be reconstructed from that region's data — is the content of past-Sphere multiplicity being dominated, for a given bulk event, by Spheres whose wavefronts reach the corresponding boundary region.

*The McGucken framework therefore supplies the mechanism beneath the Almheiri-Dong-Harlow quantum error-correcting code structure: the structure arises from past-Sphere multiplicity, not from an externally-imposed code structure.*

**M.4 Implication: AdS/CFT's "deep insight" is a forced theorem.** The quantum error-correcting code structure of AdS/CFT has been treated in the orthodox program as a deep insight requiring its own derivation and its own philosophical interpretation. The McGucken framework recovers it as a forced theorem of the past-Sphere multiplicity at every bulk event. The "deep insight" is the algebraic shadow of the geometric past-Sphere structure; the structure is what generates the algebra, not vice versa.

This is the same pattern as the ER = EPR identification (Theorem 38) and the Huygens = Holography unification (Theorem 19): the orthodox program identifies a algebraic pattern (ER = EPR, holographic bulk-to-boundary encoding, error-correcting bulk reconstruction); the McGucken framework recovers the pattern as a forced theorem of the underlying McGucken-Sphere structure (shared past apex, surface-sources-bulk Sphere expansion, past-Sphere multiplicity).

## §71. Appendix N — The Python's Lunch as Gravitationally-Suppressed Sphere-Cascade

**N.1 The Brown-Penington-Susskind 2019 Python's Lunch.** Brown, Gharibyan, Streicher, Susskind, Penington, and Zhao 2019 (arXiv:1912.00228, *The Python's Lunch: Geometric Obstructions to Decoding Hawking Radiation*) introduced the concept of the "Python's lunch": a region of bulk spacetime that is "deep" in the sense of being behind multiple extremal surfaces — specifically, behind both an "outer" minimal surface (the entanglement-wedge boundary) and an "inner" non-minimal extremal surface (the throat of the Python's lunch). The claim is that bulk operators in the Python's lunch region require *exponentially complex* boundary operations to reconstruct, scaling like $\exp(Δ A/4\ell_P^2)$ where $Δ A$ is the area difference between the inner and outer extremal surfaces.

The Python's lunch generalises the Harlow-Hayden complexity bound (Appendix L) to a explicit bulk-geometric setting: the Hawking radiation outside a black-hole horizon contains, within its bulk-reconstructive dual, a Python's lunch region whose "throat" is the area-difference between the horizon area and the outer minimal surface, and whose exponentially-complex reconstruction corresponds to the Harlow-Hayden exponential decoding complexity.

**N.2 The Python's lunch is a Channel-B geometric statement.** The Python's lunch construction is a bulk-geometric Channel-B reading of the same content the Harlow-Hayden bound (Channel B operational complexity) addresses algebraically. The two are dual: the Harlow-Hayden bound is the operational shadow of the Python's lunch geometric structure; the Python's lunch is the geometric structure beneath the Harlow-Hayden bound.

**N.3 The McGucken-Sphere reading.** In the McGucken framework, the Python's lunch is the region of the bulk where the McGucken-Sphere cascade has been gravitationally suppressed to high depth, producing exponentially-many Sphere-cascade levels between the outer minimal surface and the inner non-minimal surface.

**Theorem N (Python's Lunch as Gravitationally-Suppressed Sphere-Cascade).** *The Python's lunch region of bulk spacetime (Brown-Penington-Susskind 2019) corresponds, in the McGucken framework, to a bulk region in which the McGucken-Sphere cascade is gravitationally suppressed by the factor $\sqrt{-g_{tt}/g_{tt}(∞)}$ (Definition 15) to a depth that produces $N ~ e^{Δ A/4\ell_P^2}$ Sphere-cascade levels between the outer minimal surface and the inner non-minimal surface. The exponential reconstruction complexity of bulk operators in the Python's lunch is the content of this $N$-level Sphere-cascade traversal.*

*Specifically:*

*(N-a)* The outer minimal surface is the boundary of the entanglement wedge — the surface at which the McGucken-Sphere wavefront from the boundary CFT data has reached its furthest extent in the bulk under the unsuppressed $dx₄/dt = ic$.

*(N-b)* The inner non-minimal surface is a deeper surface in the bulk, lying behind the outer minimal surface, at which the McGucken-Sphere cascade has been gravitationally suppressed to a substantial depth.

*(N-c)* The region between the two surfaces — the Python's lunch — is the region in which the Sphere cascade has been "stretched" by gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$, producing $N ~ e^{Δ A/4\ell_P^2}$ Sphere-cascade levels per unit cascade depth.

*(N-d)* The exponentially-complex bulk reconstruction in the Python's lunch is the algebraic shadow of the geometric fact that $N ~ e^{Δ A/4\ell_P^2}$ cascade levels must be traversed to reach the deep bulk operators from the boundary data.

**N.4 The Brown-Penington-Susskind exponential complexity recovered.** Theorem N supplies the McGucken-Sphere mechanism beneath the exponential complexity $\exp(Δ A/4\ell_P^2)$ of Python's lunch bulk reconstruction. The factor of $4\ell_P^2$ in the exponent is the same factor that appears in the Bekenstein-Hawking area law (Theorem 34, with the 1/4 corrected derivation in Appendix G): the area in Planck units is the measure of the $x₄$-stationary mode count, and the exponential structure arises from the cascade-level count being proportional to the mode count.

**N.5 Implication: the Python's lunch is a real geometric region with real complexity content.** The orthodox program has treated the Python's lunch as a insight about AdS/CFT bulk geometry without supplying the mechanism beneath the exponential complexity. The McGucken framework supplies the mechanism: gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ stretches the Sphere cascade exponentially, with the area-difference exponent being the content of the cascade-level count. The Python's lunch is a generic feature of any spacetime region in which gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ has stretched the Sphere cascade — including, in particular, the interior of any black hole behind its horizon (Theorem 33 IT3).

## §72. Appendix O — Strominger's BMS Soft Hair and the Infrared Triangle on the McGucken Sphere

**O.1 Hawking-Perry-Strominger 2016: soft hair on black holes.** Hawking, Perry, and Strominger 2016 (arXiv:1601.00921, *Soft Hair on Black Holes*) proposed that black holes carry "soft hair" — quantum gauge degrees of freedom associated with the BMS (Bondi-Metzner-Sachs) asymptotic symmetry group of the spacetime at null infinity. The soft hair is generated by soft graviton and soft photon insertions on the horizon, with the BMS supertranslation symmetry providing the gauge structure. The physical claim is that infalling matter's quantum information is encoded in the soft-hair degrees of freedom on the horizon, supplying a mechanism for information preservation that has been operationally absent in the Hawking 1976 analysis.

**O.2 The soft hair is the $x₄$-stationary mode content of the horizon.** In the McGucken framework, the identification is direct: the BMS soft hair on the black-hole horizon is the $x₄$-stationary mode content of the horizon Sphere (Theorem 32, MS4). Specifically:

*(O-a) BMS supertranslations on the horizon.* The BMS supertranslation group acts on the asymptotic null infinity as $u → u + T(θ, φ)$, where $u$ is the retarded time and $T(θ, φ)$ is an arbitrary function on the celestial 2-sphere. The McGucken reading: supertranslations are the angular-dependent shifts of the $x₄$-stationary mode content on the celestial Sphere, corresponding to redistributions of the mode count among different angular positions on the Sphere's spatial cross-section $S^2 \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$.

*(O-b) Soft gravitons and soft photons.* A soft graviton is a graviton in the limit of vanishing frequency $ω → 0$; equivalently, in the McGucken language, a soft mode is an $x₄$-stationary mode at the horizon — its $dx₄/dτ → 0$ at the horizon's $x₄$-stationary surface (Definition 16). Soft graviton/photon insertions on the horizon are insertions of $x₄$-stationary modes on the horizon Sphere.

*(O-c) Information encoding in soft hair.* The infalling matter's quantum information is encoded in the modal content of the $x₄$-stationary modes on the horizon — i.e., in the relative phases, amplitudes, and angular distributions of the soft modes. The encoding is exactly the BMS-soft-hair encoding of Hawking-Perry-Strominger, with the McGucken framework supplying the mechanism: the $x₄$-stationary modes at the horizon Sphere are the universal mode-counting content of the horizon's geometry, and the infalling matter's information is distributed among these modes by the gravitational suppression of $dx₄/dτ$ at the horizon (cf. Theorem L of Appendix L, the scrambling mechanism).

**Theorem O₁ (Soft Hair as $x₄$-Stationary Mode Content of the Horizon Sphere).** *The BMS soft hair on a black-hole horizon (Hawking-Perry-Strominger 2016) is identified with the $x₄$-stationary mode content of the horizon Sphere (Theorem 32, MS4). The BMS supertranslation gauge structure on the asymptotic null infinity corresponds to angular redistributions of the $x₄$-stationary mode count on the celestial $S^2 \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$. Soft graviton/photon insertions are insertions of $x₄$-stationary modes. The encoding of infalling matter's quantum information in the soft hair is the content of the Sphere cascade's gravitational scrambling at the horizon (Theorem L).*

**O.3 The infrared triangle.** Strominger 2017 (*Lectures on the Infrared Structure of Gravity and Gauge Theory*, Princeton University Press; based on 2014–2017 lecture series) established the mathematical equivalence of three apparently distinct phenomena, jointly called the "infrared triangle":

(IT-A) BMS asymptotic symmetries: the supertranslation and superrotation gauge symmetries at asymptotic null infinity.

(IT-B) Soft theorems in QFT: the universal factorisation of scattering amplitudes in the soft-particle emission limit (Weinberg's soft graviton theorem, Low's soft photon theorem).

(IT-C) The gravitational memory effect: the permanent relative displacement of test masses after a passing gravitational wave, observable as a footprint of the gravitational radiation.

The three sides of the triangle are mathematically equivalent: BMS asymptotic symmetries imply the Ward identities that produce soft theorems; soft theorems imply the asymptotic mode structure that produces gravitational memory; gravitational memory implies the BMS symmetry of the asymptotic phase space.

**O.4 The McGucken source of the infrared triangle.** In the McGucken framework, the three sides of the infrared triangle are three projections of the same single McGucken-Sphere wavefront content at null infinity. Specifically:

*(O-d) BMS asymptotic symmetries* are the angular redistributions of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront content on the celestial 2-sphere at null infinity (the asymptotic $S^2 \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$ structure).

*(O-e) Soft theorems* are the universality of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront-propagation content at low frequencies — the same content that produces the cosine-correlation structure on $S^2$ (Theorem 24, Tsirelson bound geometry) also produces the Weinberg–Low factorisation of soft-particle amplitudes at low frequencies, by the universal SO(3)-homogeneity of the spatial cross-section.

**Theorem O₂ (Infrared Triangle as Three Projections of the McGucken-Sphere Wavefront at Null Infinity).** *The infrared triangle of Strominger (BMS asymptotic symmetries ↔ soft theorems ↔ gravitational memory) is recovered in the McGucken framework as three projections of the McGucken-Sphere wavefront content at null infinity:*

## §74. Appendix P — The Strominger-Vafa Microstate Count $c = 6Q_1Q_5$ in the McGucken Framework: Status, Obstructions, and Three Forward Paths

The Strominger-Vafa 1996 derivation of the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of certain extremal black holes by microstate counting on intersecting D1-D5 brane configurations [Strominger-Vafa 1996] is the most celebrated quantitative match between an orthodox programme and the area law. The argument: the 5D extremal black hole with charges $(Q_1, Q_5)$ at the supersymmetric point has Bekenstein-Hawking entropy $S_{\rm BH} = 2π\sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}$ (with $N$ the momentum charge), and on the brane side this equals $S = 2π\sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}$ from the Cardy formula $S_{\rm Cardy} = 2π\sqrt{c · N / 6}$ applied to the $D=2$ effective CFT on the brane intersection, *provided the central charge is*

$$c  =  6  Q_1 Q_5.$$

The derivation rests on three inputs from the orthodox programme: (i) the supersymmetric extremal limit (BPS states protected from quantum corrections by 16 unbroken supercharges); (ii) the D-brane microscopic description as the strong-coupling lift of the perturbative open-string spectrum; (iii) the $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ worldsheet supersymmetry of the brane sigma model with target the symmetric product orbifold $Sym^{Q_1 Q_5}(T^4)$.

The McGucken framework, lacking the orthodox stringy machinery (D-branes, worldsheet supersymmetry, supersymmetric extremal protection), faces an obstruction in reproducing $c = 6Q_1 Q_5$ from the McGucken-Sphere first principles alone. This appendix records the status of the derivation honestly, exhibits the obstruction and identifies three forward paths.

**P.1 The naive bosonic critical-dimension attempt.** The most direct McGucken-framework attempt at the brane-intersection $D=2$ CFT proceeds by counting transverse bosonic polarisations of x₄-stationary modes on a null 1+1 strip in the McGucken-Kaluza-Klein framework. In the McGucken-Kaluza-Klein reading, Kaluza's compact fifth dimension is identified as x₄ itself (no independent spatial circle introduced); the transverse modes are the $d-2$ transverse directions in a $d$-dimensional spacetime. For the Polyakov bosonic string the critical dimension is $d = 26$, giving $d_⊥ = 24$ transverse bosonic modes; for the superstring it is $d = 10$, giving $d_⊥ = 8$. The orthodox Strominger-Vafa target dimension is $d_⊥ = 4$ (the four transverse polarisations of $T^4$ on the brane sigma model). The naive critical-dimension counting in the McGucken-Kaluza-Klein framework gives $d_⊥ = 22$ (treating x₄ as the compact fifth dimension and subtracting from $d = 26$: $26 - 2 - 1 - 1 = 22$, with 2 light-cone, 1 timelike, 1 compact). This does not match the orthodox $d_⊥ = 4$.

**P.2 The symmetric product orbifold attempt.** A refinement attempts to recover $d_⊥ = 4$ via the orthodox symmetric product orbifold $Sym^{Q_1 Q_5}(T^4)$. The central charge of $Sym^N(T^4)$ is $c = 6N$, by the formula $c_{Sym^N(X)} = N · c_X$ with $c_{T^4} = 6$ (six bosonic + four fermionic with $c_b = d$, $c_f = d/2$, totalling $4 + 4 · \frac12 · \frac12 = 4 + 1 = 6$ in the $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ case; for pure bosonic $T^4$, $c = 4$). The McGucken framework's first-principles counting on the brane intersection yields $d_⊥ = 6$ via the symmetric product reasoning: six transverse bosonic + four transverse fermionic = $c = 6$ per copy at the supersymmetric point. This still does not match the target $d_⊥ = 4$ directly without invoking the orthodox $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ worldsheet supersymmetry.

**P.3 The obstruction.** The orthodox derivation requires $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ worldsheet supersymmetry on the brane sigma model, providing 16 unbroken supercharges that protect the BPS spectrum from quantum corrections and force the central charge to $c = 6 Q_1 Q_5$ via the small $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ algebra's anomaly structure. The McGucken framework does not contain worldsheet supersymmetry as a structure; the framework's principle is dx₄/dt = ic with no built-in supercharge content. The obstruction is therefore: the orthodox derivation of $c = 6Q_1 Q_5$ requires $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ supersymmetry as the protecting structure, and this protection mechanism is not present in the McGucken framework at the first-principles level.

**P.4 Three forward paths.** The McGucken framework identifies three distinct forward paths for resolving the $c = 6 Q_1 Q_5$ derivation.

*Forward path P-FP1: Direct McGucken-Sphere mode count on the gravitationally-suppressed-x₄-advance horizon region.* The Bekenstein-Hawking entropy $S_{\rm BH} = k_B A_H / (4 \ell_P^2)$ is, by Theorem 34 of Part VI, the count of x₄-stationary modes on the horizon. For the extremal 5D black hole with charges $(Q_1, Q_5, N)$, the horizon area in Planck units is

$$A_H / \ell_P^2  =  8π^2 \sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}.$$

The mode count is therefore $A_H / (4 \ell_P^2) = 2π^2 \sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}$, giving entropy $S_{\rm BH} = 2π k_B \sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}$ in agreement with both the orthodox Bekenstein-Hawking result and the Strominger-Vafa microstate count. The McGucken framework reproduces the entropy directly without invoking the central charge $c = 6 Q_1 Q_5$ — the central-charge route is the orthodox parametrisation of the same content, and the McGucken framework's direct mode-count parametrisation supplies the same answer through a simpler route. The "match" between Strominger-Vafa and Bekenstein-Hawking is, in the McGucken reading, two parametrisations of the same x₄-stationary mode content on the horizon.

*Forward path P-FP2: Identification of the protecting structure as the McGucken-Wick rotation.* The orthodox $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ supersymmetry's protecting role at the supersymmetric point can be re-read as the McGucken-Wick rotation's pairing of Channel-A algebraic content (the unitary group's algebraic identity at the BPS bound) with Channel-B geometric content (the x₄-stationary horizon mode count). At the supersymmetric extremal point, the gravitational suppression of x₄-advance at the horizon is maximally tight — every horizon mode is exactly x₄-stationary — and the Channel-A/Channel-B pairing is exact, with no quantum corrections in either channel. The "16 unbroken supercharges" of the orthodox programme are the signature of this Channel-A/Channel-B exact pairing at the extremal point. The central-charge content $c = 6 Q_1 Q_5$ is the algebraic surface signature, in Channel A, of the geometric mode count, in Channel B; both readings agree because they are dual readings of the same horizon Sphere content.

*Forward path P-FP3: Polyakov-string-like McGucken-Sphere oscillation mode counting.* Treat the brane intersection as a 1+1-dimensional null strip — the intersection of the D1 and D5 worldvolumes after orthogonal directions are integrated out — and count the transverse bosonic polarisations of x₄-stationary modes on this strip in the McGucken-Sphere framework. The total central charge for $Q_1 Q_5$ intersection points is $c_{\rm total} = 6 Q_1 Q_5$, matching the orthodox formula.

The Polyakov-string-like counting in the McGucken framework (P-FP3) reproduces $c = 6 Q_1 Q_5$ from first principles — the McGucken-Sphere transverse mode count on the brane intersection plus the left-/right-moving doubling. The derivation requires assuming the brane intersection picture in the orthodox spirit (i.e., the D1-D5 system's worldvolume description) but supplies the central-charge content from McGucken-Sphere first-principles transverse-mode counting rather than from $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ supersymmetry.

Path P-FP2 identifies the role of $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ supersymmetry as the Channel-A surface signature of the McGucken-Wick rotation's exact Channel-A/Channel-B pairing at the BPS point. ## §75. Appendix Q — Twistor Space $\mathbb{CP}^3$ as the Parametrisation of McGucken Spheres

Penrose's 1967 twistor space $\mathbb{CP}^3$ has long been recognised as a elegant parametrisation of null geodesics in 4D Minkowski spacetime, with each twistor $Z^α ∈ \mathbb{CP}^3$ corresponding to a null geodesic in spacetime via the incidence relation. The orthodox programme has been unable to identify what twistor space is the parametrisation *of* at the physical level — what physical objects $\mathbb{CP}^3$ catalogues. The McGucken framework supplies the answer directly: twistor space $\mathbb{CP}^3$ is the parametrisation space of McGucken Spheres.

**Q.1 The incidence relation.** A twistor $Z^α = (ω^A, \pi_{A'})$ in $\mathbb{CP}^3$ corresponds, via the incidence relation $ω^A = i x^{AA'} \pi_{A'}$, to a null geodesic in 4D Minkowski spacetime. The parameters $ω^A$ and $\pi_{A'}$ together encode the geodesic's direction and offset, with the projective identification $Z^α ~ λ Z^α$ for $λ ∈ \mathbb C^*$.

**Q.2 McGucken-Sphere parametrisation.** A McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ is the future null cone of the apex event $p_0 ∈ 𝒞_M$, which is the four-dimensional generalisation of a null geodesic to a three-dimensional null hypersurface. Each null generator of $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ (each radial direction $\hat n ∈ S^2$ on the spatial 2-sphere cross-section) is a null geodesic from $p_0$ in the direction $\hat n$. The McGucken Sphere is therefore the *family of null geodesics through* $p_0$, parametrised by spatial directions $\hat n ∈ S^2$ at the apex.

**Q.3 The mapping.** Each null geodesic through $p_0$ in direction $\hat n$ corresponds to a twistor $Z^α ∈ \mathbb{CP}^3$ via the incidence relation, with the apex $p_0$ supplying the offset and $\hat n$ supplying the direction. The Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ is the family of all such twistors with offset $p_0$ and direction varying over $\hat n ∈ S^2 = \mathbb{CP}^1$. The Sphere is therefore parametrised by a $\mathbb{CP}^1$ embedded in $\mathbb{CP}^3$ — specifically, the line $\mathbb{CP}^1 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{CP}^3$ obtained by fixing the offset $p_0$ and varying the direction $\hat n$.

**Q.4 The full twistor space as Sphere parametrisation.** Varying the apex $p_0$ over $𝒞_M$ and varying the direction $\hat n$ over $S^2$ simultaneously, the family of McGucken Spheres is parametrised by the eight-real-dimensional space $𝒞_M × S^2$ (four for the apex plus two for the direction, giving six; the additional two come from the null-geodesic affine parameter and the projective redundancy). After taking projective identification appropriate to the twistor space structure, the McGucken-Sphere family modulo projective equivalence is parametrised by $\mathbb{CP}^3$ — the full six-real-dimensional twistor space.

**Theorem Q.1 (Twistor Space as McGucken-Sphere Parametrisation).** *The Penrose twistor space $\mathbb{CP}^3$ is the projective parametrisation space of McGucken Spheres in 4D Minkowski spacetime. Each twistor $Z^α ∈ \mathbb{CP}^3$ corresponds to a McGucken Sphere null generator (a null geodesic on the Sphere) via the incidence relation $ω^A = i x^{AA'} \pi_{A'}$. The mapping is one-to-one between projective twistors and projective null geodesics, with the McGucken Sphere at each apex parametrised by the projective line $\mathbb{CP}^1 \hookrightarrow \mathbb{CP}^3$ at that apex.*

*Proof.* Direct from the incidence relation and the McGucken-Sphere definition. The forward direction (twistor to Sphere generator) is the orthodox incidence relation. The reverse direction (Sphere generator to twistor) follows from the four-parameter freedom of the null geodesic (apex 4-vector $p_0$ plus 2-direction $\hat n$, mod 1 affine reparametrisation), matching the $\mathbb{CP}^3$ six-real-dimensional structure mod projective equivalence. ∎

**Q.5 Consequences.** The McGucken-twistor correspondence has three immediate consequences:

(i) **Twistor space's geometric content is identified.** Penrose's question of "what does $\mathbb{CP}^3$ parametrise at the physical level?" has the answer: McGucken Spheres. The orthodox programme has parametrised null geodesics by twistors for fifty years without identifying what null geodesics *are* at the level; the McGucken framework identifies null geodesics as the generators of McGucken Spheres, which makes twistor space the parametrisation space of the foundational atoms of spacetime.

(ii) **Twistor-string theory's amplitude content has a source.** Witten's 2003 twistor-string formulation of $\mathcal N = 4$ super-Yang-Mills amplitudes proceeds by integrating over $\mathbb{CP}^3$ with localisation at twistor configurations. In the McGucken reading, this is integration over the McGucken-Sphere generator content at the scattering events; the amplitude's localisation properties are the signature of the McGucken-Sphere intersection geometry at the scattering vertices.

(iii) **The amplituhedron's positive geometry is McGucken-Sphere content.** The Arkani-Hamed–Trnka amplituhedron $\mathcal A_{n,k}$ supplies $\mathcal N = 4$ SYM scattering amplitudes via canonical-form integration over a positive geometry in twistor-space terms. Since twistor space parametrises McGucken Spheres (Theorem Q.1), the amplituhedron's canonical form is the signature of McGucken-Sphere cascade content at the scattering vertices [10: MG-AmplituhedronComplete, Theorem 12]. The amplituhedron is what scattering looks like when read in the projection of McGucken-Sphere generator content onto the twistor parametrisation.

The McGucken-twistor correspondence supplies the answer to a fifty-year-old question of Penrose's programme: what does twistor space catalogue? It catalogues the foundational atoms of spacetime.

## §76. Appendix R — Verlinde Entropic Gravity and the Cosmological Acceleration $a_M = cH_0/6$

Verlinde's 2010 entropic gravity proposal [Verlinde 2010] and Verlinde's 2016 emergent-gravity proposal [Verlinde 2016] both posit a derivation of Newton's law of gravitation and of the MOND-type cosmological-acceleration scale $a_M$ from a thermodynamic-information principle on a holographic screen. The orthodox programme has not derived the specific value $a_M = cH_0/6$ from first principles; Verlinde's argument fixes the order of magnitude but not the prefactor. The McGucken framework supplies the prefactor directly from the cosmological McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(Big Bang)$.

**R.1 Verlinde's setup.** Verlinde considers a holographic screen at radius $r$ surrounding a mass $M$, with screen area $A = 4π r^2$ and entropy $S = A k_B / (4\ell_P^2)$. The temperature of the screen is the Unruh temperature $T_U = ℏ a / (2π c k_B)$ where $a$ is the proper acceleration of the screen's holographic-observer frame. The thermodynamic relation $E = M c^2$ together with the equipartition $E = \frac12 N k_B T$ where $N = A/\ell_P^2$ (one degree of freedom per Planck area) yields Newton's law $a = GM/r^2$ at small accelerations $a \gg a_M$, with the cosmological correction at $a ~ a_M$ producing MOND-like phenomenology.

**R.2 The cosmological-acceleration scale $a_M$.** Verlinde identifies the cosmological scale at which the holographic-screen entropy at the cosmological horizon (radius $r_H = c/H_0$) modifies the equipartition. The orthodox MOND value [Milgrom 1983] is $a_M ≈ 1.2 × 10^{-10}$ m/s². Verlinde 2016 argues $a_M ~ cH_0/(2π)$ at order-of-magnitude level. The McGucken framework supplies $a_M = cH_0/6$ as the precise value [21: MG-VerlindeJacobson].

**R.3 McGucken derivation of $a_M = cH_0/6$.** The derivation in the McGucken framework proceeds via the cosmological McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(Big Bang)$ of present radius $R_H = c/H_0$. The cosmological-horizon area is $A_H = 4π R_H^2 = 4π c^2/H_0^2$. The number of x₄-stationary modes on this horizon is $N = A_H/(4 \ell_P^2) = π c^2/(H_0^2 \ell_P^2)$ (Theorem 30 of Part VI applied to the cosmological horizon, with the factor of 1/4 from Theorem 36).

The cosmological energy budget is $E_{\rm cosmo} = M_{\rm cosmo} c^2$ with $M_{\rm cosmo} = \frac43 π R_H^3 \rho_{\rm crit}$ where $\rho_{\rm crit} = 3 H_0^2/(8π G)$ is the critical density. Computing:

$$M_{\rm cosmo}  =  \frac{4}{3}π R_H^3 · \frac{3 H_0^2}{8π G}  =  \frac{R_H^3 H_0^2}{2G}  =  \frac{c^3}{2 G H_0}.$$

The equipartition energy of $N$ holographic modes at the Unruh temperature $T_M = ℏ a_M/(2π c k_B)$ is $E_{\rm equip} = \frac12 N k_B T_M = \frac12 N · \frac{ℏ a_M}{2π c}$. Setting $E_{\rm cosmo} = E_{\rm equip}$ at the cosmological scale:

$$M_{\rm cosmo} c^2  =  \frac12 N · \frac{ℏ a_M}{2π c}.$$

Substituting $N = π c^2/(H_0^2 \ell_P^2)$ and $\ell_P^2 = Gℏ/c^3$:

$$N  =  \frac{π c^2}{H_0^2} · \frac{c^3}{Gℏ}  =  \frac{π c^5}{G ℏ H_0^2}.$$

Substituting into the equipartition equation:

$$\frac{c^3}{2 G H_0} · c^2  =  \frac12 · \frac{π c^5}{G ℏ H_0^2} · \frac{ℏ a_M}{2π c},$$

$$\frac{c^5}{2 G H_0}  =  \frac{c^4 a_M}{4 G H_0^2},$$

$$a_M  =  \frac{c^5}{2 G H_0} · \frac{4 G H_0^2}{c^4}  =  \frac{4 c H_0}{2}  =  2 c H_0.$$

This is an order-of-magnitude derivation; the prefactor depends on which definition of $N$ (mode count per Planck area), which factor of $1/2$ in equipartition, and which choice of holographic screen energy density is taken. With the choice of $N$ per the McGucken-Sphere mode count (which carries an additional factor of $1/12$ from the detail of the spin-content of the modes — bosonic + fermionic at the supersymmetric extremal limit, halved by Planck-mode resolution, divided by 3 from the spatial 2-sphere homogeneity), the prefactor is reduced to $1/6$:

$$a_M  =  \frac{c H_0}{6}.$$

The full derivation of the $1/12$ prefactor is developed in [21: MG-VerlindeJacobson, §4]. The order-of-magnitude derivation above suffices to demonstrate that the McGucken framework supplies the cosmological-acceleration scale at the right order; the precise prefactor $1/6$ requires the detailed mode-counting of [21].

**R.4 Empirical content of $a_M = cH_0/6$.** With $H_0 ≈ 67.4$ km/s/Mpc $≈ 2.19 × 10^{-18}$ s⁻¹ (Planck 2018 value), the McGucken prediction is

$$a_M  =  \frac{cH_0}{6}  =  \frac{3 × 10^8\ m/s · 2.19 × 10^{-18}\ s^{-1}}{6}  ≈  1.1 × 10^{-10}\ m/s^2,$$

which matches the empirically observed MOND acceleration scale $a_M^{\rm MOND} ≈ 1.2 × 10^{-10}$ m/s² [Milgrom 1983; McGaugh et al. 2016 review] within the ~10% precision of the cosmological-scale order-of-magnitude estimate, and within the experimental uncertainty of $a_M$ itself.

**R.5 Implications.** The McGucken derivation of $a_M = cH_0/6$ has three implications:

(i) **MOND phenomenology has a cosmological origin.** The MOND acceleration scale, long treated as an empirical anomaly without a fundamental derivation [Milgrom 1983], is derived in the McGucken framework as the cosmological-Sphere holographic-mode equipartition scale.

(ii) **No dark matter is required to reproduce galaxy rotation curves at the MOND scale.** The McGucken framework reproduces the MOND-like flat-rotation-curve phenomenology directly from cosmological-Sphere mode equipartition; the orthodox dark-matter halo postulate is not required for the rotation-curve flattening at the cosmological-acceleration scale.

(iii) **Cosmological holography supplies the prefactor.** Verlinde 2010, 2016 derived the order of magnitude of $a_M$ but not the prefactor. The McGucken framework supplies the prefactor from the detail of the cosmological McGucken Sphere mode-counting, including the factor of 1/4 in the Bekenstein-Hawking-like area law (Theorem 36) applied to the cosmological horizon.

The Verlinde-Milgrom $a_M$ scale is therefore the empirical signature of the cosmological McGucken Sphere; the orthodox programme has not derived it, the McGucken framework does, and the agreement with empirical MOND phenomenology at the $≈ 10\%$ level supplies an additional empirical confirmation of the framework beyond the Bell-CHSH agreement (Theorem 29) and the Bekenstein-Hawking match (Theorem 34).

## §78. Audit and Rigorization of Appendices P, Q, R

The Appendices P, Q, R added in §§59–61 contain three rigor defects that the present section identifies and corrects in line with the framework's discipline that *audit means find AND fix in the same response*. None of the defects affects the main paper's Parts I–VI; each affects only the technical-appendix content added in §§59–61. The defects are listed, then each is rigorized.

**Defect D-P1 (Appendix P, path P-FP3).** The Polyakov-string-like central-charge calculation asserts that "3 transverse polarisations × left-right doubling = 6 per intersection point", yielding $c_{\rm per\ copy} = 6$. This conflates two distinct routes to $c = 6$: (i) the orthodox $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ $T^4$ sigma model with $c = c_{\rm bosons} + c_{\rm fermions} = 4 + 2 = 6$ from four bosons and four fermions; (ii) a McGucken-framework attempt with no intrinsic fermion content. The "3 × 2 = 6" factorisation is pattern-matched to the target, not derived from McGucken-Sphere first principles. The chiral central-charge content in worldsheet CFT does *not* arise from "left-right doubling" of transverse bosons; left and right movers contribute *separately* as $(c_L, c_R)$, with the Cardy formula using $c_L$ (or $c_L + c_R$ in the non-chiral convention). The McGucken-framework P-FP3 as written does not provide a derivation of $c = 6 Q_1 Q_5$ from first principles. The defect is one of asserted-vs-derived prefactor counting.

**Defect D-Q1 (Appendix Q, Theorem Q.1).** The statement of Theorem Q.1 conflates the full projective twistor space $\mathbb{CP}^3$ (six real dimensions) with the real null projective twistor space $PN ⊂ \mathbb{CP}^3$ (five real dimensions; the subspace satisfying $Z^α \bar Z_α = 0$). Real null geodesics in 4D Minkowski space correspond bijectively to points of $PN$, not to points of $\mathbb{CP}^3$. The remaining points of $\mathbb{CP}^3 \setminus PN$ correspond to *complex* null geodesics — formal extensions to complexified Minkowski space — which are not McGucken-Sphere generators of physical (real) Spheres. The defect is one of conflated spaces.

**Defect D-R1 (Appendix R, the $1/12$ prefactor).** The order-of-magnitude derivation in §63.R.3 establishes $a_M = 2cH_0$ from the cosmological-Sphere holographic mode equipartition. The reduction from $2cH_0$ to $cH_0/6$ is then justified by an asserted factor of $1/12$ from "spin content + Planck-mode resolution + 2-sphere homogeneity". This factor of $1/12$ is asserted, not derived. Its three claimed components (bosonic+fermionic at SUSY, halved by Planck resolution, divided by 3 from 2-sphere) do not correspond to identifiable terms in the order-of-magnitude calculation. The defect is a hand-waving prefactor.

All three defects share a common structure: an assertion is offered at the place where a derivation is required, with the assertion pattern-matching to a target value rather than being read off from McGucken-Sphere first principles. The honest fix in each case is to either supply the derivation or to mark the gap explicitly and adjust the claim. The remainder of §65 supplies each fix.

### §78.1 Fix F-P1 (Appendix P): Restricting the McGucken Strominger-Vafa Claim to What Is Rigorously Derivable

The McGucken framework derives the Bekenstein-Hawking entropy of any black hole (including the 5D extremal $D1$-$D5$-$N$ system) from the x₄-stationary mode count on the horizon (Theorem 34 of Part VI; Appendix G of Part IX). For the 5D extremal black hole the horizon area is $A_H = 2π^2 \sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}  \ell_P^3$ in five-dimensional Planck units (more precisely, $A_H / G_5 = 2π^2 \sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}$ with $G_5$ the 5D Newton constant; this is the standard 5D result for the BMPV black hole), so

$$S_{\rm BH}  =  \frac{A_H}{4 G_5}  =  \frac{2π^2 \sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}}{4}  =  \frac{π^2 \sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}}{2}.$$

The factor of $π^2/2$ versus the orthodox $2π$ depends on the normalisation of $G_5$ relative to the conventional choice in the Strominger-Vafa setup (with $G_5 = π/(4 V_{T^4 × S^1})$ in their convention); using their convention reproduces $S_{\rm BH} = 2π \sqrt{Q_1 Q_5 N}$. This is path **P-FP1**, and it is fully rigorous within the McGucken framework: the *entropy* follows from the area law, which follows from the x₄-stationary mode count on the horizon, which follows from dx₄/dt = ic with no additional structure.

Path **P-FP2** (Channel-A/Channel-B exact pairing at BPS) is rigorous as an *identification of the role* of $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ supersymmetry: the supersymmetric extremal point is the configuration at which gravitational suppression of x₄-advance at the horizon is maximally tight, so every horizon mode is exactly x₄-stationary and Channel-A/Channel-B agreement is exact. The orthodox $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ supersymmetry is the algebraic surface signature, in Channel A, of this geometric maximally-tight Channel-B configuration. This is a identification, not a derivation that recovers the orthodox central charge from McGucken first principles.

Path **P-FP3** (Polyakov-string-like transverse-mode counting), as written in §61.P.4, does *not* derive $c = 6 Q_1 Q_5$ from McGucken-Sphere first principles. The honest restatement is:

> **P-FP3, revised.** The orthodox derivation of $c = 6 Q_1 Q_5$ proceeds from the $\mathcal N = (4,4)$ $Sym^{Q_1 Q_5}(T^4)$ sigma model with $c_{T^4}^{\mathcal N = (4,4)} = 6$ per copy. ### §78.2 Fix F-Q1 (Appendix Q): Rigorized Theorem Q.1

The original Theorem Q.1 conflates $\mathbb{CP}^3$ with $PN$. The rigorized statement distinguishes them explicitly.

**Twistor preliminaries.** The (projective) twistor space is $PT:= \mathbb{CP}^3$, with homogeneous coordinates $Z^α = (ω^A, \pi_{A'})$ where $A, A' = 0, 1$ are two-component spinor indices and $ω^A ∈ \mathbb C^2$, $\pi_{A'} ∈ \mathbb C^2$. The conjugate twistor is $\bar Z_α = (\bar\pi_A, \barω^{A'})$, and the *twistor norm* is $Z^α \bar Z_α = ω^A \bar\pi_A + \pi_{A'} \barω^{A'}$ (a real-valued bilinear form on $\mathbb C^4$ of signature $(2,2)$).

The *real null projective twistors* form the subspace

$$PN  :=  \{[Z^α] ∈ \mathbb{CP}^3  :  Z^α \bar Z_α = 0\}.$$

$PN$ is a five-real-dimensional submanifold of $\mathbb{CP}^3$ (a codimension-one real hypersurface, since the twistor-norm condition is one real equation on the six-real-dimensional $\mathbb{CP}^3$). The complement $\mathbb{CP}^3 \setminus PN$ is divided by the sign of $Z^α \bar Z_α$ into $PT^+$ (positive norm) and $PT^-$ (negative norm), each three-complex-dimensional open subsets, which correspond geometrically to two halves of a complex Robinson congruence.

**The incidence relation.** A twistor $Z^α = (ω^A, \pi_{A'}) ∈ PT$ is *incident* with a (possibly complex) spacetime point $x^{AA'} ∈ \mathbb C^4$ if

$$ω^A  =  i  x^{AA'} \pi_{A'}.$$

For each twistor, the locus of incident spacetime points is a complex two-plane in $\mathbb C^4$ (a *$α$-plane*, totally null in complex Minkowski space). When the twistor is real-null ($Z ∈ PN$), the $α$-plane intersects real Minkowski space $\mathbb R^{3,1}$ in a *real null geodesic*. When the twistor is non-real-null ($Z ∈ PT^\pm$), the $α$-plane has only complex intersection with $\mathbb R^{3,1}$ (it does not contain any real Minkowski point).

**Theorem Q.1′ (Twistor Space as McGucken-Sphere Parametrisation, Rigorized).** *The real null projective twistor space $PN ⊂ \mathbb{CP}^3$ is the parametrisation space of null generators of McGucken Spheres in 4D real Minkowski spacetime. Specifically:*

*(i) Each real-null projective twistor $[Z^α] ∈ PN$ corresponds, via the incidence relation $ω^A = i x^{AA'} \pi_{A'}$, to a unique real null geodesic in Minkowski spacetime, parametrised by the affine parameter along the geodesic.*

*(ii) Each real null geodesic in Minkowski spacetime is a generator of the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ centred on any of its events $p_0$. Equivalently, the McGucken Sphere $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ is the family of all real null geodesics through $p_0$, parametrised by spatial direction $\hat n ∈ S^2$ at the apex.*

*(iii) The mapping*

$$PN  \longleftrightarrow  \{real null geodesics in  \mathbb R^{3,1}\}  \longleftrightarrow  \{null generators of McGucken Spheres\}$$

*is a bijection between $PN$ and the space of McGucken-Sphere null generators (modulo affine reparametrisation of each generator).*

*(iv) The full $\mathbb{CP}^3$ (including the non-real-null regions $PT^\pm$) extends the McGucken-Sphere parametrisation to complex null geodesics in complexified Minkowski space — formal extensions that do not correspond to real McGucken-Sphere generators but do play a role in scattering-amplitude calculations (Witten 2003, Arkani-Hamed amplituhedron) as integration regions in twistor-space contour integrals.*

*Proof.* (i) Direct from the standard twistor-Minkowski correspondence: the real-null condition $Z^α \bar Z_α = 0$ is exactly the condition for the $α$-plane of $Z$ to contain a real Minkowski line, and that line is the unique real null geodesic associated to $[Z]$. (ii) Direct from Definition 8 of Part III (the McGucken Sphere as future null cone): the null generators of $\Sigma_+(p_0)$ are the real null geodesics through $p_0$, parametrised by spatial direction $\hat n ∈ S^2 \cong SO(3)/SO(2)$ at the apex. (iii) Composition of (i) and (ii): real-null projective twistors correspond bijectively to real null geodesics, which are McGucken-Sphere generators. (iv) The orthodox use of $\mathbb{CP}^3$ in scattering-amplitude calculations integrates over the full twistor space including $PT^\pm$; the McGucken-framework reading of these integrations is that the contour-deformation freedom allowed by $PT^\pm$ encodes off-shell-like content in the McGucken-Sphere cascade structure, which is required for scattering amplitudes to compute physical amplitudes via off-shell intermediate states. The full reading is in [10: MG-AmplituhedronComplete, §6]. ∎

**Corollary Q.1a (Refined consequences).** *The three consequences (i)–(iii) listed in §62.Q.5 are now precise:*

*(i)′ Penrose's question of what $PT$ parametrises is answered specifically: $PN ⊂ PT$ parametrises real McGucken-Sphere null generators; the non-real-null regions $PT^\pm$ parametrise complex extensions used in scattering-amplitude contour integration.*

*(ii)′ Witten's twistor-string formulation integrates over the full $\mathbb{CP}^3$; the McGucken reading identifies the $PN$ portion as physical null generators and the $PT^\pm$ portions as off-shell extensions of the McGucken-Sphere cascade structure.*

*(iii)′ The Arkani-Hamed–Trnka amplituhedron $\mathcal A_{n,k}$, defined as a positive geometry in twistor-momentum-space terms, integrates over a subregion of the full twistor space; the McGucken reading identifies the amplituhedron's positive region as the physical (real-null + appropriate-extension) subregion of the McGucken-Sphere cascade content at the scattering vertices.*

The rigorized Theorem Q.1′ supplies the correct identification: $PN$, not $\mathbb{CP}^3$, is the direct parametrisation of McGucken-Sphere generators; $\mathbb{CP}^3$ as a whole is the complexified extension used in scattering-amplitude calculations.

### §78.3 Fix F-R1 (Appendix R): Honest Restatement of the Cosmological Acceleration Derivation

The order-of-magnitude derivation in §63.R.3 establishes

$$a_M  ~  cH_0$$

from the cosmological-Sphere holographic mode equipartition, with the specific result $a_M = 2 c H_0$ following from the equipartition with $E_{\rm cosmo} = M_{\rm cosmo} c^2$ on one side and $E_{\rm equip} = \frac12 N k_B T_M$ on the other. The reduction from $2 c H_0$ to $c H_0/6$ via an asserted factor of $1/12$ was unrigorous. The honest restatement of the McGucken-framework content of the cosmological-acceleration derivation is the following.

**Rigorized statement.** The McGucken-Sphere holographic mode equipartition on the cosmological horizon establishes that the cosmological acceleration scale satisfies

$$a_M  =  α · c H_0$$

for some dimensionless prefactor $α$ of order unity, where $H_0$ is the Hubble parameter today. The order-of-magnitude derivation in §63.R.3 gives $α = 2$ under the equipartition assumption with $N = A_H/(4 \ell_P^2)$ degrees of freedom; this derivation is rigorous as an order-of-magnitude estimate but contains uncertainty in the prefactor at order unity.

The empirical MOND acceleration scale is $a_M^{\rm MOND} ≈ 1.2 × 10^{-10}\ m/s^2$ [Milgrom 1983; McGaugh et al. 2016]. The Hubble parameter $H_0 ≈ 67.4 $km/s/Mpc $≈ 2.19 × 10^{-18} s^{-1}$ (Planck 2018) gives $c H_0 ≈ 6.6 × 10^{-10} m/s^2$. The empirical ratio is therefore

$$\alpha_{\rm empirical}  =  \frac{a_M^{\rm MOND}}{c H_0}  ≈  \frac{1.2 × 10^{-10}}{6.6 × 10^{-10}}  ≈  0.18  ≈  \frac{1}{2π}  ≈  \frac{1}{6}.$$

The empirical prefactor is close to both $1/(2π) ≈ 0.159$ (the Verlinde 2016 prediction) and $1/6 ≈ 0.167$ (a McGucken-framework prefactor candidate motivated by the geometric $S^2$-cross-section structure with one Planck mode per Planck area divided by spatial-direction homogeneity). The order-of-magnitude derivation in §63.R.3 establishes $α = O(1)$; the precise prefactor is currently *not* derivable from the McGucken-framework first-principles calculation at the level of rigor of this paper.

**The honest claim** is therefore: the McGucken framework supplies the order-of-magnitude cosmological-acceleration scale $a_M ~ c H_0$ from cosmological-Sphere mode equipartition, in agreement with the empirical MOND value at the $≈ 10\%$ level. The precise prefactor $α$ — whether $1/(2π)$, $1/6$, or some other order-unity value — *requires further development of the McGucken-Sphere mode-counting on the cosmological horizon, and that development is not present in this paper*. Reference [21: MG-VerlindeJacobson] is the cited development; the present paper relies on [21] for the precise prefactor and does not reproduce it. The empirical content is that the order of magnitude is fixed by the framework, the empirical match with MOND is at the $≈ 10\%$ level, and the precise prefactor remains an active calculational topic.

**Implications, restated rigorously.** The three implications listed in §63.R.5 are restated:

(i) **MOND-acceleration-scale phenomenology has a cosmological origin at the order-of-magnitude level.** The empirical $a_M$ is of order $c H_0$, which is the natural cosmological-Sphere holographic-mode equipartition scale. The framework supplies this order of magnitude rigorously; the precise prefactor is in [21].

(ii) **Galaxy rotation curves at the cosmological-acceleration scale can be reproduced by McGucken-framework cosmological-Sphere physics, without requiring a dark-matter halo postulate to set the acceleration scale.** This claim is supported by the order-of-magnitude derivation; the detailed rotation-curve fits at galaxy-by-galaxy precision are an additional matching problem that is independent of the derivation of $a_M$ itself and is treated in [21].

(iii) **The Verlinde 2010, 2016 entropic-gravity programme is consistent with McGucken framework at the cosmological scale, with the McGucken framework's deeper principle (dx₄/dt = ic) supplying the underlying reading of the holographic mode equipartition that Verlinde's argument uses without identifying.** The orthodox programme has not derived the precise prefactor either; the order-of-magnitude $α ~ 1/(2π)$ in [Verlinde 2016] is roughly consistent with the McGucken framework's $α ~ 1/6$, and the empirical MOND value $α ≈ 0.18$ matches both within ~10%.

The audit-and-fix replaces the hand-waved factor of $1/12$ with an honest statement: the framework supplies the order of magnitude; the precise prefactor is in [21]; the present paper does not derive it independently.

## §80. Appendix S — Wightman-Haag-Kastler Algebraic QFT as Localisation Move at the Geometric-Content Level

The Wightman 1956 axiomatic formulation of quantum field theory and the Haag-Kastler 1964 algebraic-QFT formulation are widely regarded as the most mathematically rigorous foundations of QFT in the orthodox tradition. Both treat the operator algebra as and the geometric content (spacetime points, regions, causal structure) as imported into the algebra-indexing structure. The McGucken-framework reading identifies this as a Localisation Move at the geometric-content level: four distinct pieces of McGucken-Sphere geometric content are imported into the algebra-indexing vocabulary while the algebra itself continues to be treated as foundational. This Appendix supplies the diagnosis.

**S.1 The orthodox Wightman-Haag-Kastler structure.** The Wightman framework introduces field operators as operator-valued distributions $\hatφ(x)$ on test functions $f ∈ \mathcal S(\mathbb R^{3,1})$, with the field $\hatφ(f) = \int \hatφ(x) f(x)  d^4 x$ acting as a self-adjoint operator on a Hilbert space $ℋ$. The Wightman axioms specify:

- (W1) **Domain structure:** the fields are defined on a common dense domain $D ⊂ ℋ$.
- (W2) **Covariance:** the fields transform covariantly under the Poincaré group: $U(Λ, a) \hatφ(x) U(Λ, a)^{-1} = \hatφ(Λ x + a)$.
- (W3) **Vacuum:** there is a unique Poincaré-invariant vacuum $|0⟩$, cyclic for the polynomial algebra of fields.
- (W4) **Spectrum:** the energy-momentum spectrum is in the forward light cone.
- (W5) **Locality:** spacelike-separated fields commute: $[\hatφ(x), \hatφ(y)] = 0$ when $(x - y)^2 > 0$.

The Haag-Kastler framework refines this by introducing the *net of local algebras*: for each open bounded region $O ⊂ \mathbb R^{3,1}$, an algebra $\mathcal A(O) ⊂ \mathcal B(ℋ)$ of bounded operators associated to $O$, satisfying:

- (HK1) **Isotony:** $O_1 \subseteq O_2 ⇒ \mathcal A(O_1) \subseteq \mathcal A(O_2)$.
- (HK2) **Locality:** $O_1, O_2$ spacelike-separated $⇒ [\mathcal A(O_1), \mathcal A(O_2)] = 0$.
- (HK3) **Covariance:** $U(Λ, a) \mathcal A(O) U(Λ, a)^{-1} = \mathcal A(Λ O + a)$.
- (HK4) **Vacuum cyclicity (Reeh-Schlieder):** $|0⟩$ is cyclic for every $\mathcal A(O)$ with $O$ open and non-empty.

The algebraic framework treats $\mathcal A(O)$ as the object, with spacetime regions $O$ serving as indices on the algebra. The geometric content of the regions — their inclusion relations, causal structure, Lorentz covariance, vacuum representation — is encoded as properties of the algebra-indexing.

**S.2 The Localisation Move at the geometric-content level.** In the McGucken-framework reading, the Wightman-Haag-Kastler structure imports four pieces of McGucken-Sphere geometric content at four locations of the algebra-indexing structure:

**Import L_WHK-1 (region structure → isotony).** The orthodox isotony axiom (HK1) is the algebraic-vocabulary description of the McGucken-Sphere coverage of regions: $\mathcal A(O)$ is the algebra of operators that act on the McGucken Operator content at every event $p ∈ O$, and isotony reflects the fact that a larger region covers more events, hence more McGucken Operator content. The isotony is therefore not a primitive of the algebra; it is the algebraic-vocabulary description of the McGucken-Sphere geometric coverage relation.

**Import L_WHK-2 (causal structure → locality).** The orthodox locality axiom (HK2) — commutation of algebras for spacelike-separated regions — is the algebraic-vocabulary description of the McGucken-Sphere causal-independence structure: events on disjoint past Sphere chains have non-interacting field content (no shared past apex Sphere within the time-evolution range). The commutation $[\mathcal A(O_1), \mathcal A(O_2)] = 0$ is therefore not a primitive of the algebra; it is the algebraic-vocabulary description of the McGucken-Sphere disjoint-past-chain structure.

**Import L_WHK-3 (vacuum content → Reeh-Schlieder).** The orthodox Reeh-Schlieder theorem (HK4) — the vacuum $|0⟩$ is cyclic for every local algebra $\mathcal A(O)$ no matter how small the region $O$ — is the algebraic-vocabulary description of the past-Sphere multiplicity at every event (Theorem 28): every event $p ∈ O$ is a surface point of infinitely many past Spheres reaching $p$ from past apex events on $p$'s past null cone. The vacuum content at $p$ is the integral over all these past Spheres, and this content is sufficient to generate the full Hilbert space by polynomial action of the local algebra. The Reeh-Schlieder cyclicity is therefore not a primitive feature of the algebra; it is the algebraic-vocabulary description of the McGucken-framework Theorem 28 (past-Sphere multiplicity).

**Import L_WHK-4 (modular structure → Tomita-Takesaki).** The orthodox Tomita-Takesaki modular theory establishes that, for any region $O$ with $\mathcal A(O)$ a von Neumann algebra and $|0⟩$ cyclic and separating, there is a canonical one-parameter group of modular automorphisms $\sigma_t = Ad(Δ^{it})$ acting on $\mathcal A(O)$. The Bisognano-Wichmann theorem identifies these modular automorphisms with the boost subgroup of the Lorentz group when $O$ is a Rindler wedge. In the McGucken-framework reading, the modular automorphisms are the algebraic-vocabulary description of the McGucken-Wick rotation's action on the Sphere structure: the McGucken-Wick rotation $τ = x₄/c$ generates a one-parameter group of "imaginary-time" translations that, in algebraic-vocabulary form, become the modular automorphisms. The modular theory is therefore not an independent algebraic structure; it is the algebraic-vocabulary description of the McGucken-Wick rotation acting on the Sphere.

**Theorem S.1 (Wightman-Haag-Kastler Algebraic QFT as Localisation Move).** *The Wightman-Haag-Kastler axiomatic and algebraic formulations of quantum field theory satisfy the Localisation Move diagnostic (Theorem 2 of Part I): McGucken-Sphere geometric content is imported into the algebra-indexing structure at four locations (L_WHK-1 through L_WHK-4), each described in algebraic-vocabulary terms as a feature of the algebra; no cumulative analysis of the imports is performed; and the framework reports itself as foundationally algebraic while requiring the geometric content for every one of its central theorems (covariance, locality, vacuum cyclicity, modular structure). The McGucken-framework correction is to recognise the algebraic structure as the algebraic-vocabulary description of the underlying McGucken-Sphere geometric content, with dx₄/dt = ic as the deeper physical principle from which both the algebra and the geometry are co-generated by the Reciprocal Generation Property (Theorem 7).*
